**Authorization**: Requires the org:manage permission. Return 403 Forbidden if the authenticated member lacks this permission.

**Soft-delete awareness**: Check the department's deleted_at column before proceeding. If deleted_at is not null, the department has been soft-deleted. Return 404 Not Found with a message indicating the department no longer exists. Do not allow updates to soft-deleted records.

**Request body fields** (all optional — only provided fields are updated):
- `name`: If provided, must be a non-empty string. Enforce the composite unique constraint [erp_hrm_organization_id, name] — query for any other department (different id) in the same organization with the same name and a null deleted_at. Return 409 Conflict if a name collision exists.
- `description`: If provided, can be any string value. To clear the description, pass an empty string or null. If omitted entirely, the existing description is preserved.
- `parent_id`: If provided, manages the parent-child relationship:
  - If null, the department becomes a top-level department (no parent).
  - If set to a UUID, validate the target parent: (a) exists in the same organization with deleted_at null, (b) has a null parent_id itself (must be top-level to enforce one-level nesting), (c) is not the department being updated (no self-referencing), (d) is not a descendant of the department being updated — traverse the hierarchy upward from the target parent to check it does not reach this department.
  - Return 400 Bad Request with a descriptive message for any violated parent constraint.
- `erp_hrm_organization_id`: MUST NOT be accepted from the request body. The organization context is determined from the authenticated session.
- System fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at): MUST NOT be accepted from the request body.

**Update execution**:
- Apply only the fields present in the request body to the department record.
- The updated_at timestamp is set to the current time automatically.
- Return the full department record after the update.

**Activity Log**: Record an activity log entry with action type reflecting the update. Include the department ID and which specific fields were changed (old values vs new values) for audit trail purposes.

responseBody.description: The complete department record reflecting all applied updates, including the automatically refreshed updated_at timestamp and all existing relationships.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the department to update (UUID v4 format).
parameters.name: departmentId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the department. All properties are optional — only the fields provided are modified, enabling partial updates. The name, if changed, must be unique within the organization among non-deleted departments. The parent_id, if changed, must reference an existing top-level department in the same organization and must not create a circular relationship.

prerequisites.description: The department must be created before it can be updated. The department identified by departmentId must exist as an active (non-deleted) record in the organization. Additionally, if the update request includes a parent_id, that parent department must also have been created via this same operation and must be a top-level department (no parent of its own) in the same organization.

operations.description:
Deletes a department within the organization.

When a department is deleted, all employees who were assigned to that department have their department association cleared — they remain active members of the organization and their records, timelogs, timesheets, contracts, and project assignments are fully preserved.

A department that serves as a parent to other departments cannot be deleted. All child departments must be reassigned to a different parent or deleted first. This prevents orphaned departments in the hierarchy.

The deletion is a soft delete: the department record is preserved with a deletion timestamp for data retention purposes, but the department is no longer visible in listings or available for new assignments.

This operation generates an activity log entry recording the deletion event, including the department name and the number of affected employees.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete a department by setting its deleted_at timestamp to the current time.

**Permission**: Require the org:manage permission. Reject with 403 Forbidden if the calling user lacks this permission.

**Pre-deletion checks**:
1. Query the department by departmentId scoped to the current organization (erp_hrm_organization_id). Return 404 if not found or already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).
2. Check for child departments: query erp_hrm_departments WHERE parent_id = departmentId AND deleted_at IS NULL AND erp_hrm_organization_id = currentOrgId. If any exist, return 409 Conflict with a message indicating that child departments must be reassigned or deleted first.

**Employee clearing**:
After passing the child check, update all employees (erp_hrm_employees) whose department reference points to this department: SET department_id = NULL WHERE department_id = departmentId AND erp_hrm_organization_id = currentOrgId. Count the affected employees for the activity log.

**Soft delete**:
Set deleted_at = NOW() and updated_at = NOW() on the department record.

**Activity log**:
Insert an entry into erp_hrm_activity_logs with action type 'department.deleted', including the department name and the count of affected employees whose department association was cleared.

**Transaction**: Wrap all operations (child check, employee clearing, soft delete, activity log insertion) in a single database transaction to ensure atomicity.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the department to delete (scoped to the current organization).
parameters.name: departmentId

prerequisites.description: Department must exist before it can be deleted. This POST operation creates the department resource within the current organization, providing the departmentId required by the DELETE operation.

operations.description:
List and search employment contracts across the organization with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

Contracts define compensation terms for employees, including pay rate, pay period, and working hours commitment. Each employee may have multiple contracts over their tenure, forming a complete historical record. Only one contract per employee is active at any given moment — the active contract is determined dynamically as the one with the most recent start date whose end date is either absent (ongoing) or not yet passed.

This endpoint supports both individual contract history viewing and organization-wide browsing by managers. Results can be filtered by employee, date ranges, pay period, and active status. Past contracts (superseded or expired) are preserved as immutable historical records and remain visible through this endpoint. Soft-deleted contracts — those removed in error before being superseded — are excluded from results.

Sorting defaults to most recent contracts first (by start date) and can be customized. Pagination is supported for efficient browsing of large contract sets.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_contracts table with pagination and filtering. Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) — only contracts that were superseded or expired, not deleted in error, remain visible.

Apply organization-scoping through the employee relationship: join erp_hrm_employees to filter by erp_hrm_employee.erp_hrm_organization_id matching the current session's organization context.

Support the following filters in the request body:
- employeeId: filter to a specific employee's contracts
- startDateFrom/startDateTo: filter by contract start date range
- endDateFrom/endDateTo: filter by contract end date range
- payPeriod: filter by one or more pay period values (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly)
- isActive: when true, return only the currently active contract (end_date is null or in the future, with the most recent start_date). When false, return only historical/ended contracts.
- search: free-text search across notes

Default sorting: by start_date descending (most recent first). Allow configurable sort by start_date, end_date, pay_rate, working_hours_per_week.

Calculate active status dynamically at query time: a contract is active when it has no end_date (ongoing) or end_date is in the future, AND it has the most recent start_date among all non-ended contracts for its employee. This determination is made at query time rather than stored as a column.

Return cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of contract summary records, each showing the employee reference, date range, pay rate, pay period, working hours, and dynamically computed active status. Ordered by start date descending by default.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering and paginating contracts. Supports filtering by employee, contract date ranges, pay period, active status, and free-text search across notes. Includes pagination parameters for offset or cursor-based traversal.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of employment contracts for a specific employee.

Each employee can have multiple contracts over their tenure, forming a complete historical record of compensation arrangements — pay rate, pay period, and working hours commitment. Only one contract is active at any given time; past contracts are preserved as immutable historical records for auditing and reference purposes.

**Filtering and Search**

Contracts can be filtered by start date range, end date range, pay period (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly), and contract status (active vs. past). The active contract is determined at query time as the one with the most recent start date on or before the current date whose end date is either absent or not yet passed.

**Access Control**

Users with the `employee:view` permission can view any employee's contracts within the organization. Employees without this permission can only view their own contracts. Contract creation and editing require the separate `employee:manage` permission and are handled by dedicated endpoints.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the `erp_hrm_contracts` table filtered by the specified employee, with pagination and optional search filters.

**Prerequisites**:
- Verify the employee exists within the current organization context by looking up `erp_hrm_employees` where `id = {employeeId}` AND `erp_hrm_organization_id = current_organization_id` AND `deleted_at IS NULL`. If not found, reject with a 404 not-found error.
- Enforce permission: users with `employee:view` permission can view any employee's contracts; employees without `employee:view` can only view their own contracts (where `erp_hrm_member_id = current_user_member_id`). Reject with 403 if unauthorized.

**Query Execution**:
- Base filter: `erp_hrm_employee_id = {employeeId}` AND `deleted_at IS NULL`.
- Apply optional filters from the request body:
  - `start_date_from` / `start_date_to`: filter by contract start date range.
  - `end_date_from` / `end_date_to`: filter by contract end date range.
  - `pay_period`: filter by pay period value (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly).
  - `status`: filter by contract status — `active` returns the current active contract (most recent start_date ≤ now and end_date IS NULL or end_date ≥ now), `past` returns superseded or expired contracts, absent returns all.
- Apply cursor-based or offset pagination from the request body.
- Order results by `start_date DESC` so the most recent contract appears first.

**Response Construction**:
- Return paginated summary records. Each summary includes: `id`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `pay_rate`, `pay_period`, `working_hours_per_week`, `created_at`.
- Include pagination metadata (total count, next cursor).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of contract summary records for the specified employee, ordered by start date descending so the most recent contract appears first.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the employee whose contracts are being retrieved (scoped to the current organization).
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria including date ranges, pay period filter, contract status (active/past), and pagination parameters.

prerequisites.description: The employee must exist within the current organization before their contracts can be listed. The endpoint verifies employee existence and rejects with 404 if not found.

operations.description:
Retrieves the full details of a specific employee contract identified by its unique identifier.

Each employee in the organization may have multiple contracts over their tenure, forming a historical record of all compensation arrangements. This endpoint returns the complete information for a single contract, including its effective dates, pay rate, pay period, working hours commitment, and any additional notes.

Employees can view their own contracts. Users holding the employee:view permission can view contracts belonging to any employee within the organization. The contract must belong to an employee in the currently selected organization context — cross-organization access is not permitted.

A contract may be active (currently in effect), future (not yet started), or historical (superseded or expired). Active contracts are editable by users with employee:manage permission, while historical contracts are immutable records preserved for auditing and compliance purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_contracts table by primary key id matching the contractId path parameter. Exclude soft-deleted records where deleted_at is not null.

Verify organization context: join through erp_hrm_employees to ensure the contract's employee belongs to the currently selected organization (erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_organization_id matches current context). If the contract exists but its employee is in a different organization, return a not-found error rather than exposing cross-organization data.

Authorization: employees may view their own contracts. Users with the employee:view permission may view any employee's contracts within the organization. If neither condition is met, return an access-denied error.

Return all contract fields: id, start_date, end_date, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes, created_at, and updated_at. Include the erp_hrm_employee_id to identify the owning employee.

responseBody.description: Full contract details including compensation terms, effective dates, and metadata.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the contract to retrieve.
parameters.name: contractId

prerequisites.description: An employee must exist within the organization before a contract can be created for them, since every contract belongs to exactly one employee via the erp_hrm_employee_id foreign key.
The contract identified by contractId must be created before it can be retrieved. This POST creates the contract record that the GET operation looks up by primary key.

operations.description:
Create a new employment contract for a specific employee.

This endpoint adds a new contract to the employee's compensation history with a specified pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, and effective date range. When a new contract is created, the system automatically closes the employee's previous active contract by setting its end date to the day before the new contract's start date. This ensures only one contract is active at any given time while preserving all past contracts as immutable historical records.

Contracts serve as the authoritative record of an employee's compensation terms throughout their tenure. Each contract captures the pay rate, pay period (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly), expected working hours per week, and optional notes for additional context such as bonus structures or special terms. The contract history provides a complete auditable trail for compliance, reporting, and reference purposes.

Access to this endpoint requires the `employee:manage` permission. Users without this permission will receive an access denied response. The employee must belong to the current organization context — contracts cannot be created for employees outside the organization.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new employment contract for the employee identified by {employeeId}.

**Authorization**: Requires `employee:manage` permission within the current organization context.

**Pre-validation**:
1. Verify the employee exists in the current organization. If not found, reject with 404 not-found.
2. Validate that `pay_rate` > 0. If zero or negative, reject with 422 validation error.
3. Validate that `working_hours_per_week` > 0. If zero or negative, reject with 422 validation error.
4. If `end_date` is provided, validate that `start_date` < `end_date`. If start_date is after or equal to end_date, reject with 422 validation error.
5. Validate that `pay_period` is one of: `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`. If not, reject with 422 validation error.

**Auto-closure of previous active contract**:
Query for the employee's current active contract (the contract with the most recent start_date on or before the current date whose end_date is either null or not yet passed). If an active contract exists, set its `end_date` to the day before the new contract's `start_date` and update its `updated_at` timestamp. This ensures only one contract is active at any time for the employee.

**Creation**:
Insert a new row into `erp_hrm_contracts` with:
- `id`: auto-generated UUID
- `erp_hrm_employee_id`: from the {employeeId} path parameter
- `start_date`, `end_date`, `pay_rate`, `pay_period`, `working_hours_per_week`, `notes`: from the request body
- `created_at`, `updated_at`: set to current timestamp
- `deleted_at`: null

**Response**: Return the newly created contract record with all fields including the server-generated id and timestamps.

**Activity Log**: Record a contract creation event in the activity log with the employee and contract identifiers.

responseBody.description: The newly created contract record with all fields populated, including the server-assigned unique identifier and creation timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the employee for whom the contract is being created. Must belong to the current organization context.
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: The contract details including start date, pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, and optional end date and notes. The employee reference is derived from the path parameter and must not be included in the request body.

prerequisites.description: The employee identified by {employeeId} must exist in the current organization before a contract can be created. The database enforces this through a foreign key constraint (erp_hrm_contracts.erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees.id), and the operation specification requires pre-validation of employee existence, returning 404 if not found.

operations.description:
Update an existing employee contract's compensation terms.

This endpoint allows users with employee management permission to modify the terms of the currently active contract for an employee. Only the active contract — the one currently in effect — can be edited. Past contracts that have been superseded or whose end date has passed are preserved as immutable historical records and cannot be modified.

The update allows changing the pay rate, pay period classification (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly), expected working hours per week, contract effective date range, and any free-form notes. All validation rules for contract fields are enforced on update, ensuring data integrity.

Upon successful update, the contract's modification timestamp is refreshed and the change is recorded in the organization's activity log. A real-time event is emitted to notify interested clients of the contract change.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update an existing employee contract identified by its UUID.

**Authorization**: Requires `employee:manage` permission within the current organization context. Reject with 403 if the user lacks this permission.

**Organization Scoping**: Verify the contract's associated employee belongs to the currently selected organization. If the contract exists but its employee does not belong to the current organization, reject with 404 (not found within organization context).

**Active Contract Only**: Only the current active contract may be edited. Determine the active contract as the one with the most recent start_date on or before the current date whose end_date is either null (ongoing) or not yet passed. If the target contract is a past contract (superseded by a newer contract or with an end_date in the past), reject with 422 and a message indicating that past contracts are immutable historical records. Do NOT emit a contract-edited event for past contracts.

**Updateable Fields**: Accept and apply changes to pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes, start_date, and end_date. System-managed fields (id, erp_hrm_employee_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) must not be accepted in the request body.

**Validation**:
- pay_rate must be greater than zero
- pay_period must be one of: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly
- working_hours_per_week must be greater than zero
- If end_date is provided, start_date must be before end_date
- If start_date is changed and there is a newer contract, ensure no overlap occurs

**On Success**: Update the contract record, set updated_at to the current timestamp, record the edit in the activity log, emit a contract-edited real-time event, and return the updated contract.

responseBody.description: The updated contract with all fields including the refreshed updated_at timestamp.

parameters.description: UUID of the contract to update. The contract must belong to an employee within the currently selected organization and must be the active (current) contract — past contracts are immutable.
parameters.name: contractId

requestBody.description: Updated contract fields. Only the active contract may be edited. System-managed fields (id, employee reference, timestamps) are not accepted.

prerequisites.description: The contract must exist before it can be updated. This operation creates a new employment contract for an employee, providing the contract record that the update operation will modify.

operations.description:
Soft-deletes a contract record that was created in error.

This operation is reserved exclusively for active contracts that were entered by mistake and have not yet been superseded by a newer contract. Only the current active contract for an employee may be deleted — contracts that have been superseded by a newer agreement or whose end date has passed are preserved as immutable historical records for auditing and compliance purposes.

A soft-deleted contract is permanently marked with a deletion timestamp in the database while the record itself is retained for audit integrity. This action is not reversible through the API.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete an active contract that was created in error.

1. Look up the contract by {contractId} UUID. Return 404 Not Found if the contract does not exist or if it has already been soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

2. Enforce organization-level data isolation: verify that the contract's associated employee (via erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_organization_id) belongs to the currently authenticated user's active organization context. Return 404 Not Found if the organization does not match — never reveal the existence of contracts in other organizations.

3. Reject deletion if the contract is not the current active contract for its employee:
   - Query for any contract belonging to the same employee (same erp_hrm_employee_id) with a start_date later than this contract's start_date AND deleted_at IS NULL. If such a contract exists, this contract has been superseded by a newer agreement and is an immutable historical record — return 409 Conflict with a clear message indicating the contract has been superseded.
   - If the contract's end_date is not null and is before the current date, the contract has expired and is a historical record — return 409 Conflict with a message indicating the contract has expired and cannot be deleted.

4. Perform soft deletion: UPDATE the contract record, setting deleted_at to the current timestamp and updated_at to the current timestamp.

5. Return 204 No Content on successful soft deletion.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the contract to soft-delete. Must reference an active, non-superseded, non-expired contract that was created in error and has not already been soft-deleted.
parameters.name: contractId

prerequisites.description: Employee must exist before a contract can be created for them, since contracts are scoped to employees via erp_hrm_employee_id.
Contract must be created before it can be soft-deleted, as the delete operation looks up the contract by its UUID and requires it to exist.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of projects within the current organization.

This endpoint provides the primary browsing interface for projects. Users with project view permission can search projects by name, filter by lifecycle status, and navigate through results with pagination.

Each project in the list displays its name, color code (for UI visual identification), current status (active, archived, or completed), and description. The response is optimized for list display with summary fields — use the detail endpoint to retrieve full project information including budget hours, dates, and membership data.

Results are scoped to the user's currently selected organization. Soft-deleted projects are excluded from the list. Projects of all statuses are returned unless filtered by the status parameter.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_projects table scoped to the current organization context (organization_id = session organization).

Apply the following filters from the request body:
- status: Filter by project status (exact match on 'active', 'archived', or 'completed'). If omitted, return projects of all statuses.
- search: Text search on the name column using the gin_trgm_ops trigram index for fuzzy matching. Supports partial name matching.

Exclude soft-deleted projects: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.

Pagination:
- Support cursor-based or offset-based pagination as specified in the IRequest type.
- Default ordering: by created_at descending (newest first). Optionally allow ordering by name.

Return a paginated response containing project summaries with fields: id, name, color_code, status, and description.

Authorization: Requires project:view permission or equivalent project-related permission. Without permission, return 403 Forbidden.

Multi-tenancy: All queries must include organization_id filter from the session's selected organization context.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project summary records optimized for list display. Each entry includes id, name, color code, status, and description.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria including optional status filter, text search on project name, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific project within the current organization.

Returns the project's full profile including its display name, description, color code for UI rendering, current lifecycle status (active, archived, or completed), optional budget hours for planned-vs-actual comparisons, and optional start and end dates for timeline tracking.

The operation is organization-scoped — only projects belonging to the user's active organization are accessible. Users must have project view permission or be a member of the requested project. Soft-deleted projects are excluded from retrieval.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_projects table by id = {projectId} with the current session's organization_id scope.

Filter: WHERE id = {projectId} AND organization_id = current_organization_id AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return 404 if no matching project found.

Return all project columns: id, organization_id, name, description, color_code, status, budget_hours, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at.

Authorization: Require project:view permission or the requesting employee must be a project member of this project. Otherwise return 403.

Response includes the full project entity for detail views, edit forms, and project management screens.

responseBody.description: Full project entity with all descriptive fields and metadata for detail views, edit forms, and project management screens.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the project to retrieve (UUID format). Scoped to the current organization.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Creates a new project within the currently selected organization. The project becomes available immediately for time tracking and task management.

A project requires a display name and a color code for visual identification in the user interface. The name appears in project lists, timelog entry forms, timesheet summaries, and reports. The color code should be a hex color value such as `#FF5733`.

Optional fields provide additional context: a description explaining the project's purpose or scope, budget hours for comparing planned effort against actual logged time in budget reports, and start and end dates to define the project timeline.

The project is automatically created in active status, meaning it accepts new timelogs from the moment it is created. Archived and completed statuses can be set later through the update operation.

Only users holding the project management permission within the organization can create projects.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new row into erp_hrm_projects with the following rules:

**Authorization**: Only users with `project:manage` permission can create projects. Extract the organization_id from the authenticated session's currently selected organization context.

**Required Fields**:
- `name` (string): Must not be empty. Project display name used in lists, forms, summaries, and reports.
- `color_code` (string): Must not be empty. Hex color value (e.g., `#FF5733`) for visual distinction in the UI. Validate format is a valid hex color.

**Optional Fields**:
- `description` (string | null): Additional context about the project's purpose or scope.
- `budget_hours` (number | null): Total estimated hours. Must be a positive number (> 0) when provided. Projects without a budget are excluded from budget utilization reports.
- `start_date` (datetime | null): Project timeline start.
- `end_date` (datetime | null): Project timeline end. When both start_date and end_date are provided, end_date must not be earlier than start_date.

**Auto-Set Fields**:
- `id`: Server-generated UUID.
- `organization_id`: From session context.
- `status`: Always `"active"` for new projects.
- `created_at`: Current timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Current timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: null.

**Edge Cases**:
- Return 400 if name is empty or missing.
- Return 400 if color_code is empty, missing, or not a valid hex color.
- Return 400 if budget_hours is provided but is zero or negative.
- Return 400 if both start_date and end_date are provided and end_date < start_date.
- Return 403 if the user lacks project:manage permission.

**Post-Creation**: Emit a project creation real-time event so subscribed clients are notified of the new project.

operations.description:
Updates the details of an existing project within the current organization.

This operation allows users with the project management permission to modify a project's display name, description, color code, budget hours, and timeline dates. All fields are optional — the client may send only the fields that need to change, and omitted fields will retain their current values.

The project's lifecycle status (active, archived, or completed) is not modified through this operation. Status transitions are handled through dedicated endpoints for archiving, completing, and reopening projects.

Validation is applied to ensure data integrity: budget hours must be a positive number when provided, and the end date must not precede the start date. The operation is scoped to the current organization context — projects belonging to other organizations cannot be accessed or modified.

Update an existing project's editable fields.

Require the caller to hold the project:manage permission. Return a 403 if the permission is absent.

Accept the following updatable fields from the request body (all are optional — only provided fields are updated; omitted fields retain their current values):
- name (string, required if provided — cannot be set to empty)
- description (string, nullable — can be set to null to clear)
- color_code (string, required if provided — cannot be empty)
- budget_hours (number, nullable — must be positive when set; can be set to null to clear)
- start_date (datetime, nullable — can be set to null to clear)
- end_date (datetime, nullable — can be set to null to clear)

Validation rules:
- When budget_hours is provided and not null, it must be a positive number greater than 0.
- When both start_date and end_date are provided (neither is null), end_date must not be earlier than start_date. Validate this against both the incoming values and the existing database values when only one date is being updated.

The status field is NOT updated through this operation. Status transitions (active ↔ archived ↔ completed) are managed through dedicated status-change operations.

The organization_id, id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields are system-managed and MUST NOT be accepted from the request body.

Update the updated_at timestamp to the current time upon any successful modification.

Return the full updated project record as the response.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a project and all its associated child data.

Before deletion proceeds, the system verifies that no timelogs are associated with the project — if any exist, the request is rejected with a conflict error regardless of the timelogs' timesheet status. When the precondition is met, all project memberships, tasks, and task history entries are permanently and irreversibly removed from the database. The project record itself is preserved with a deletion timestamp for referential integrity.

Requires `project:manage` permission within the user's currently selected organization. The operation is scoped to the user's active organization context — only projects belonging to that organization can be deleted. Upon successful deletion, a real-time event is dispatched to all project members confirming the permanent removal.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a project by its unique identifier using soft-delete for the project and permanent removal for all child data.

Authorization:
- Require `project:manage` permission within the current organization context.
- Reject with 403 Forbidden if the calling user lacks this permission.

Precondition — No Timelogs:
- Query the `erp_hrm_timelogs` table scoped to the target project's organization to check for any timelog rows where `project_id` equals the target project ID.
- If ANY timelogs exist (regardless of their timesheet status — draft, submitted, or approved), reject the request with a 409 Conflict error indicating that all timelogs must be removed before the project can be deleted.

Organization Scoping:
- Look up the project by `id` AND `organization_id` matching the user's active organization context.
- Return 404 Not Found if no matching project exists or if the project's `deleted_at` is already set (project was already soft-deleted).

Cascading Permanent Removal:
- Execute within a single database transaction.
- Permanently DELETE all rows from `erp_hrm_project_members` where `project_id` equals the target project ID.
- Permanently DELETE all rows from `erp_hrm_task_histories` whose `task_id` belongs to any task of the target project (join through `erp_hrm_tasks`).
- Permanently DELETE all rows from `erp_hrm_tasks` where `project_id` equals the target project ID.
- Soft-delete the project itself: SET `deleted_at = NOW()` and `updated_at = NOW()` on the `erp_hrm_projects` row. Do NOT hard-delete the project record — the `deleted_at` column preserves referential integrity for historical references.

Real-time Event:
- After successful deletion, emit a `project.deleted` real-time event.
- Event payload: `{ projectId: string, organizationId: string }`.
- Target subscribers: all project members (query `erp_hrm_project_members` before the cascading deletion to build the subscriber list) and any WebSocket channel subscribers within the organization.

Response:
- Return the soft-deleted project entity with `deleted_at` populated so the caller can confirm the deletion timestamp.
- HTTP 200 OK on success.

operations.description:
Lists the members assigned to a specific project with pagination, filtering, and search capabilities.

Each member entry includes the employee's profile information (display name, position, employment type, status), their assigned role within the project (member or project-lead), and the date they joined the project. The response is paginated to efficiently handle projects with many members.

The operation supports filtering members by their project role, making it easy to identify project leads or regular members. Free-text search across employee names enables quick lookup of specific individuals. By default, only active memberships are returned — soft-deleted (removed) members are excluded unless explicitly requested.
operations.name: index

Join with erp_hrm_employees and erp_hrm_members to include employee profile information (display name, position, employment type, status). Apply optional filters from the request body: role (member or project-lead), employee status (active or deactivated), and free-text search on the member's display name via trigram similarity on erp_hrm_members.display_name. Exclude soft-deleted project members (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) by default; include them only when explicitly requested via an 'includeDeleted' filter flag. Support cursor-based or offset pagination via page/pageSize parameters. Sort by joined_at descending by default; support sort by employee name or role. Verify the project exists and belongs to the current organization context before querying. Return a paginated summary of project members with their employee details and membership metadata.

operations.description:
Assign an employee to a project with a specified membership role.

This endpoint creates a project membership, linking an active employee to a project within the current organization. The membership carries a role of either "member" for regular project participants or "project-lead" for those with elevated task management authority within the project.

**Authorization**: Requires the `project:manage` permission. Users without this permission will receive a 403 Forbidden response.

**Project Status Restriction**: Only projects with an `active` status accept new members. Attempting to assign a member to an archived or completed project results in a 422 Unprocessable Entity error.

**Employee Validation**: The employee must be active within the organization and belong to the same organization as the target project. Deactivated employees and employees from different organizations are rejected.

**Duplicate Prevention**: An employee cannot be assigned to the same project more than once. Attempting a duplicate assignment returns a 409 Conflict error.

**Role Default**: If no role is specified in the request, the membership defaults to "member".
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a project membership record that links an employee to a project with an assigned role.

**Validation Sequence**:
1. Verify the requesting user holds the `project:manage` permission within the current organization context.
2. Look up the project by `projectId` — reject with 404 if not found or if `deleted_at` is set. Verify the project belongs to the current organization.
3. Reject with 422 if the project status is `archived` or `completed` — new members cannot join non-active projects.
4. Look up the employee by `employeeId` from the request body — reject with 404 if not found or if `deleted_at` is set.
5. Reject with 422 if the employee's `status` is `deactivated`.
6. Reject with 422 if the employee's `erp_hrm_organization_id` does not match the project's `organization_id`.
7. Check the unique constraint `[erp_hrm_employee_id, erp_hrm_project_id]` — reject with 409 if a membership already exists (even if soft-deleted, reactivate the existing record or reject).

**Creation**:
- Set `erp_hrm_employee_id` from the request body.
- Set `erp_hrm_project_id` from the path parameter.
- Set `role` from the request body; if not provided, default to `"member"`. Validate the value is either `"member"` or `"project-lead"`.
- Set `joined_at` to the current timestamp (immutable — never updated).
- Set `created_at` and `updated_at` to the current timestamp.

**Response**: Return the newly created project membership record with all fields populated.

responseBody.description: The newly created project membership record, including the immutable joined-at timestamp and all identifying fields.

operations.description:
Update the role of an existing project member.

Changes the assigned role for a member who is already part of the project. The role can be switched between "member" (regular participant with time tracking and view access) and "project-lead" (elevated authority with task management permissions within the project).

The specific membership is identified by the combination of the project ID in the path and the employee ID provided in the request body. Only one membership record exists per employee-project pair.

This operation updates the membership's role without affecting the original join date. It does not create new project assignments — employees must already be members of the project.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update an existing project member's assigned role.

1. Validate the project exists within the current organization context and is not soft-deleted.
2. Look up the erp_hrm_project_members record matching projectId (from path) and the employeeId (from request body).
3. Reject with 404 if no active (deleted_at IS NULL) membership record exists for this employee-project pair.
4. Validate the requested role is either "member" or "project-lead".
5. Update the role column and set updated_at to now.
6. Do NOT modify joined_at — it remains the original assignment timestamp.
7. Return the updated project member record.

Edge cases:
- If the new role is the same as the current role, the update is idempotent — still succeeds and returns the record.
- The employee must belong to the same organization as the project.
- This operation does not create new memberships; use POST for assignment.

responseBody.description: The updated project member record reflecting the new role assignment, including the unchanged joined_at timestamp.

operations.description:
Removes an employee from a project by soft-deleting their project membership record.

The operation requires `project:manage` permission — project leads cannot remove other members from the project. Only users who hold the project management permission at the organization level may perform this action.

When a member is removed, the system clears all task assignments that linked the removed employee to tasks within this project. The tasks themselves remain in the project but become unassigned. All historical timelogs the employee recorded against the project are preserved intact and continue to appear in reports, timesheets, and other views.

Project-lead privileges held by the removed employee within this project are immediately revoked. The employee can no longer create, edit, or view tasks through project-lead authority within this project.

The project membership record is soft-deleted — the `deleted_at` timestamp is set while the record itself is retained for audit integrity. If the specified employee is not currently a member of the specified project, the request is rejected.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. VERIFY the requesting user holds `project:manage` permission. Reject with 403 Forbidden if not authorized.
2. QUERY the project by `projectId` scoped to the current organization (`organization_id`). Reject with 404 Not Found if the project does not exist or is soft-deleted (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL`).
3. QUERY the project membership using the composite unique constraint `@@unique([erp_hrm_employee_id, erp_hrm_project_id])` — match `erp_hrm_employee_id = employeeId` AND `erp_hrm_project_id = projectId`. Reject with 404 Not Found if no active membership exists (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL`).
4. SOFT-DELETE the membership record: SET `deleted_at = NOW()`, SET `updated_at = NOW()`.
5. CLEAR TASK ASSIGNMENTS: UPDATE all tasks in this project (`erp_hrm_project_id = projectId`) where `erp_hrm_employee_id` matches `employeeId`. Set `erp_hrm_employee_id = NULL` on those tasks.
6. PRESERVE TIMELOGS: Do not modify any timelogs belonging to the removed employee for this project. They remain intact.
7. RETURN 204 No Content on success.

operations.description:
List and search tasks within a specific project with comprehensive filtering, sorting, and pagination.

This endpoint returns a paginated collection of task summaries scoped to a single project. Each task summary includes essential fields — title, status, priority, due date, estimated hours, assigned employee name, and parent task reference — sufficient for project task boards and list views.

Filters allow narrowing results by status (open, in-progress, completed, closed), priority level, assigned employee, parent task relationship, and due date range. A text search filter leverages trigram indexing on task titles for fuzzy matching, enabling quick lookup by partial title.

Sorting is supported on due date, priority, and creation date in either ascending or descending order. The default ordering places most recently created tasks first.

Access is restricted to members of the project. Project leads can view all tasks within their project, and users with project management or project view permissions can access tasks across any project in the organization. Non-members receive a 403 Forbidden response.

Results exclude deleted tasks by default. Pagination metadata includes a cursor or page token for retrieving the next page of results and the total matching count for building UI pagination controls.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_tasks table filtered by the project ID from the path parameter. Apply additional filters from the request body:

- status: filter by one or more task statuses (open, in-progress, completed, closed).
- priority: filter by one or more priority levels (low, medium, high, urgent).
- assignedEmployeeId: filter by a specific assigned employee UUID.
- parentTaskId: filter by parent task UUID to retrieve subtasks of a specific parent, or filter where parentTaskId IS NULL to retrieve top-level tasks only.
- dueDateFrom / dueDateTo: filter by due date range (inclusive).
- search: text search on title using trigram index.

Sorting: support sort by due_date, priority, created_at in ascending or descending order. Default sort is by created_at descending.

Pagination: cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size. Return total count for UI pagination controls.

Authorization checks:
1. Verify the requesting user's employee record belongs to the same organization as the project.
2. Check that the employee is a member of the project via erp_hrm_project_members (non-deleted record) OR holds project:manage / project:view permission in the organization.
3. Reject with 403 Forbidden if none of the above conditions are met.

Exclude soft-deleted tasks (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results unless the requesting user holds project:manage permission and explicitly requests deleted tasks.

Join with erp_hrm_employees to include assignee display name in summary results. For subtasks, include parent task title for context.

Return paginated results with cursor/token for next page and total count.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of task summary records optimized for project task boards and list views. Includes assignee display name, parent task title, total matching count, and pagination cursor or page token.

Retrieves full details of a single task within a project.

Access to task details is governed by project membership. Employees can view tasks in projects they are assigned to. Project leads have broader access within their led projects. Users holding organization-level project management or project view permissions can access any task across the organization.

Authorization (per analysis section 156):
- Employees can view tasks only in projects they are assigned to as project members.
- Project leads (role: 'project-lead' in erp_hrm_project_members) can view all tasks within projects they lead.
- Users with 'project:manage' or 'project:view' permission can view any task in the organization.

Exclude soft-deleted tasks (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results unless the requesting user holds elevated permissions. Exclude soft-deleted project memberships when checking authorization.

Return a 404 if the project does not exist, the task does not exist, or the task does not belong to the specified project. Return a 403 if the requesting user is not authorized to view the task.

operations.description:
Creates a new task within a project.

Tasks are the fundamental units of work within a project, breaking down larger goals into individually manageable items that can be tracked, assigned, prioritized, and completed. Each task belongs to exactly one project and follows a status workflow from open through in-progress and completed to closed.

**Authorization**: Only users with organization-level project management permission (`project:manage`) or project-lead role on the target project may create tasks. A project-lead's authority is scoped to the specific project where they hold that role.

**Task Hierarchy**: Tasks support one level of subtask nesting through an optional parent task reference. A parent task cannot itself be a subtask (maximum depth of one). The parent task must belong to the same project.

**Assignment**: A task may optionally be assigned to an employee who must be an active member of the project. When the assigned employee is later removed from the project, the task assignment is cleared.

**Status and Priority**: New tasks default to `open` status and `medium` priority unless explicitly specified. Every status change is automatically recorded in the task's history for a complete audit trail.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new task within the specified project.

**Authorization**: The requesting user must hold either `project:manage` permission at the organization level, or be assigned as a project-lead on the target project via erp_hrm_project_members. Regular project members and unaffiliated users cannot create tasks.

**Validation**:
- Verify the project exists, belongs to the current organization, and is not soft-deleted.
- Reject if the project status is `archived` or `completed` — only active projects accept new tasks.
- If `assignedEmployeeId` is provided, verify the employee exists, belongs to the same organization, and holds an active (non-soft-deleted) membership in the project via erp_hrm_project_members. If not, return a validation error.
- If `parentTaskId` is provided, verify the parent task exists, belongs to the same project, is not soft-deleted, and does not itself have a parent task (enforcing one-level maximum nesting depth). Reject with an error if the parent task is already a subtask, does not belong to the same project, or references itself.
- `title` must be non-empty.
- `estimatedHours` must be a positive number when provided.
- `dueDate` must be in the future when provided.

**Defaults**:
- If `status` is not provided, default to `open` (the initial workflow state).
- If `priority` is not provided, default to `medium`.

**Execution**:
1. Validate all input constraints as described above.
2. Insert the task record into erp_hrm_tasks with `created_at` and `updated_at` set to the current timestamp.
3. Record the creation event in erp_hrm_task_histories as a status entry with old_status = null (indicating creation) and new_status = the chosen status.
4. Return the created task with all fields populated.

responseBody.description: The fully populated task entity including all generated fields such as id, timestamps, and the initial status.

operations.description:
Updates an existing task's details within a project.

Editable fields include the task's title, description, priority level, estimated hours, due date, assigned employee, and parent task relationship. The operation enforces project-level authorization — project leads can update tasks only within projects they lead, while users with organization-wide project management permission can update any task.

When reassigning the task to a different employee, the system validates that the new assignee is an active member of the project. When modifying the parent task for subtask nesting, the system enforces the one-level nesting rule, prevents cross-project parent references, and guards against circular relationships. The task's project association and status are immutable through this endpoint; status changes are handled through a dedicated workflow endpoint.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update an existing task identified by {taskId} within the project identified by {projectId}.

**Authorization:**
- Project leads can update tasks within projects where they hold the project-lead role (erp_hrm_project_members.role = 'project-lead').
- Users with project:manage permission can update any task in the organization.
- If the authenticated user is a project lead but the task belongs to a project where they are only a member (not project-lead), reject with a 403 Forbidden error unless they also hold project:manage permission.

**Validation:**
1. Verify the task exists and its erp_hrm_project_id matches {projectId}. If no match, return 404 Not Found.
2. Verify the task is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). If soft-deleted, return 404 Not Found.
3. If assigning an employee (erp_hrm_assigned_employee_id provided):
   a. Verify the employee exists in the same organization and is active.
   b. Verify the employee is a member of the project (exists in erp_hrm_project_members with erp_hrm_project_id matching {projectId} and deleted_at IS NULL).
   c. If not a project member, reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
4. If setting a parent task (erp_hrm_parent_task_id provided):
   a. Verify the parent task exists and belongs to the same project (erp_hrm_project_id = {projectId}).
   b. If the parent task belongs to a different project, reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
   c. Verify the parent task does not already have a parent of its own (erp_hrm_parent_task_id IS NULL on the parent). If it does, reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity — only one level of nesting is allowed.
   d. Verify the parent task is not the task itself (no self-referencing). If it is, reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
   e. Verify the parent task is not a descendant of the task being updated (no circular reference).
5. Reject any attempt to modify the task's project (erp_hrm_project_id) — tasks cannot be moved between projects.
6. Reject any attempt to modify the task's status through this endpoint — status changes go through the dedicated status transition endpoint.
7. Title must not be empty if provided.
8. Estimated hours must be a positive number if provided.

**Update Behavior:**
- Only fields explicitly provided in the request body are updated (partial update semantics).
- Automatically set updated_at to the current timestamp.
- All other fields (id, erp_hrm_project_id, created_at) remain unchanged.

operations.description:
Soft-deletes a task within a project.

Marks the specified task as deleted by setting its deletion timestamp. The task is excluded from normal queries thereafter but its data is preserved for referential integrity — historical timelogs, task history entries, and subtask relationships remain intact. The task is only physically removed when its parent project undergoes permanent deletion.

This operation requires the `project:manage` permission. Project leads, despite having task management authority within their projects, are not permitted to delete tasks. Task deletion is a management-level decision reserved for users with organization-wide project management privileges.

Soft-deleted tasks do not cascade to subtasks — child tasks remain accessible and must be deleted individually if desired. Existing timelogs referencing the deleted task continue to appear in timesheets and reports without interruption.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete a task by setting its `deleted_at` timestamp to the current time. The task is not physically removed — physical deletion only occurs when the parent project is deleted (cascade).

Authorization: Only users holding the `project:manage` permission may delete tasks. Project leads (employees with project-lead role on the project) are explicitly prohibited from deleting tasks, even within their own projects.

Validation rules:
- The task must exist and belong to the specified project (validate `erp_hrm_task_id` matches and `erp_hrm_project_id` equals `projectId`).
- The task must not already be soft-deleted (`deleted_at IS NULL`).
- The requesting user must have `project:manage` permission.

On success:
- Set `deleted_at` to the current timestamp.
- Set `updated_at` to the current timestamp.
- Task history entries (`erp_hrm_task_histories`) are preserved — they are only cascade-deleted when the parent project is deleted.
- Child tasks (subtasks via `erp_hrm_parent_task_id`) are NOT automatically deleted; they remain intact with their parent reference intact.
- Any timelogs linked to this task are NOT affected.

Error cases:
- 404 if task not found or does not belong to the specified project.
- 409 if task is already soft-deleted.
- 403 if requesting user lacks `project:manage` permission.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the project that owns the task.
parameters.name: projectId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the task to soft-delete.
parameters.name: taskId

prerequisites.description: The project identified by projectId must exist in the current organization and not be soft-deleted. Without a project, the task has no container and cannot be referenced.

The task identified by taskId must exist within the specified project and not already be soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). The delete operation sets deleted_at, so the task must be in a non-deleted state.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated, chronologically ordered list of status change history entries for a specific task.

Task history entries are immutable audit trail records that the system creates automatically whenever a task's status transitions. Each entry captures the old status before the change, the new status after the change, the timestamp of the transition, and the member who made the change.

Supported status values follow the task workflow: open, in-progress, completed, and closed. The history provides a complete record of how a task progressed through its lifecycle, enabling teams to audit workflow patterns and understand the full context of each task's development.

Access to task history follows the same visibility rules as viewing the task itself. Employees can view history for tasks in projects they are assigned to. Users with project management or project view permissions can view history for any task in the organization.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_task_histories table filtered by erp_hrm_task_id matching the {taskId} path parameter. First verify the task exists and belongs to the project specified by {projectId} — reject with 404 if the task does not exist or does not belong to the given project.

Enforce access control: the requesting user must be an employee assigned to the task's parent project, or hold project management permission, or hold project view permission. Reject with 403 otherwise.

Apply optional filters from the request body:
- Filter by old_status (one or more of: open, in-progress, completed, closed)
- Filter by new_status (one or more of: open, in-progress, completed, closed)
- Filter by changed_by_member_id (a specific member)
- Filter by created_at date range (from/to timestamps)

Exclude history entries for soft-deleted tasks (where the task's deleted_at is set).

Return results in chronological order by created_at ascending (oldest first). Apply cursor-based or offset-based pagination as specified in the request body. Each returned entry must include the id, old_status, new_status, created_at, and the changed_by_member_id.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of task status history entries in chronological order, each showing the old and new status, the member who made the change, and the timestamp of the transition.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the project containing the task.
parameters.name: projectId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the task whose status history is being retrieved.
parameters.name: taskId

requestBody.description: Optional filters for narrowing the status history results, including status values, the member who made the change, date range on when the change occurred, and pagination parameters.

prerequisites.description: Project must exist before any of its tasks or task histories can be accessed. The projectId path parameter must reference an existing project.
Task must exist and belong to the specified project before its status history can be queried. The taskId path parameter must reference an existing task within the project.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single task status history entry by its unique identifier.

Task history entries form an immutable audit trail that records every status transition a task undergoes. Each entry captures the status before and after the change, the timestamp of the transition, and the member who performed it. Status values follow the defined workflow: open, in-progress, completed, and closed.

Access is restricted to employees who are members of the parent project, or users holding project:manage or project:view permissions within the organization. This ensures task history visibility aligns with task visibility — users can only see history for tasks they are authorized to view.

History entries are created automatically by the system whenever a task's status is updated. They cannot be modified or deleted, preserving a complete and trustworthy chronological record of the task's lifecycle.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a single task history entry by its ID, validating the full parent chain.

1. Validate the project ({projectId}) exists in the current organization context and is not soft-deleted.
2. Validate the task ({taskId}) exists, belongs to the validated project, and is not soft-deleted.
3. Validate the history entry ({historyId}) exists and belongs to the validated task (erp_hrm_task_id matches).
4. Enforce access control following task visibility rules:
   - The requesting employee must be a member of the parent project (via project_members), OR
   - The user must hold project:manage or project:view permission in the organization.
5. Return the history entry with all fields: id, erp_hrm_task_id, changed_by_member_id, old_status, new_status, created_at.

Task history entries are immutable audit records — no update or delete operations exist. Status values are one of: open, in-progress, completed, closed.

responseBody.description: The full task history entry including the status transition details (old and new status), the member who performed the change, and the timestamp of the transition.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the project that contains the task whose history entry is being retrieved (UUID).
parameters.name: projectId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the task whose status change history entry is being retrieved (UUID).
parameters.name: taskId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific task history entry to retrieve (UUID).
parameters.name: historyId

prerequisites.description: Project must exist and be in active status before tasks can be created within it and before any task history entries can be accessed. The operation validates that {projectId} exists in the current organization context and is not soft-deleted.

Task must exist within the project before its history entries can be retrieved. The operation validates that {taskId} exists, belongs to the validated project, and is not soft-deleted. Task history entries are auto-generated by the system on status change — no POST endpoint exists for creating history entries directly.

operations.description:
List and search timelogs within the organization, with filtering, sorting, and pagination.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of timelog summaries. Employees can view only their own timelogs, while users with the view-all-time permission can browse all timelogs across the organization.

Multiple filter dimensions are supported simultaneously: narrow results by date range to focus on a specific period, by project or task to see time logged against particular work items, by billable status to distinguish billable from non-billable hours, and by employee (for managers) to review a specific team member's time entries.

Soft-deleted timelogs are excluded from results. Timelogs belonging to approved timesheets remain visible but are locked against modification — this endpoint only returns data, it does not perform mutations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_timelogs table with pagination and multi-dimensional filtering. Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from all results.

Authorization scoping:
- Without view-all-time permission: restrict to timelogs where employee_id matches the requesting employee, enforcing self-only visibility.
- With view-all-time permission: return all timelogs across the organization without employee restriction.

Filtering:
- Date range: filter by date between start and end dates when provided.
- Project: filter by project_id when specified.
- Task: filter by task_id when specified.
- Billable status: filter by billable flag when specified (true = billable only, false = non-billable only).
- Employee: when user has view-all-time permission and an employee_id filter is provided, restrict to that employee's timelogs.

Sorting: default sort by date descending, then created_at descending. Support optional sort by date, duration_minutes, or created_at in ascending or descending order.

Pagination: use cursor-based or offset-based pagination. Include total count for UI pagination controls.

Join with erp_hrm_projects for project name and erp_hrm_tasks for task title when populating summary DTO fields for display context.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timelog summary records optimized for list displays, including project name, task title, date, duration, billable status, and employee context.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering and paginating timelogs. Supports date range, project, task, billable status, and employee filters. All filters are optional and combinable.

operations.description:
Create a new timelog entry to record work performed by an employee on a specific date.

Each timelog captures a duration in minutes against a required project and an optional task within that project. The billable flag, defaulting to true, distinguishes billable from non-billable work for reporting purposes.

Employees can only create timelogs for themselves by default. Users with the time:manage permission may create timelogs on behalf of any active employee within the organization. The employee must be a member of the target project, and the project must be in active status to accept new time entries.

Timelogs are created independently of timesheets. Once created, a timelog can later be added to a draft timesheet through the timesheet management operations.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new timelog entry recording work performed by an employee.

**Authorization & Ownership:**
- Without the `time:manage` permission: the employee is derived from the authenticated user's session. The request must NOT include an employee_id. The timelog is automatically associated with the calling employee.
- With the `time:manage` permission: an optional `employee_id` may be specified to create the timelog on behalf of another employee. If omitted, defaults to the calling employee.

**Validation Rules:**
- The employee must be in `active` status. Reject with error if deactivated (section 333).
- The employee must be a member of the specified project through erp_hrm_project_members. Reject if not.
- The project must be in `active` status. Reject if archived or completed (section 110).
- If `task_id` is provided, the task must belong to the same project referenced by `project_id`. Reject if the task's project does not match.
- `duration_minutes` must be a positive integer. Reject if zero or negative.
- `date` must be a valid calendar date.
- `billable` defaults to `true` when not explicitly provided.

**Database Operations:**
- INSERT a single row into `erp_hrm_timelogs` with the validated fields.
- Set `created_at` and `updated_at` to the current timestamp.
- Return the complete created timelog including all server-generated fields (id, created_at, updated_at).

**Edge Cases:**
- Deactivated employees cannot create timelogs (section 333).
- If the employee's active timer is stopped, that is a separate flow handled by the timer stop operation — this endpoint does not interact with timers.

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog with all server-assigned fields including the unique identifier and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Data required to create a new timelog. Includes the project, date, duration in minutes, optional task and description, and billable status. The employee_id may be specified by users with the time:manage permission to create timelogs on behalf of other employees.

prerequisites.description: Project must exist and be in active status before any timelog can be created against it. project_id is a required field in the timelog request body.

The logging employee must be a member of the target project before time can be logged against it. Business rules reject timelogs where the employee lacks an active project membership (sections 49, 62, 451).

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timelog entry by its unique identifier.

Returns the full timelog record including the date, duration in minutes, billable flag, description, and timestamps. Related entity information — such as the owning employee, associated project, optional task, and optional timesheet — is included to provide complete context for the time entry.

Access is restricted to the timelog's owner and to users with the view-all-time permission. All access is scoped to the currently selected organization; timelogs from other organizations are never exposed.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a single timelog by its primary key. Query the erp_hrm_timelogs table filtering by id = :timelogId and deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted records).

Enforce organization scoping: join through erp_hrm_employees to verify the timelog's employee belongs to the current session's organization. If the timelog does not belong to the current organization, return 404.

Enforce access control:
- If the requesting user is the timelog owner (employee.user_id matches session user), allow access.
- Otherwise, the user must hold the view-all-time permission. If neither condition is met, return 403.

Include related entity details suitable for a detail view: the employee's display name, the project's name, the task's title (if task_id is set), and the timesheet's week range (if timesheet_id is set). Return the full timelog with all fields including id, date, duration_minutes, description, billable, created_at, updated_at, and the related entity summaries.

If no timelog matches the given ID (either it does not exist or is soft-deleted), return 404 with an appropriate error message.

responseBody.description: The complete timelog record with all fields and related entity summaries.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timelog to retrieve (UUID format).
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Update an existing timelog entry.

Allows the owner of a timelog or a user with the time:manage permission to modify the details of a previously logged time entry. This operation supports correcting dates, adjusting durations, reassigning work to different projects or tasks, updating descriptions, and toggling the billable flag.

**Lock enforcement:** Timelogs that are part of an approved timesheet are immutable — no fields can be changed regardless of the user's permissions. Timelogs assigned to draft or submitted timesheets remain editable by their owner or a time:manage holder.

**Project membership:** The employee who owns the timelog must be an active member of the target project. Only projects with active status accept timelog updates; archived and completed projects reject modifications.

**Task integrity:** When a task is specified, it must belong to the selected project. This constraint maintains referential integrity across the project-task-timelog relationship chain.

**Soft-deleted exclusion:** Soft-deleted timelogs cannot be updated. Any attempt to update a soft-deleted timelog results in a 404 response.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update an existing timelog identified by timelogId.

**Authorization:**
- The requesting employee must either own the timelog (employee_id matches the requesting user's employee record) OR hold the time:manage permission.
- When the employee owns the timelog but lacks time:manage, only their own timelogs can be updated.
- When the user holds time:manage, they may update any employee's timelog within the organization.

**Preconditions — reject with appropriate status if violated:**
- The timelog must exist and not be soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). Return 404 if not found or soft-deleted.
- The timelog must not belong to an approved timesheet. If the timelog's timesheet_id references an erp_hrm_timesheets record with status 'approved', reject with 409 Conflict (Section 279 — approved-timesheet lock).

**Validation rules:**
1. date (required): The calendar date the work was performed. Must be a valid date.
2. duration_minutes (required): A positive integer representing the work session length in minutes. Must be greater than zero.
3. project_id (required): Must reference an erp_hrm_projects record in the same organization. The project must have status 'active' (Sections 45, 110). The timelog owner (employee_id) must be an active member of the project (exists in erp_hrm_project_members with matching employee_id and project_id).
4. task_id (optional): If provided, must reference an erp_hrm_tasks record whose project_id matches the supplied project_id. If task_id is provided but does not belong to the selected project, reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
5. description (optional): Free-text description of the work performed. May be set to null to clear the description.
6. billable (required): Boolean indicating whether the time entry is billable.

**Execution:**
- Locate the timelog by id (UUID). Return 404 if not found or soft-deleted.
- Verify the requesting user's organization context matches the timelog owner's organization.
- Verify authorization: ownership check (timelog.employee_id equals the requesting user's employee ID) OR permission check (time:manage).
- Verify approved-timesheet lock: if timesheet_id is set, load the referenced timesheet and check its status is not 'approved'.
- Validate all input fields against the rules above.
- Update the timelog record: set date, duration_minutes, project_id, task_id, description, billable. The updated_at field is set to the current timestamp automatically.
- Return the updated timelog with all fields populated, including its related employee, project, task, and timesheet references.

responseBody.description: The updated timelog with all fields reflecting the applied changes. Includes populated references to the owning employee, target project, associated task (if any), and timesheet (if assigned).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timelog to update. UUID v4 format.
parameters.name: timelogId

requestBody.description: Complete set of updatable fields for the timelog. All required fields (date, duration_minutes, project_id, billable) must be provided. Optional fields (task_id, description) may be omitted or set to null to clear their value. Employee ownership and timesheet assignment are managed through separate workflows and cannot be changed via this endpoint.

prerequisites.description: The project referenced by the request body's required project_id field must exist and be in active status. Archived or completed projects freeze timelog modifications per Section 110, so the project must be created and active before the timelog can be updated.

The employee who owns the timelog must be an active member of the target project. Per Section 49, project membership is a prerequisite for time logging — the specification explicitly validates that the timelog owner exists in erp_hrm_project_members with matching employee_id and project_id.

The timelog identified by the path parameter timelogId must exist and not be soft-deleted before it can be updated. The PUT operation returns 404 if the timelog is not found, so the timelog must be created first via this endpoint.

operations.description:
Delete a timelog entry.

Removes a single timelog entry via soft deletion, preserving the record for audit purposes while making it unavailable for further operations. The deletion is subject to strict access control and timesheet workflow constraints.

Employees may only delete their own timelogs, and only when those timelogs are not currently under review (not part of a submitted or approved timesheet). Users with the time management permission (time:manage) have broader authority and may delete any employee's timelog, including those within submitted timesheets awaiting approval.
