This endpoint creates the erp_hrm_member_password_resets record — generating the cryptographic token, setting the expiration, and linking to the target member — which provides the resetId required by the completion endpoint's path parameter.

operations.description:
Verify an email address by consuming a one-time verification token sent during the sign-up process.

When a guest completes sign-up, the system creates a member account and dispatches a verification email containing a unique, time-limited token. This endpoint accepts that token and confirms that the email address belongs to the user who created the account.

Upon successful verification, the system automatically matches any pending organization invitations targeting the verified email address. The user is enrolled into each inviting organization as an employee with the role specified in the invitation, and those invitations are marked as fulfilled. This automatic enrollment operates regardless of whether the user is authenticated at the time of verification.

Tokens are single-use and expire after a system-defined duration. An expired token is rejected with an appropriate error. Verification is idempotent — submitting an already-verified token returns a success response confirming the email has already been verified, rather than producing an error.
operations.name: verify
operations.specification:
Receive a verification token from the request body and verify the associated email address.

Look up the `erp_hrm_member_email_verifications` record by the unique `token` value provided in the request body. If no matching record exists, reject with a generic error message — do not reveal whether the token corresponds to an existing account.

Validate the token has not expired: compare `expires_at` against the current server timestamp. If `expires_at` is in the past, reject the verification with an expired-token error. The expired record is preserved for audit purposes.

Check that the token has not already been consumed: `verified_at` must be null. If `verified_at` is already populated, return a success response with the existing record — do not reject, as verification is idempotent.

Upon passing all validations, set `verified_at` to the current timestamp and `updated_at` to the current timestamp. Persist the update in a transaction.

After successful verification, within the same transaction or as a post-commit action, automatically match any pending invitations in the `erp_hrm_invitations` table where `email` equals the verified email address and `status` is `pending`. For each matched invitation:
- Update the invitation `status` to `fulfilled`.
- Create the corresponding `erp_hrm_employees` record linking the member (`erp_hrm_member_id`) to the inviting organization with the role specified in the invitation.

Return the updated verification record including the `verified_at` timestamp.

responseBody.description: The email verification record after successful verification. Includes the `verified_at` timestamp confirming when the email address was verified. If the token was already verified, returns the previously verified record.

requestBody.description: The verification token string received via email. This is a cryptographically secure, globally unique token generated during the sign-up process and delivered to the user's email address.

operations.description:
Verify a member's email address by consuming a one-time verification token delivered during sign-up.

This endpoint confirms email ownership and completes the registration verification step. The verification token is embedded in the link sent to the user's email address after sign-up. Tokens have a limited lifespan — expired tokens are rejected and the user must request a new verification email.

**Invitation Fulfillment**: Upon successful verification, the system automatically checks for any pending organization invitations sent to the verified email address. Matching invitations are fulfilled and the user is enrolled as an employee in those organizations, gaining immediate access upon their next login.

**Security**: Each token can only be used once. Attempting to verify an already-consumed token returns a conflict error. The token is cryptographically secure and globally unique, preventing enumeration attacks.
operations.name: verify
operations.specification:
Verify a member's email address by consuming a one-time verification token.

Look up the erp_hrm_member_email_verifications record where token equals the {verificationId} path parameter. The lookup uses the unique token index — do not use the UUID primary key for lookup.

Reject the request if:
- No verification record exists with the given token (return 404 not-found)
- The token has already been consumed (verified_at is not null) — return a conflict error indicating the email was already verified
- The token has expired (expires_at is before the current timestamp) — return a gone/expired error

On success, update the record:
- Set verified_at to the current timestamp
- Set updated_at to the current timestamp

After successful verification, automatically fulfill pending invitations:
- Query erp_hrm_invitations where email equals the verified email address and status is 'pending'
- For each matching invitation, update its status to 'fulfilled' and create an erp_hrm_employees record linking the member to the inviting organization with the role specified in the invitation

Return the updated verification record including the email, verified_at timestamp, and status.

responseBody.description: The verification record confirming successful email verification, including the verified email address and the timestamp when verification occurred.

parameters.description: The cryptographically secure verification token sent to the user's email address during sign-up. This is the unique token string, not the UUID primary key of the verification record.
parameters.name: verificationId

operations.description:
Permanently delete the authenticated member's own account.

This endpoint initiates full account deletion. Before deletion proceeds, the system verifies that the member is not the sole owner of any active organization. If the member is the sole owner anywhere, the request is rejected and the member must first transfer ownership to another active employee in that organization or delete the organization entirely.

When deletion is allowed, all of the member's employee records in other organizations are deactivated rather than removed. This preserves historical data — including timelogs, timesheets, activity log entries, and contracts — ensuring organizational records remain intact. The member's global profile information is permanently removed, and the member can no longer authenticate or access any organization.

Account deletion events are emitted to all affected organizations so that owners and managers can take appropriate action regarding the deactivated employee's projects, tasks, and pending timesheets.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Identify the authenticated member from the current session context.

**Sole Owner Check**: Before proceeding, query all organizations where the member holds the built-in Owner role. For each such organization, count the total number of active employees assigned the Owner role. If any organization has exactly one active Owner (the requesting member), reject the deletion with an error indicating ownership must be transferred or the organization must be deleted first.

**Employee Deactivation**: For all other organizations where the member is an active employee but NOT a sole owner, update the corresponding `erp_hrm_employees` records: set `status` to `deactivated` and set `updated_at` to the current timestamp. Do NOT delete these employee records — historical timelogs, timesheets, contracts, and activity logs must remain intact.

**Member Soft Delete**: Set `deleted_at` to the current timestamp on the `erp_hrm_members` record. The member's authentication credentials become invalid immediately — subsequent login attempts with this email must be rejected.

**Event Emission**: Emit an account deletion event to each organization where the member held an active employee record. The event payload must include the deleted member ID, the deletion timestamp, and a notification that the corresponding employee record has been deactivated.

**Transaction**: Wrap the employee deactivation updates and member soft-delete in a database transaction to ensure atomicity.

operations.description:
Send an employee invitation to join the current organization by email.

Creates a pending invitation record and delivers an invitation email to the specified address. The invitation remains in pending status indefinitely until the recipient signs up with the matching email address, at which point it is automatically fulfilled and the user is added as an employee.

This operation requires the employee:manage permission. Only one pending invitation per email address can exist within an organization at a time.

If the invited email address corresponds to an existing user who has not yet joined this organization, the invitation is fulfilled immediately upon signup with email matching.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new pending invitation in the current organization context.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the authenticated user has employee:manage permission in the current organization (reject with 403 if not).
2. Validate the invited email address format.
3. Check for duplicate pending invitation: if a pending invitation already exists for the same email in the current organization, reject with a conflict error (409).
4. Create the invitation record with status='pending', recording the current timestamp as the sent time.
5. Deliver the invitation email to the recipient (fire-and-forget; email delivery failure does not roll back the invitation creation).
6. Return the created invitation with all fields.

Edge cases:
- If the invited email already belongs to an active employee in the organization, reject with 409 (already a member).
- Multi-org: the same email can have pending invitations in different organizations simultaneously.
- The invitation has no expiration and remains pending indefinitely until fulfilled, revoked, or the organization is deleted.

responseBody.description: The created invitation record including its ID, invited email, pending status, and sent timestamp.

requestBody.description: The email address to send the invitation to.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of invitations sent from the current organization.

This endpoint allows users with the employee:manage permission to browse all invitations associated with their organization. Each invitation record includes the invited email address, the invitation's current status (pending, fulfilled, or revoked), the timestamp when the invitation was sent, and identifying information about the user who sent the invitation.

The list supports filtering by invitation status — managers can narrow results to pending invitations awaiting acceptance, fulfilled invitations already accepted, or revoked invitations that were cancelled. Users can also search by the invited email address using partial matching to locate a specific invitation.

Results are paginated and returned sorted with the most recently sent invitations first. Only invitations belonging to the caller's currently selected organization context are returned.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query all invitation records belonging to the current session's selected organization.

Enforce permission check: the caller's assigned role within the current organization must include the employee:manage permission. Return 403 Forbidden if the caller lacks this permission.

Apply request body filters as AND conditions:
- status: when provided, filter by the invitation's status field. Valid values are 'pending', 'fulfilled', and 'revoked'. When omitted, return invitations regardless of status.
- email: when provided, perform a case-insensitive partial substring match (e.g., SQL ILIKE '%value%' or equivalent) against the invited email address field. When omitted, no email filter is applied.
- Apply standard pagination parameters (page size, cursor or offset) as defined in IErpHrmInvitation.IRequest.

The inviter's identifying information (such as name and email from the associated user record) should be included in each result row via a join with the user/employee tables through the invitation's sender reference.

Sort results by the invitation creation timestamp in descending order so the most recently sent invitations appear first.

Restrict all results to invitations belonging to the caller's currently selected organization — never return invitations from other organizations.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of invitation summary records. Each record contains the invitation identifier, the invited email address, the current status, the timestamp when the invitation was sent, and basic information about the inviter (name and email).

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for browsing invitations. Includes an optional status filter (one of: pending, fulfilled, revoked), an optional email search string for case-insensitive partial matching against the invited email address, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Revoke a pending invitation.

Cancels a pending invitation so it can no longer be fulfilled. The invitation transitions from "pending" to "revoked" status and the invited email address will not automatically receive organization membership upon signup.

This operation requires the employee:manage permission. It is scoped to the current organization context — only invitations belonging to the user's active organization can be revoked.

Once revoked, the invitation is permanently finalized in that state. It cannot be reactivated or returned to pending status. The revoked invitation record remains in the system for audit purposes and is only removed if the entire organization is deleted.

Only invitations in "pending" status are eligible for revocation. Attempting to revoke an invitation that has already been fulfilled (the user signed up and joined the organization) or was previously revoked will result in a conflict error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Transition the invitation status from "pending" to "revoked".

Implementation steps:
1. Validate that the authenticated user has the employee:manage permission in their current organization context. Reject with 403 Forbidden if not.
2. Look up the invitation by invitationId, scoped to the user's current organization (erp_hrm_organization_id).
3. If no invitation matches, return 404 Not Found.
4. Check the invitation's current status:
   - If "pending": proceed with revocation.
   - If "fulfilled": return 409 Conflict — fulfilled invitations cannot be revoked.
   - If "revoked": return 409 Conflict — already revoked.
5. Update the invitation record: set status to "revoked", record the revocation timestamp, and record the revoking user for accountability.
6. Log the revocation action to the activity log (action type: invitation_revoked).
7. Return the updated invitation record with all fields including the new status and revocation timestamp.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the invitation to revoke, scoped to the current organization.
parameters.name: invitationId

prerequisites.description: An invitation must be created and be in "pending" status before it can be revoked. The target operation looks up the invitation by invitationId and requires it to exist with "pending" status — otherwise it returns 404 or 409.

operations.description:
Deactivates an active employee, immediately suspending their ability to log time entries and submit timesheets within the organization.

Deactivation is a reversible status change that marks the employee as inactive while preserving all historical records without modification. Timelogs, timesheets, contract records, and project assignments remain fully intact and can be accessed through appropriate read endpoints.

This action requires the `employee:manage` permission. The operation is scoped to the acting user's currently selected organization — only employees within that organization can be deactivated.

If the target employee is already deactivated, the operation completes successfully as a no-op, returning the employee's current state without any data modification.
operations.name: deactivate
operations.specification:
Deactivate an active employee by setting their status to 'deactivated'.

**Authorization**: Requires `employee:manage` permission. The operation is scoped to the session's current organization (`erp_hrm_organization_id`).

**Implementation steps**:
1. Look up the employee by `employeeId` UUID within the session's current organization. Return 404 if the employee is not found or if `deleted_at` is set (soft-deleted records are excluded).
2. If the employee's current `status` is already 'deactivated', return 200 with the existing employee record and a no-op indication — no database write is performed.
3. Otherwise, update the employee record: set `status` to 'deactivated', set `updated_at` to the current timestamp.
4. Return 200 with the updated employee record.

**Side effects**: The deactivated employee can no longer create timelogs, edit existing timelogs, or submit timesheets. Existing project and task assignments are retained but effectively suspended. All historical data — timelogs, timesheets, contracts — is preserved without modification or deletion.

**Edge cases**:
- Deactivating an already-deactivated employee → no-op, return current state.
- Employee belongs to a different organization → 404.
- Employee is soft-deleted → 404.
- Insufficient permissions → 403.

responseBody.description: The employee record reflecting the deactivated status. If the employee was already deactivated, the record is returned unchanged with an indication that no state change occurred.

parameters.description: UUID of the employee to deactivate. Scoped to the acting user's current organization context.
parameters.name: employeeId

prerequisites.description: Employee must exist before deactivation — the deactivate operation looks up the employee by employeeId and returns 404 if not found. POST /erpHrm/member/employees creates the employee record.

operations.description:
Reactivates a previously deactivated employee, restoring their ability to log time entries, submit timesheets, and participate in projects and tasks within the organization.

Reactivation is the inverse of deactivation. It restores an employee to active status without modifying any of their existing data — role assignment, department membership, position, employment type, and all historical records remain exactly as they were before deactivation. The reactivated employee's permissions take effect immediately based on their assigned role.

If the employee is already active at the time of the request, the operation completes successfully without any changes to the record (no-op).

Only users with the employee management permission can perform this operation.
operations.name: reactivate
operations.specification:
Locate the employee by `employeeId` UUID within the currently selected organization context (`erp_hrm_organization_id`). Verify the employee record exists and belongs to the calling user's active organization — return 404 if not found or if the record has a non-null `deleted_at` timestamp.

Authorization: the calling user must hold the `employee:manage` permission within the organization. Return 403 if the permission is absent.

Check the current `status` column:
- If already `active`, respond with 200 and the employee record as-is (no-op — per Section 210). No database write occurs.
- If `deactivated`, update the `status` column to `active` and set `updated_at` to the current timestamp. Return 200 with the updated employee record.

No other fields are modified during reactivation. The employee retains their existing role (`erp_hrm_role_id`), department (`erp_hrm_department_id`), position, and employment type. All historical data — timelogs, timesheets, contracts, and project memberships — is already preserved and requires no action.

After reactivation, the employee can immediately log time entries, submit timesheets, and be assigned to projects and tasks per their role permissions.

responseBody.description: The employee record reflecting the active status. If the employee was already active, the record is returned unchanged. All associated fields — role, department, position, and employment type — are preserved as-is.

parameters.description: UUID identifying the employee to reactivate within the currently selected organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Changes the role assigned to an employee within the current organization.

The new role's permission set determines all access rights for the employee and takes effect immediately upon successful assignment. Each employee holds exactly one role at any given time — this operation replaces the existing role assignment with the specified target role.

Any available role within the organization may be assigned, including both built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) and custom roles. There is no restriction on how many employees may hold the same role, including the Owner role.

The role change is recorded in the activity log with the previous role, new role, and the identity of the user who performed the change, ensuring full auditability.

Requires the `employee:manage` permission. The target role must belong to the same organization as the employee.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the `erp_hrm_role_id` field on the `erp_hrm_employees` record identified by `employeeId`.

**Authorization**: Requires `employee:manage` permission. The calling user must belong to the same organization as the target employee.

**Validation**:
1. Look up the employee by `employeeId` within the current organization context (filter by `erp_hrm_organization_id`). Return 404 if not found or if the employee is soft-deleted (`deleted_at` is not null).
2. Look up the target role by the provided role ID. Return 404 if the role does not exist.
3. Verify the role belongs to the same organization as the employee (`erp_hrm_organization_id` must match). Return 400 if the role belongs to a different organization.
4. Verify the role is not soft-deleted (`deleted_at` must be null). Return 400 if the role has been deleted.
5. Optionally, skip the update if the employee is already assigned to the requested role (no-op success).

**Update**:
1. Capture the previous `erp_hrm_role_id` before the update.
2. Set `erp_hrm_role_id` to the new role ID and update `updated_at` to the current timestamp.
3. Insert an activity log entry into `erp_hrm_activity_logs` with:
   - `action_type`: "role_changed"
   - `target_entity`: "employee"
   - `target_id`: the employee's ID
   - `user_id`: the authenticated user performing the change
   - `organization_id`: the current organization ID
   - `details`: JSON containing `{ "previous_role_id": "...", "new_role_id": "..." }`
   - `created_at`: current timestamp
4. Return the updated employee record with its new role assignment.

**Edge cases**:
- If the employee is deactivated (`status` = "deactivated"), the role change should still be allowed — deactivation does not prevent administrative actions.
- The new permissions take effect immediately upon successful update. No cache invalidation delay.

responseBody.description: The updated employee record reflecting the new role assignment.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the employee whose role is being changed.
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: The target role to assign to the employee. Must reference a role within the same organization.

prerequisites.description: Target role must exist in the organization before it can be assigned to an employee. The operation validates the role exists, is not soft-deleted, and belongs to the same organization as the employee.
Employee must exist in the organization before their role can be changed. The operation looks up the employee by ID and returns 404 if not found or soft-deleted.

operations.description:
Stops a currently running timer and automatically creates a timelog from the tracked session.

When called, this endpoint calculates the elapsed time from when the timer was started to the current moment, rounds the duration to the nearest whole minute, and creates a new timelog entry. The resulting timelog carries over the project, optional task, and description that were set on the timer at the moment of stopping. The billable flag on the new timelog defaults to true.

After the timelog is successfully created, the timer is permanently deleted. This frees the employee to start a new timer — each employee may only have one active timer at any given time.

The timer must belong to the authenticated employee. Attempting to stop a timer owned by another employee results in a forbidden error. If no timer exists with the given identifier, or if the timer has already been stopped or discarded, the request is rejected because no active timer exists to stop.
operations.name: stop
operations.specification:
Stop the running timer identified by timerId and create a corresponding timelog.

1. Verify the timer exists. If not found, return 404.
2. Verify the timer belongs to the authenticated employee (erp_hrm_employee_id matches). If not, return 403.
3. Verify the timer is currently running. The timer must exist — since stopped and discarded timers are deleted from the erp_hrm_timers table, a found timer is necessarily running. If no timer exists for this timerId, return 404 with an error indicating no active timer exists to stop.
4. Calculate elapsed duration: compute the difference between the current timestamp and the timer's start_timestamp. Convert to minutes and round to the nearest whole minute. Use standard rounding (0.5 and above rounds up, below rounds down).
5. Create a new timelog in erp_hrm_timelogs with the following properties:
   - employee_id: the authenticated employee's ID
   - project_id: the timer's erp_hrm_project_id
   - task_id: the timer's erp_hrm_task_id (may be null)
   - date: the current date (date-only, use today's date at time of stopping)
   - duration_minutes: the calculated and rounded duration
   - description: the timer's description (may be null)
   - billable: true (default)
   - timesheet_id: null (not assigned to any timesheet initially)
6. Delete the timer row from erp_hrm_timers. This frees the employee to start a new timer (the @@unique([erp_hrm_employee_id]) constraint allows only one active timer per employee).
7. Emit a timer-stopped event with the calculated duration and confirmation that the timelog was created. Deliver the event exclusively to the employee who stopped the timer.
8. Return the newly created timelog record.

Edge cases:
- If the elapsed duration rounds to 0 minutes (timer was started and immediately stopped within ~29 seconds), still create the timelog with duration_minutes = 0.
- If the timer has been running for a very long duration (employee forgot to stop it), accept the full elapsed duration as valid. There is no maximum duration limit.
- The start_timestamp remains unchanged throughout the timer's life; only project, task, and description are editable while running.

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog resulting from stopping the timer. Contains the calculated duration (rounded to the nearest minute), the project, optional task, description carried over from the timer, and the billable flag defaulting to true. The date reflects the current date when the timer was stopped.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the running timer to stop. Must be a timer that belongs to the authenticated employee and is currently active. (UUID format)
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: A running timer must exist before it can be stopped. The timer is created by starting a live time tracking session, which establishes the timer record with its project, optional task, description, and start timestamp. Without this prerequisite, the stop operation returns 404 because no active timer exists to stop.

operations.description:
Discards the currently running timer, permanently removing all tracking data without creating a timelog.

When an employee discards their running timer, the system permanently deletes the timer record including its start timestamp, associated project, task, and description. No timelog entry is created, and no record of the elapsed time is retained. This operation is irreversible — once discarded, the tracked time is lost.

An employee may only discard a timer that is currently running and belongs to them. Attempting to discard a timer that does not exist or is not actively running results in an error. Each employee is limited to at most one active timer at any time, enforced by a unique constraint on the employee reference in the database. After discarding, the employee is free to start a new timer.
operations.name: discard
operations.specification: Look up the timer by the provided timerId UUID in the erp_hrm_timers table. Verify the timer exists and belongs to the currently authenticated employee — compare erp_hrm_employee_id against the authenticated user's employee record within the current organization context. If the timer does not exist or does not belong to the requesting employee, reject with a 404 error. If the timer exists but is not actively running (edge case guarded by the @@unique constraint on erp_hrm_employee_id, but verify nonetheless), reject with an error indicating no active timer exists to discard. On success, delete the timer row from erp_hrm_timers entirely — do NOT create a timelog, do NOT retain any record of the elapsed time, do NOT persist any timer data elsewhere. Emit a timer-discarded real-time event scoped exclusively to the owning employee. The event payload must confirm that no timelog was created as a result of the discard operation. If no active timer exists for the employee at the time of the request, reject the operation and do not emit any event.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the running timer to discard. Must be a valid UUID referencing an existing timer owned by the authenticated employee in the current organization context. (global scope)
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: A running timer must exist before it can be discarded. The timer is created by starting a live time tracking session via this operation, which establishes the timerId referenced in the discard path.

operations.description:
Submits a draft timesheet for review.

When an employee submits a timesheet, the system transitions it from draft to submitted status, records the submission timestamp, and makes it available for review by users with time approval permission.

The timesheet must meet several conditions to be submittable: it must be in draft status, must contain at least one timelog, must belong to the authenticated employee, and must cover a week that has already started (future week submissions are rejected). Additionally, only one timesheet per employee per calendar week can be in submitted or approved status at any time — duplicate submissions for the same week are rejected.

Once submitted, the timesheet can be approved or rejected by an authorized reviewer. If rejected, it returns to draft status and the employee can modify its timelogs and resubmit.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification:
Transition the specified timesheet from draft to submitted status.

1. Look up the timesheet by {timesheetId}. Return 404 if not found.
2. Verify the timesheet belongs to the authenticated employee (scope to current organization via employee.organization_id). Return 403 if the timesheet is not owned by the authenticated employee.
3. Verify the timesheet is in 'draft' status. Return 409 Conflict if status is not 'draft'.
4. Verify the timesheet contains at least one timelog (JOIN erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id = {timesheetId} AND deleted_at IS NULL). Return 422 if no timelogs are associated.
5. Verify the timesheet's week_end_date (Sunday) is not in the future — the week must have already started. Return 422 if week_end_date is after the current date.
6. Verify no other timesheet for the same employee and same week_start_date is already in 'submitted' or 'approved' status (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM erp_hrm_timesheets WHERE employee_id = timesheet.employee_id AND week_start_date = timesheet.week_start_date AND id != {timesheetId} AND status IN ('submitted', 'approved') AND deleted_at IS NULL). Return 409 Conflict if a duplicate exists.
7. Update the timesheet: SET status = 'submitted', submitted_at = NOW().
8. Return the updated timesheet.

responseBody.description: The timesheet after successful submission, with status updated to 'submitted' and the submission timestamp recorded.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to submit for approval.
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: A draft timesheet must be created before it can be submitted. The timesheet identified by {timesheetId} must exist and be in draft status for the submit operation to succeed.

The timesheet must contain at least one timelog before submission. The submit operation specification explicitly checks for timelogs and returns 422 if none are associated. This prerequisite must execute after the timesheet is created.

operations.description:
Approves a submitted timesheet, finalizing the review process.

This endpoint transitions a timesheet from submitted to approved status. Approval is a terminal state — once approved, a timesheet cannot be modified, rejected, or returned to any other status. All timelogs contained within the approved timesheet become permanently locked against editing or deletion, regardless of the caller's permission level.

Only users who hold the time:approve permission within the current organization may perform this action. The reviewer's identity and the approval timestamp are automatically recorded from the authenticated session.

Upon successful approval, the system emits a real-time event notifying both the timesheet owner and all other approvers in the organization that the timesheet has been approved and its timelogs are now locked.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Approve a submitted timesheet, transitioning it from submitted to approved status and locking all contained timelogs.

**Authorization**: Require the authenticated user to hold the `time:approve` permission within the current organization context. Return 403 Forbidden if the user lacks this permission.

**Lookup**: Query the `erp_hrm_timesheets` table by `id` matching `timesheetId`. The timesheet must belong to the currently selected organization — join through `erp_hrm_employees.organization_id` using the timesheet's `employee_id`. Return 404 Not Found if no matching timesheet exists or if it belongs to a different organization.

**Status Validation**: Verify the timesheet's `status` field value:
- If `"approved"`: return 409 Conflict with a message indicating the timesheet has already been approved (approved is a terminal state and no further transitions are permitted).
- If `"draft"`: return 422 Unprocessable Entity indicating the timesheet must be submitted before it can be approved.
- If `"rejected"`: return 422 Unprocessable Entity indicating the timesheet must be resubmitted by the employee before approval.
- If `"submitted"`: proceed with approval.

**Update (in a single transaction)**:
- Set `status` to `"approved"`
- Set `reviewed_by_user_id` to the current authenticated user's ID (from `erp_hrm_members`)
- Set `reviewed_at` to the current timestamp
- Set `updated_at` to the current timestamp

**Timelog Locking**: All records in `erp_hrm_timelogs` where `timesheet_id` equals this timesheet's `id` become locked. This lock is enforced at the service layer — subsequent attempts to edit or delete these timelogs must be rejected regardless of the caller's permissions, including the `time:manage` permission. The lock is permanent; no unlock mechanism exists.

**Event Emission**: Emit a timesheet approval event containing the timesheet ID, the reviewer's identity (user ID), and the review timestamp. Deliver this event to:
- The timesheet owner (the employee identified by `employee_id`)
- All users who hold the `time:approve` permission within the organization
Event delivery must be scoped to the current organization context.

**Response**: Return the fully updated timesheet record including the new status, reviewer information (`reviewed_by_user_id`), and review timestamp (`reviewed_at`).

responseBody.description: The approved timesheet with updated status set to approved, the reviewer's identity, and the review timestamp. All timelogs contained within this timesheet are now permanently locked.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the timesheet to approve. Must reference a timesheet in submitted status that belongs to the currently selected organization.
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: The timesheet must exist before it can be approved. This operation creates the draft timesheet that will later be submitted and approved.
The timesheet must be in submitted status before approval. The approve operation validates status and rejects draft or rejected timesheets with 422 Unprocessable Entity.

operations.description:
Rejects a submitted timesheet and returns it to draft status for revision.

This endpoint is used by managers and organization owners who hold the time:approve permission to review timesheets submitted by employees. When a timesheet is rejected, it transitions from submitted back to draft status, allowing the employee to make corrections and resubmit.

A rejection reason is mandatory and is stored with the timesheet to provide the employee with clear context for the rejection. The reviewing user's identity and the review timestamp are also recorded for audit purposes.

Only timesheets in submitted status can be rejected. After rejection, all timelogs within the timesheet remain editable since the timesheet returns to draft status. The employee may modify the timesheet by adding or removing timelogs and then resubmit it following the standard submission rules.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Reject a submitted timesheet, returning it to draft status for the employee to revise.

Implementation steps:
1. Authenticate the requesting user and verify they hold the time:approve permission within the current organization context. If not, return 403 Forbidden.
2. Look up the timesheet by timesheetId. If not found, return 404 Not Found.
3. Verify the timesheet belongs to the same organization as the requesting user's current context. If not, return 404 Not Found.
4. Verify the timesheet's status is submitted. If not, return 409 Conflict with a message indicating only submitted timesheets can be rejected.
5. Validate that rejection_reason is provided and non-empty in the request body. If missing or blank, return 422 Unprocessable Entity with a validation error.
6. Update the timesheet record:
   - Set status to draft
   - Set reviewed_by_user_id to the requesting user's member ID
   - Set reviewed_at to the current timestamp
   - Set rejection_reason to the provided value
   - Update updated_at to the current timestamp
7. Return the updated timesheet with all fields.

Edge cases:
- The employee who owns the timesheet cannot reject their own timesheet; only a user with time:approve permission can perform this action.
- Timelogs within the timesheet remain unchanged; only the timesheet status and review metadata are modified.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet with its status changed to draft, including the rejection reason, reviewer identity, and review timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the timesheet to reject. Must be an existing timesheet in submitted status within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: The rejection payload containing the mandatory reason for rejecting the timesheet.

prerequisites.description: A timesheet must be created (in draft status) before it can be rejected. The timesheetId path parameter must reference an existing timesheet record.
The timesheet must be in 'submitted' status before rejection can proceed. The reject operation validates this state and returns 409 Conflict if the timesheet is not submitted.

operations.description:
Add a new timelog entry to a draft timesheet.

This operation creates a time entry and immediately associates it with the specified timesheet. Only draft timesheets accept new timelogs — once a timesheet has been submitted, its timelog set is frozen. The timelog must fall within the timesheet's calendar week (Monday through Sunday) and belong to the same employee who owns the timesheet.

Employees without the time:manage permission can only log time for themselves — the timelog's employee is automatically set to their own employee record. Managers and owners with the time:manage permission may create timelogs for any employee, but the timelog's employee must still match the timesheet's owning employee.

Deactivated employees are prevented from logging time entirely. The project must be active and the employee must be a project member. When the timelog is successfully created, the timesheet's total hours are recalculated to reflect the new entry.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new timelog and associate it with the timesheet specified by {timesheetId}.

Validate the timesheet exists within the current organization context and is in "draft" status. Reject if the timesheet is in submitted, approved, or rejected status — timelogs can only be added to draft timesheets.

Resolve the employee for whom the timelog is created:
- If the authenticated user lacks the time:manage permission, automatically set the timelog's employee_id to the authenticated user's own employee record. Reject any attempt to specify a different employee.
- If the authenticated user has the time:manage permission, set the timelog's employee_id to the timesheet's employee_id. The timelog's employee must match the timesheet's employee.

Validate the employee is active (not deactivated). A deactivated employee cannot create timelogs.

Validate the project exists, belongs to the same organization, and has an active status (not archived or completed). The employee must be a member of the project (has an erp_hrm_project_members record).

If task_id is provided, validate the task exists, belongs to the same project as specified by project_id, and has not been deleted.

Validate the timelog's date falls within the timesheet's week range: week_start_date <= date <= week_end_date.

Validate duration_minutes is a positive integer.

Set timesheet_id to the {timesheetId} from the path. Set created_at and updated_at to the current timestamp. Set billable to the provided value or default to true if not specified.

After successful insertion, recalculate the timesheet's total hours by summing duration_minutes of all timelogs associated with the timesheet.

Return the created timelog with all fields populated.

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog record with all fields populated, including the assigned timesheet association, computed timestamps, and the generated UUID.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the draft timesheet to add the timelog to. The timesheet must be in draft status and owned by the same employee who will own the new timelog.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Timelog creation data including project, optional task, date, duration in minutes, optional description, and billable flag. The employee and timesheet are derived from authentication context and the path parameter respectively.

prerequisites.description: Project must exist and be in active status before timelogs can be logged against it. The project_id is a required field in the timelog creation request body, and the employee must be a member of the project.
Timesheet must exist and be in draft status before timelogs can be added to it. The timesheetId is a path parameter that must reference an existing draft timesheet owned by the same employee.

operations.description:
Erase a timelog entry within a timesheet.

Permanently soft-deletes a timelog that belongs to a specific timesheet. The timelog record is preserved in the database for audit integrity but excluded from all normal queries, reports, and timesheet calculations.

**Access Control**: Employees may delete only their own timelogs. Users holding the time:manage permission may delete any employee's timelogs within the organization, subject to the timesheet status restrictions described below.

**Timesheet Status Restrictions**:
- **Approved timesheet**: Deletion is unconditionally blocked for all users, including those with time:manage permission. The approved-timesheet lock is absolute — no timelog in an approved timesheet can ever be removed.
- **Submitted timesheet**: Only users with time:manage permission may delete timelogs. The owning employee is blocked once the timesheet has been submitted for review.
- **Draft timesheet**: Deletion is permitted for the owning employee and for users with time:manage permission.

**Effect**: The timelog's deleted_at timestamp is set, and its association with the timesheet is cleared (timesheet_id is set to null) so the timesheet's total hours and timelog counts remain accurate.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete a timelog entry that is scoped to a specific timesheet.

**Validation Steps**:
1. Look up the timesheet by {timesheetId}. Verify it exists and belongs to the current organization (via timesheet → employee → organization). If not found or out of scope, return 404.
2. Look up the timelog by {timelogId}. Verify it exists, belongs to the current organization scope (via timelog → employee → organization), and its timesheet_id matches {timesheetId}. If the timelog does not belong to this timesheet, return 404 with a message indicating the timelog is not associated with the specified timesheet.
3. If the timelog's deleted_at is already set, return 404 (already deleted).

**Authorization and Timesheet Status Checks**:
4. Determine the requesting user's permissions:
   - Identify the current employee record for the requesting user in the active organization.
   - Check whether the user holds the `time:manage` permission.

5. Branch on the timesheet's status:
   - **status = 'approved'**: Reject unconditionally with 409 Conflict. Message: "This timelog is locked by an approved timesheet and cannot be deleted." This lock applies to ALL users including those with time:manage permission (sections 165, 273, 279).
   - **status = 'submitted'**: If the requesting user is the timelog's owning employee AND does NOT hold time:manage, return 403 Forbidden: "You cannot delete a timelog that is part of a submitted timesheet." If the user holds time:manage, allow deletion.
   - **status = 'draft'**: If the requesting user is the timelog's owning employee OR holds time:manage, allow deletion. Otherwise, return 403 Forbidden.
   - **status = 'rejected'**: Treat the same as 'draft' (rejected timesheets return to draft status).
   - **Any other status**: Return 400 Bad Request indicating an unrecognized timesheet status.

**Deletion Execution**:
6. Perform the soft delete in a transaction:
   - Set timelog.deleted_at to the current timestamp.
   - Set timelog.timesheet_id to null (removing the timelog from the timesheet so the timesheet's computed totals remain accurate).
   - Set timelog.updated_at to the current timestamp.

7. Record the deletion in the activity log (action type: timelog.deleted) with the actor's user ID, affected timelog ID, and organization context.

**Edge Cases**:
- If the timelog's employee has been deactivated, deletion still proceeds based on the same permission and status rules — historical data ownership is preserved.
- Concurrent deletion attempts: the transaction isolation level should handle the race; the second request will find deleted_at already set and return 404.

parameters.description: UUID of the timesheet containing the timelog to be deleted (global scope).
parameters.name: timesheetId

parameters.description: UUID of the timelog entry to be deleted (global scope). Must belong to the timesheet identified by timesheetId.
parameters.name: timelogId

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must exist before a timelog scoped to it can be deleted. The target operation validates the timesheet identified by {timesheetId} exists and belongs to the current organization (returns 404 if not found).

Timelog must exist and be associated with the timesheet before it can be soft-deleted. The target operation validates the timelog exists, belongs to the current organization, and its timesheet_id matches {timesheetId} (returns 404 if not associated).

authorizations.name: guest
authorizations.description: Unauthenticated visitors who can sign up, log in, and accept organization invitations after creating an account.

authorizations.name: member
authorizations.description: Authenticated users who belong to one or more organizations. Within each organization, they hold a role (Owner, Manager, Employee, or custom) that determines their permissions. All authenticated actions are scoped to the currently selected organization context.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the permission.

A UUID v4 string that serves as the primary key. This identifier is stable across all organizations — the same nine permissions have the same IDs regardless of organization context, since permissions are global system constants.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_permissions.id. UUID primary key assigned by the system when the permission is seeded.

key.description:
Unique dot-notation identifier for this permission.

The key follows a `{domain}:{action}` convention and serves as the canonical reference used in authorization checks throughout the system. Examples include "org:manage" for organization management, "employee:view" for viewing employee records, and "time:approve" for approving timesheets.

This key is the primary way permissions are referenced in code and configuration. It is unique across the entire permission catalog.
key.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_permissions.key. Unique dot-notation identifier with a unique constraint enforced at the database level.

description.description:
Human-readable explanation of what operations this permission grants.

Describes the scope of access in plain language so administrators can understand what each permission enables when building or assigning roles. This description appears in the role management interface to help organization owners make informed decisions about permission assignments.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_permissions.description. Plain text with no maximum length enforced at the application layer.

IErpHrmPermission.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a system permission available for role assignment.

Each permission is identified by a unique dot-notation key following the `{domain}:{action}` convention (e.g., "org:manage", "employee:view", "time:approve") and carries a human-readable description of the access it grants. Permissions are immutable system constants — the fixed catalog of nine built-in permissions is seeded into the system and shared across all organizations within the HRM platform.

Permissions define granular access rights that are grouped into roles. When a role is assigned to an employee, the employee inherits all permissions granted to that role, determining what operations they can perform within their organization context.
IErpHrmPermission.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping of id, key, and description columns from erp_hrm_permissions. Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) excluded as they are not essential for list and summary display. The HAS-MANY relation permissionRoles excluded per ISummary convention — role-permission assignments are viewed through the Role entity, not the Permission side. No organization scoping required: permissions form a fixed system catalog shared across all organizations and are never created, updated, or deleted at runtime.

search.description:
Text search on role names using trigram similarity matching.

Performs fuzzy matching against role names to support partial and approximate searches. Matches role names that are similar to the provided text, enabling users to find roles even with incomplete or slightly misspelled names. Leave empty or omit to return all roles without name filtering.
search.x-autobe-specification: Trigram similarity search against erp_hrm_roles.name using the GIN index (gin_trgm_ops). Applied as a WHERE clause with the similarity operator when the search string is provided. Matches partial role names for flexible browsing. Empty or whitespace-only values should be treated as no search filter.

is_builtin.description:
Filter by role classification.

When `true`, returns only the three built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) that are provisioned automatically at organization creation and cannot be deleted. When `false`, returns only custom roles created by organization owners. Omit this parameter to include both built-in and custom roles in the results.
is_builtin.x-autobe-specification: Direct WHERE filter on erp_hrm_roles.is_builtin. When true, returns only built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee). When false, returns only custom roles. Omitted returns both classifications.

cursor.description:
Cursor for pagination, representing the `created_at` timestamp of the last role in the previous page.

Enables stable cursor-based pagination where each page boundary is anchored to a specific role's creation timestamp. Returns roles created before this timestamp for consistent forward traversal, preventing duplicate or missed entries when roles are added during browsing. Omit on the first request to begin from the most recent roles.
cursor.x-autobe-specification: Cursor-based pagination keyed on erp_hrm_roles.created_at. Represents the created_at timestamp of the last role in the previous page. Returns roles where created_at < cursor value, ordered by the current sort direction. Ensures consistent forward traversal — newly created roles do not shift existing pages. When omitted, starts from the most recent roles.

limit.description:
Maximum number of roles to return per page.

Controls how many role records appear in each page of results. Must be between 1 and 100. The server applies a sensible default when this parameter is omitted. The actual number of returned roles may be less than this value on the final page.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of roles to return per page. Applied as a LIMIT clause. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. When omitted, the server applies a reasonable default (e.g., 20).

sort.description:
Sort order for results.

Controls how roles are ordered in the response. `name_asc` sorts alphabetically from A to Z (the default ordering). `name_desc` sorts in reverse alphabetical order. `created_at_asc` returns the oldest roles first. `created_at_desc` returns the newest roles first, useful for seeing recently created custom roles.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Sort order for the result set. Applied as an ORDER BY clause. 'name_asc' sorts by erp_hrm_roles.name ascending (default). 'name_desc' sorts by name descending. 'created_at_asc' sorts by erp_hrm_roles.created_at ascending (oldest first). 'created_at_desc' sorts by created_at descending (newest first). Defaults to 'name_asc' when omitted.

page.description:
Target page number to retrieve (1-indexed).

Specifies which page of results to return for direct page navigation. Page numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1. When omitted or set to null, the first page is returned. Requesting a page number beyond the available range returns an empty result set with accurate pagination metadata indicating the actual number of total records and pages.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed target page number for direct page navigation. Converted internally to a cursor offset based on (page - 1) * limit. Defaults to page 1 when null or omitted. Requesting a page beyond the available range returns an empty data array with valid pagination metadata reflecting the actual totals.

IErpHrmRole.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for browsing roles within the current organization.

Supports filtering by built-in classification, text search on role names, cursor-based pagination for consistent forward traversal, configurable sort order, and direct page navigation. All parameters are optional — when omitted, the endpoint returns all active roles ordered by name ascending.
IErpHrmRole.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query filter, search, and pagination parameters for the PATCH /erpHrm/roles role listing endpoint.

search: trigram similarity search against erp_hrm_roles.name using the GIN index (gin_trgm_ops). Applied as a WHERE clause condition when provided.

is_builtin: boolean WHERE filter on erp_hrm_roles.is_builtin. When true, returns only built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee). When false, returns only custom roles. Omitted to include both classifications.

cursor: created_at timestamp for cursor-based forward pagination. Returns roles where created_at < cursor value, ensuring consistent traversal even as new roles are created.

limit: maximum number of roles per page (1-100). Controls page size via LIMIT clause.

sort: controls result ordering via ORDER BY clause. 'name_asc' (default) and 'name_desc' sort by the name column. 'created_at_asc' and 'created_at_desc' sort by the created_at column.

page: 1-indexed target page number. Converted to cursor offset internally. Defaults to page 1 when null or omitted.

deleted_at IS NOT NULL rows are ALWAYS excluded server-side regardless of filter values. Organization context (erp_hrm_organization_id) is ALWAYS applied from the authenticated session.

search.description:
Case-insensitive text search applied to the permission key and description fields.

Filters the permission catalog by matching the provided text against both the dot-notation key (e.g., "org:manage") and the human-readable description. Matching is case-insensitive and uses prefix-based trigram matching for efficient lookup.

When omitted or left empty, all nine permissions are returned without text filtering.
search.x-autobe-specification: Case-insensitive text search applied to both the key and description columns of erp_hrm_permissions using the gin_trgm index on description for efficient prefix matching. When omitted or empty, no text filter is applied and all nine permissions are returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of permission records to return per page.

Controls the page size for the paginated response. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Since the permission catalog contains only nine entries, any value of 9 or above returns all permissions in a single page.

The actual number of records in the response may be less than this value when fewer results remain.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of permission records to return per page. Clamped between 1 and 100. Applied as a LIMIT clause on the erp_hrm_permissions query. Since total results are always exactly nine, values above 9 are effectively unbounded.

cursor.description:
Cursor token for pagination, obtained from a previous response to fetch the next page of results.

Enables cursor-based pagination by providing an opaque token that marks the position after which to continue fetching. When omitted, the query starts from the first record.

This property is mutually exclusive with the page parameter — use one pagination strategy at a time.
cursor.x-autobe-specification: Opaque cursor token for cursor-based pagination. Obtained from a previous response to fetch the next page of results. When provided, the query returns records after the cursor position. When omitted, the query starts from the beginning.

page.description:
Target page number to retrieve (1-indexed).

Specifies which page of results to return. Page numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1. When omitted or null, defaults to page 1.

Requesting a page beyond the available range returns an empty data array with valid pagination metadata reflecting the actual totals. This property is mutually exclusive with the cursor parameter — use one pagination strategy at a time.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed target page number for page-based pagination. Defaults to 1 if omitted or null. When provided, the query skips (page - 1) * limit records and returns up to limit records. Requesting a page beyond the available range returns an empty data array with valid pagination metadata.

IErpHrmPermission.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for listing system permissions.

Permissions are a fixed catalog of nine immutable access rights. This request body supports optional text search on permission keys and descriptions, along with pagination controls for navigating the result set.

When the request body is entirely omitted (all fields unspecified), the endpoint returns all nine permissions with default pagination settings.
IErpHrmPermission.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query the erp_hrm_permissions fixed catalog of nine immutable permissions.

Apply optional text search via the search parameter using case-insensitive prefix matching on both the key and description columns, leveraging the gin_trgm index on description. When the request body is empty or all fields are omitted, return all nine permissions.

Apply cursor-based pagination using limit and cursor parameters. The page parameter provides 1-indexed page navigation as an alternative to cursor-based traversal. Since the total result set is always exactly nine items, pagination is straightforward but maintained for API consistency.

No organization scoping is required — permissions are global system constants shared across all organizations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the password reset token record.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies this password reset request across all organizations. Used as the path parameter when retrieving or consuming the token.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_member_password_resets.id. Primary key, UUID v4.

token.description:
Cryptographically secure token string sent to the member's email.

This is the one-time verification token that the member presents to prove ownership of the registered email address. The token is globally unique across all active password reset records. Once the password reset is completed, this token record is deleted to prevent reuse.
token.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_member_password_resets.token. Globally unique across all active tokens per @@unique([token]) constraint.

member.description:
The member who requested this password reset.

Contains the member's summary profile — including display name, email, avatar, and organization-specific employment details such as position, employment type, status, role name, and department — for identifying who initiated the reset request.
member.x-autobe-specification: Join via erp_hrm_member_id to erp_hrm_members. Returns IErpHrmMember.ISummary — the member's global profile combined with organization-specific employment details.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this password reset token was generated.

Records the exact moment the reset token was created and sent to the member's email address. Stored in UTC with timezone information.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_member_password_resets.created_at. Timestamptz.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp after which this token becomes invalid.

Once the current time passes this timestamp, the token can no longer be used for password reset. Consumers must compare this value against the current time to determine token validity. Expired tokens are still returned by the API — the caller is responsible for enforcing expiration. This time limit prevents indefinite use of a compromised token.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this record.

Tracks when the password reset token record was last updated. Stored in UTC with timezone information.

IErpHrmMemberPasswordReset.description:
Full detail of a password reset token record.

The token is the cryptographically secure string sent to the member's email address for identity verification during the password reset flow. The expired_at timestamp marks when the token becomes invalid — consumers are responsible for checking this field to determine whether the token can still be used.

This record is associated with exactly one member who requested the password reset. Once the password is successfully changed, the token record is deleted to prevent reuse.
IErpHrmMemberPasswordReset.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_member_password_resets table by primary key (id = resetId). Scalar fields: id, token, created_at, expired_at, updated_at. Relation: erp_hrm_member_id JOIN erp_hrm_members → member as IErpHrmMember.ISummary. If no record exists, return 404 Not Found. Expired tokens are still returned — the consumer is responsible for checking expired_at against current time. All queries scoped to the current organization context through the associated member's organization membership.

display_name.description:
The member's display name shown across the platform.

This is the visible name displayed in all organization contexts — employee lists, project member views, task assignments, activity logs, and every other place where the member's identity is shown. The display name is part of the global profile shared across all organizations the member belongs to.

Must not be empty or whitespace-only when provided. Omit this field from the request body to leave the current display name unchanged.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.display_name. Validate non-empty and non-whitespace when provided. Partial update: only applied if key is present in the request body.

avatar_image.description:
URL to the member's avatar image for visual identification.

Part of the global profile shared across all organizations. When set, this image is displayed alongside the member's display name throughout the platform. When null, a default placeholder is used.

Provide a valid URI string to set or update the avatar. Send null to clear the existing avatar and revert to the default placeholder. Omit this field from the request body to leave the current avatar unchanged.
avatar_image.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.avatar_image. Validate URI format when a string is provided. Set to null in the database when null is sent. Partial update: only applied if key is present in the request body.

phone_number.description:
Contact phone number for the member.

Part of the global profile shared across all organizations. Stored as free-text to accommodate international number formats without imposing a specific structure.

Send null to clear the existing phone number. Omit this field from the request body to leave the current phone number unchanged.
phone_number.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.phone_number. Free-text — no format validation is applied to accommodate international number formats. Set to null in the database when null is sent. Partial update: only applied if key is present in the request body.

IErpHrmMember.IUpdate.description:
Profile fields to update for the authenticated member's global profile.

This DTO carries the mutable subset of the member's global profile — display name, avatar image, and phone number. These fields are shared across all organizations the member belongs to, so any change takes effect immediately in every organization context.

Only include fields that should be changed. Omitted fields retain their current values. Set avatar_image or phone_number to null to clear them.
IErpHrmMember.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification:
Partial update of erp_hrm_members record identified by the current session's member_id from JWT. Only fields present in the request body are applied — omitted fields retain existing values.

Mutable fields:
- display_name: Direct column mapping. Validate non-empty and non-whitespace when provided.
- avatar_image: Direct column mapping. Validate URI format when provided, or set to null to clear.
- phone_number: Direct column mapping. Free-text for international formats, or set to null to clear.

Immutable fields not in this DTO: id (primary key), email (immutable identity), password_hash (changed via dedicated password endpoint), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed timestamps). After update, set updated_at to now() and emit a real-time event broadcasting changed fields to all active members across every organization where this member holds an active employee record.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the permission.

A UUID v4 string that serves as the primary key. Used to retrieve individual permission records via GET /erpHrm/permissions/{permissionId}.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_permissions.id. UUID primary key. No transformation — returned as-is from the database.

key.description:
Unique dot-notation identifier for this permission.

Follows the {domain}:{action} convention and serves as the canonical reference in authorization checks. The nine built-in keys are: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, and report:view.
key.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_permissions.key. Unique dot-notation string following {domain}:{action} convention. Enforced by @@unique constraint. Returned as-is.

description.description:

Describes the scope of access in plain language so administrators can understand what each permission enables when assigning roles. For example, "org:manage" grants full administrative control over organization settings and member roles.
