Three states are possible for each verification record. A pending token has no verified_at timestamp and has not yet reached its expires_at deadline. A verified token has a populated verified_at timestamp, indicating the member successfully confirmed their email. An expired token has no verified_at timestamp and its expires_at deadline has passed, rendering it invalid.

Results are scoped to the currently selected organization context. Only verification records belonging to members who hold an employee record in the active organization are returned.
IErpHrmMemberEmailVerification.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Summary view JOINing erp_hrm_member_email_verifications with erp_hrm_members via erp_hrm_member_id → id (BELONGS-TO). Direct field mappings: id, email, expires_at, verified_at, created_at, updated_at. Relation: member resolved through the belongs-to join to erp_hrm_members, returning IErpHrmMember.ISummary. Excluded DB properties: token (cryptographically secure one-time verification string — security-sensitive, non-essential for list display where status is derived from verified_at and expires_at); erp_hrm_member_id (FK column exposed as member relation object). Results scoped to the currently selected organization context: only verification records belonging to members who hold an employee record in the active organization are returned.

name.description:
New display name for the role.

Must be unique within the organization — no two roles in the same organization can share the same name. The uniqueness check excludes the current role, so renaming a role to its existing name is permitted.

If unchanged, omit this field entirely.
name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_roles.name. Optional — omit to keep current name. When provided, uniqueness within the organization is enforced via @@unique([erp_hrm_organization_id, name]) at service layer, excluding the current role from the check. Organization scoping resolved from session context.

oneOf.description: Clear the role's description.

description.description:
Updated description explaining the role's purpose and responsibilities.

Provides context for organization owners and administrators when managing roles, clarifying what level of access each role entails.

Set to `null` to clear an existing description. Omit this field to leave the current description unchanged.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_roles.description. Optional and nullable — send null to clear an existing description. Omit entirely to leave the current description unchanged.

permission_ids.description:
Complete set of permission IDs to assign to this role.

Replaces all existing permissions atomically — the previous permission set is deleted and the new set is inserted in a single transaction. Permission changes propagate immediately; any employee assigned to this role will have their effective access rights updated instantly.

Each element is a UUID referencing a system permission from the fixed permissions catalog. Omit this field entirely to leave the current permissions unchanged.
permission_ids.x-autobe-specification: Computed from rolePermissions relation (erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table). Optional — omit to leave permissions unchanged. When provided: delete all existing erp_hrm_role_permissions records for this role, then INSERT new records for each UUID in the array. All operations within a single database transaction for atomicity. Each permission ID must reference a valid erp_hrm_permissions.id.

IErpHrmRole.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing role within the current organization context.

All fields are optional — send only the properties you wish to change. When `permission_ids` is provided, the complete permission set is replaced atomically; omitted permissions remain unchanged.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be modified — the service layer rejects updates to immutable roles regardless of the request content.
IErpHrmRole.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification:
Maps to erp_hrm_roles table for partial updates. All fields are optional — only send properties to change.

Field mappings:
- name: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_roles.name. Optional. When provided, uniqueness within the organization is enforced at service layer via @@unique([erp_hrm_organization_id, name]). Uniqueness check excludes the current role. Organization scoping via session context — erp_hrm_organization_id never appears in request body.
- description: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_roles.description. Optional and nullable — set to null to clear existing description.
- permission_ids: Computed from rolePermissions relation (erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table). When provided, delete all existing erp_hrm_role_permissions records for this role, then INSERT new records for each UUID in the array. All operations within a single database transaction for atomicity. When omitted, leave permissions unchanged.

Built-in role protection: Before any field updates, check is_builtin flag. Reject immediately for built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) — these are immutable. This check happens at service layer, not in DTO validation.

Path parameter: roleId resolved from URL path, not in request body.
Organization context: erp_hrm_organization_id filtered by session, not user-provided.
Timestamps: updated_at set to current timestamp on successful update. created_at unchanged.

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token previously issued during join or a prior refresh operation.

Identifies the member session to be extended. This token is single-use — after a successful refresh, the presented token becomes invalid and must be discarded. The server issues a new refresh token as part of the rotation strategy to prevent replay attacks.

If this token has already been consumed by a previous refresh, is expired, or belongs to a deleted member account, the request will be rejected with 401 Unauthorized.
refresh_token.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_member_sessions.refresh_token. This value is used to look up the member session record. The server reads this token to find the session, then rotates (replaces) it with a new refresh_token on successful refresh. The old token becomes invalid immediately after rotation.

IErpHrmGuest.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing an expiring or expired JWT access token.

Presents a previously issued refresh token to obtain a new access token and a rotated refresh token. Each refresh token is single-use — a successful refresh invalidates the presented token and issues a new one, preventing replay attacks.

The refresh operation extends the authenticated session without requiring the user to authenticate again. If the refresh token has already been used (rotated), is expired, or the associated member account has been deleted, the request is rejected with 401 Unauthorized.
IErpHrmGuest.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Request body DTO for the refresh token endpoint. The refresh_token value maps to erp_hrm_member_sessions.refresh_token and is used to look up the member session record. Validation: (1) find session by refresh_token column, (2) check expired_at has not passed, (3) verify member account (erp_hrm_members) is not soft-deleted. On success, generate new access_token and rotated refresh_token, update session record, return IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized. No database write occurs from the request body itself — this is a lookup-only DTO that carries the token value for server-side processing.

search.description:
Partial text search on member display name using fuzzy trigram matching.

Performs typo-tolerant search against the member's display name via PostgreSQL trigram similarity. Supports partial matches — searching for 'jon' will match both 'Jonathan' and 'Jone'. The search is case-insensitive and leverages a GIN trigram index for efficient execution against large member directories.

When combined with other filters (status, employment_type, role_id, department_id), the search is AND-combined — only members matching both the text search and the additional criteria are returned. An empty or whitespace-only search value is treated as no search filter, returning members regardless of display name.
search.x-autobe-specification: Fuzzy text search on erp_hrm_members.display_name using the GIN trigram index (gin_trgm_ops). Implement as ILIKE '%value%' with trigram similarity matching for typo-tolerant discovery. The GIN trigram index on display_name optimizes this query pattern for large member directories. When the search value is empty, null, or whitespace-only, skip the search filter entirely (no-op) rather than applying an empty match-all condition.

email.description:
Email address filter for locating a specific member by their registered email.

Supports two matching modes determined automatically by the input format. A complete email address (e.g., 'john@example.com') triggers an exact lookup, returning at most one member due to the uniqueness constraint. A partial prefix (e.g., 'john@' or 'jo') triggers prefix matching, returning all members whose email starts with that pattern.

Useful for precise member lookup by known email address or for exploratory browsing within an email domain. When combined with other filters using AND logic, an email filter with a status filter returns only members matching both criteria.
email.x-autobe-specification: Email address filter on erp_hrm_members.email. When the value contains a full email address (includes '@' and a domain part), apply exact match using the unique index on email for O(1) lookup. When the value is a partial prefix (no '@' or '@' present but incomplete domain), apply prefix match via LIKE 'value%'. Use case-insensitive comparison (ILIKE or LOWER()). The unique constraint on email guarantees at most one result for exact matches.

oneOf.description: Filter by employee status within the organization.
Filter by employee status within the organization.

status.description:
Filter members by their employee status within the current organization.

Narrows results to members whose employee record is either active (can log time, submit timesheets, and participate in projects and tasks) or deactivated (suspended from performing new actions but retaining all historical data including timelogs, timesheets, and contracts).

Useful for administrative workflows such as auditing the active workforce, reviewing deactivated employees for potential reactivation, or generating status-based headcount reports. Omitting this filter returns members regardless of their employee status.
status.x-autobe-specification: Equality filter on erp_hrm_employees.status. Valid values: 'active' (employee can log time entries, submit timesheets, and participate in projects) and 'deactivated' (employee suspended from new actions but all historical data preserved). Apply as WHERE erp_hrm_employees.status = value. The composite index on (erp_hrm_organization_id, status) optimizes this filter within the organization scope. AND-combine with other active filters.

employment_type.description:
Filter members by their employment type classification within the organization.

Narrows results to members whose employee record carries one of four employment classifications: full-time (standard full-time employees), part-time (reduced-hours employees), contractor (external contractors), or intern (temporary interns).

Used for workforce segmentation, headcount reporting by employment category, organizational planning, and compliance auditing. Omitting this filter returns members across all employment types.
employment_type.x-autobe-specification: Equality filter on erp_hrm_employees.employment_type. Valid values: 'full-time' (standard full-time employees), 'part-time' (reduced-hours employees), 'contractor' (external contractors), 'intern' (temporary interns). Apply as WHERE erp_hrm_employees.employment_type = value. The composite index on (erp_hrm_organization_id, employment_type) provides efficient filtering within the organization scope. AND-combine with other active filters.

role_id.description:
Filter members by their assigned role within the organization.

Accepts a role's unique identifier (UUID format) and returns only members whose employee record is assigned to that specific role. This includes members assigned to the three built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) and any custom roles created by organization owners.

Useful for role-based member discovery — finding all managers in the organization, auditing members with custom roles, or verifying role distribution across departments. Omitting this filter returns members regardless of their role assignment.
role_id.x-autobe-specification: UUID equality filter on erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_role_id. References the unique identifier of a role in erp_hrm_roles. Apply as WHERE erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_role_id = value. The index on erp_hrm_role_id optimizes this query. Validate the value as a well-formed UUID before querying to prevent database errors. AND-combine with other active filters.

department_id.description:
Filter members by their assigned department within the organization.

Accepts a department's unique identifier (UUID format) and returns only members whose employee record belongs to that specific department. Members not assigned to any department are automatically excluded from results when this filter is active, as department-less employees cannot satisfy an equality match.

Useful for department-level member browsing — viewing all members in the Engineering department, generating department rosters, or cross-referencing department membership with other filter criteria. Omitting this filter returns members across all departments including those without a department assignment.
department_id.x-autobe-specification: UUID equality filter on erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_department_id. References the unique identifier of a department in erp_hrm_departments. Apply as WHERE erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_department_id = value. The composite index on (erp_hrm_organization_id, erp_hrm_department_id) optimizes this filter. When active, members without a department assignment (NULL erp_hrm_department_id) are automatically excluded since the equality comparison filters out NULLs. Validate the value as a well-formed UUID before querying.

sort.description:
Sort specification controlling the order of returned member results.

Specifies which field to sort by and whether the sort direction is ascending or descending. Valid sort fields span both member and employee dimensions: display_name (member's visible name), email (member's email address), created_at (when the employee record was created), and status (employee activity status).

Format uses a colon separator between the field name and direction — for example, 'display_name:asc' sorts alphabetically A to Z, while 'created_at:desc' shows the newest employees first. If the direction suffix is omitted, ascending order is used by default. When no sort value is provided or an unrecognized field is specified, results default to ascending alphabetical order by display name.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Sort specification for constructing the SQL ORDER BY clause. Parse the value by splitting on the last colon (':') to extract the column name and optional direction suffix. Valid column values and their mappings: 'display_name' → erp_hrm_members.display_name, 'email' → erp_hrm_members.email, 'created_at' → erp_hrm_employees.created_at, 'status' → erp_hrm_employees.status. Valid direction suffixes: ':asc' for ascending (default when no suffix present), ':desc' for descending. When the value is omitted, null, empty, or specifies an unrecognized column, default to 'display_name:asc'. Multiple sort columns are not supported — only a single sort field is applied. Construct the final clause as: ORDER BY <column> <direction>. For safe SQL construction, validate the column name against a whitelist before interpolation.

cursor.description:
Opaque cursor token for keyset-based pagination through member results.

Enables stable, sequential traversal through paginated results without the consistency issues of offset-based pagination — newly inserted or deleted records between page requests do not cause duplicates or gaps. On the first request, omit the cursor to receive the initial page of results. Each response includes a cursor pointing to the next page; include that cursor value verbatim in the subsequent request to fetch the next page.

The cursor is an implementation-internal token whose structure should not be parsed, constructed, or modified by API consumers. Treat it as an opaque string to pass back unchanged between paginated requests.
cursor.x-autobe-specification: Opaque cursor token for keyset-based (cursor) pagination. When provided, decode the base64-encoded token to extract the last-seen value of the active sort column and the last-seen primary key (erp_hrm_members.id). Construct a WHERE clause to fetch records positioned after the cursor: for ascending sort, WHERE (sort_column > cursor_sort_value) OR (sort_column = cursor_sort_value AND erp_hrm_members.id > cursor_id); for descending sort, reverse the comparison operators (< instead of >). Omit the cursor condition entirely when no cursor is provided (first page request). The cursor's internal structure (base64-encoded JSON with sortValue and id fields) is an implementation detail — API consumers treat it as an opaque string. Each response must include the next cursor value for sequential page traversal.

limit.description:
Maximum number of member records to return per page.

Controls the page size for paginated member listing responses. Lower values produce smaller, faster-loading pages; higher values reduce the total number of requests needed to browse through all matching results.

The enforced maximum of 100 prevents excessive data transfer and query load in a single request. When the total number of matching members is less than the requested limit, fewer records are returned — this is expected behavior indicating the final (or only) page of results.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of results per page. Applied as the SQL LIMIT clause value. Default to 20 when the value is omitted, null, or undefined. Enforce the configured maximum of 100 — clamp any value greater than 100 down to 100. If the value is less than 1, fall back to the default of 20. The actual number of returned records may be less than the limit on the final page or when the total number of matching records is smaller than the limit. Always return exactly the number of matching records up to the limit — never pad with empty entries.

page.description:
Target page number for direct page-based navigation through member results.

Specifies which page of results to return using 1-indexed numbering — the first page is page 1 (not 0). Defaults to the first page when omitted or set to null.

Useful for direct page access in UI pagination controls, such as jumping to page 5 of 12. When the requested page number exceeds the total available pages, an empty result set is returned with accurate pagination metadata showing the actual total records and pages, allowing the client to adjust its navigation accordingly.

For sequential traversal through all results, cursor-based pagination using the cursor parameter is recommended as it avoids consistency issues with record insertions or deletions between page requests.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for page-based navigation. Default to page 1 when the value is omitted, null, or undefined. Calculate the SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit. Validate that the page number is a positive integer — a value of 0 or negative defaults to page 1. When the requested page number exceeds the available range (beyond the last page), return an empty data array with accurate pagination metadata reflecting the actual total records and pages rather than an error. For requests specifying both cursor and page, cursor-based positioning takes precedence for the starting point while page determines the offset within the remaining result set.

IErpHrmMember.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing members within the current organization.

Combines filter parameters from both the member's global profile (erp_hrm_members) and their organization-specific employee record (erp_hrm_employees), enabling precise member discovery through the organization directory. Each matching result returns the member's identity fields alongside their employment details — role, department, position, employment type, and status.

Supports partial text search on display name using fuzzy trigram matching for typo-tolerant discovery, exact or prefix matching on email address, and filtering by employee status (active or deactivated), employment type classification (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern), assigned role UUID, and department UUID.

Includes both cursor-based pagination for sequential traversal and page-based navigation for direct page access. Sorting is configurable across display_name, email, created_at, and status dimensions with ascending or descending direction. All results are strictly scoped to the currently selected organization; members who are employees in other organizations but not the current one are never exposed.
IErpHrmMember.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameter DTO for cross-table member listing. Builds dynamic SQL WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and OFFSET clauses from user-provided filter criteria. The core query joins erp_hrm_members INNER JOIN erp_hrm_employees ON erp_hrm_member_id, scoped to the session's current organization (erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_organization_id) with soft-delete exclusions on both tables (deleted_at IS NULL).

Property-to-column mappings:
- search → erp_hrm_members.display_name via ILIKE with GIN trigram index for fuzzy, typo-tolerant matching
- email → erp_hrm_members.email via exact match (full address) or LIKE prefix match (partial)
- status → erp_hrm_employees.status equality filter (enum: active, deactivated)
- employment_type → erp_hrm_employees.employment_type equality filter (enum: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern)
- role_id → erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_role_id UUID equality filter
- department_id → erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_department_id UUID equality filter
- sort → ORDER BY clause construction; parse colon-delimited format (column:direction); valid columns: display_name, email, created_at, status; default: display_name ASC
- cursor → opaque base64-encoded keyset pagination token; decode to extract last-seen sort value and id; construct WHERE clause for forward traversal
- limit → SQL LIMIT; default 20, max 100; clamp out-of-range values
- page → 1-indexed page number; compute OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit; default 1

All filters are AND-combined when multiple are present. Organization scoping is implicit via session context. password_hash must never appear in any query result or filter parameter.

Unique identifier for the member account.

This UUID is the member's primary key in the erp_hrm_members table and is globally unique across all organizations. It remains stable for the lifetime of the account and serves as the canonical reference for the member in all cross-organization contexts.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.id. UUID primary key.

email.description:
The member's email address used for authentication and primary contact.

This email is unique across all member accounts in the system. It serves as the login credential and the target for organization invitations. When an invitation is sent to an email address matching an existing member, the member is automatically added to the inviting organization.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.email. Unique constraint enforced at database level.

display_name.description:
The member's visible name displayed across the platform.

Part of the global profile shared across all organizations the member belongs to. This name appears in employee directories, project member lists, task assignments, activity logs, and all other contexts where the member's identity is shown.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.display_name. Indexed with GIN trigram for fuzzy search.

URI pointing to the member's avatar image for visual identification.

position.x-autobe-specification: Resolved from erp_hrm_employees.position via INNER JOIN on erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_member_id = erp_hrm_members.id.

Classification of the member's employment relationship with the current organization.

Indicates the nature of the employment arrangement, such as full-time, part-time, contract, or internship. This classification affects how the member appears in reports and may influence access to certain features.
employment_type.x-autobe-specification: Resolved from erp_hrm_employees.employment_type via INNER JOIN on erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_member_id = erp_hrm_members.id.

The member's current employment status within the organization.

Indicates whether the employee is active and able to log time entries, submit timesheets, and participate in projects and tasks, or deactivated with suspended access. Deactivated employees retain their historical data but cannot perform new actions.

Summary view of a member within the current organization, combining the member's global profile with their organization-specific employment details.

Used in paginated member listing responses where each entry represents one employee-member pairing scoped to the active organization.

Direct fields from erp_hrm_members: id, email, display_name, avatar_image, phone_number. From erp_hrm_employees: id (aliased as employee_id), position, employment_type, status. Resolved via relation traversals: role name from erp_hrm_roles JOINed through erp_hrm_employees.role_id, department name from erp_hrm_departments JOINed through erp_hrm_employees.department_id. id.description:
Unique identifier for the employee record.

A UUID v4 value assigned at creation when the employee joins the organization through invitation acceptance or direct assignment. Immutable throughout the employee's lifecycle — remains the same across role changes, department reassignments, and status transitions.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.id. UUID primary key, unique across all employee records.

member.description:
The member's global profile and organization-specific employment details.

Combines the member's identity — display name, email address, avatar image, and phone number — with their employment record in the current organization: position title, employment type classification, active/deactivated status, assigned role name, and department name. This consolidated view provides everything needed to identify and categorize the person behind the employee record.
member.x-autobe-specification: INNER JOIN via erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_member_id → erp_hrm_members.id, resolved to IErpHrmMember.ISummary. Guaranteed non-null — every employee must reference a valid member account. The member's global profile (display_name, email, avatar_image, phone_number) is shared across all organizations the member belongs to.

role.description:
The role assigned to this employee within the organization.

Every employee holds exactly one role that defines their permissions. The role can be one of the three built-in types — Owner, Manager, or Employee — or a custom role created by the organization owner. Role changes take effect immediately and are reflected in the employee's access rights without requiring re-authentication.

The summary includes the role's name, built-in status, description, and total count of granted permissions, enabling quick identification of the employee's access level without loading the full permission set.
role.x-autobe-specification: INNER JOIN via erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_role_id → erp_hrm_roles.id, resolved to IErpHrmRole.ISummary. Guaranteed non-null — every employee must have exactly one role at all times. The role determines the employee's permission set within the organization.

department.description:
The optional department this employee belongs to.

When null, the employee is not assigned to any department. When a department is deleted, affected employees have their department reference cleared to null without removing the employee record itself.
department.x-autobe-specification: LEFT JOIN via erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_department_id → erp_hrm_departments.id, resolved to IErpHrmDepartment.ISummary | null. Nullable — employees can exist without a department assignment. Department membership is purely organizational and carries no inherent permissions.

position.description:
The employee's job title or position name within the organization.

A free-text description such as "Software Engineer", "Marketing Lead", or "Finance Manager" that provides organizational clarity. This field is purely descriptive and does not affect permissions, access rights, or system behavior.

When null, no position has been specified for this employee. May be updated independently of role changes and department reassignments.
position.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.position. Nullable free-text field describing the employee's job title or function. Purely descriptive — carries no inherent permissions or system behavior.

employment_type.description:
Classification of the employment relationship.

Indicates the nature of the employee's engagement with the organization. Supported values are:
- **full-time**: A regular full-time employee with standard working hours commitment
- **part-time**: A regular part-time employee with reduced working hours commitment
- **contractor**: An external contractor engaged on a contractual basis

Used for filtering employee lists and generating workforce composition reports. The employment type influences how the employee appears in organizational charts and workforce summaries.

status.description:
Current activity status of the employee within the organization.

Determines whether the employee can perform work-related actions:
- **active**: The employee can log time entries, submit timesheets, participate in projects, and be assigned to tasks. All platform features are available.
- **deactivated**: The employee cannot create new time entries, submit timesheets, or participate in new project assignments. All historical data — timelogs, timesheets, contracts, and past project contributions — is preserved and remains accessible. Deactivation is reversible via reactivation.

Status does not affect the employee's role assignment or department membership. A deactivated employee retains their role but cannot exercise its permissions.

Formatted as an ISO 8601 date-time string with timezone offset. Compare with created_at to determine how recently the employee's organizational profile has been modified.

Identity fields include the member's display name, email, avatar, and phone number, alongside organization-specific employment details: position title, employment type classification (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern), and active/deactivated status. IErpHrmMemberPasswordReset.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing password reset tokens within the currently selected organization.

Password reset tokens are generated when a member requests a password reset and are sent to their registered email address. This request schema provides the filter parameters for browsing token records — by associated member, by token validity status (active or expired), by creation date range, and by free-text search against member identity fields.

Results are paginated using cursor-based navigation on the creation timestamp. Sorting is supported by creation time and expiration time in either ascending or descending order. The default sort is newest first by creation time. All filter parameters are optional and combined with AND logic when multiple are provided.

For security, the raw cryptographic token values are never exposed through any API response, and this request schema does not include any mechanisms to retrieve them.

All filters are optional and AND-combined when multiple are provided. Filters: memberId (UUID exact match on erp_hrm_member_id), status (computed: 'active' = expired_at > NOW(), 'expired' = expired_at <= NOW()), createdFrom/createdTo (date-time range on created_at), search (LIKE on member display_name OR email via JOIN). IErpHrmEmployee.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, pagination, and sort criteria for browsing the employee directory within the current organization.

All properties are optional — when none are specified, the endpoint returns all active employees in the organization with default pagination. Filters are combined with AND logic when multiple are provided, and soft-deleted employees are always excluded regardless of filter settings.

The search field performs a free-text match against employee display names using partial matching. The department_id filter restricts results to employees in a specific department. The employment_type and status filters use exact matching against the employee's current classification and activity state.

Filters (AND-combined when multiple provided):
- search: ILIKE or trigram similarity match on erp_hrm_members.display_name (%search%)
- department_id: exact match on erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_department_id
- employment_type: exact match on erp_hrm_employees.employment_type (values: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern)
- status: exact match on erp_hrm_employees.status (values: active, deactivated)

Pagination: page-based offset — (page - 1) * limit. page defaults to 1, limit capped at 100.

Sort: order by the specified column. Supported columns: name (maps to erp_hrm_members.display_name), employment_type, status, created_at. Prefix with '-' for descending order. Default: name ascending (display_name ASC).

name.description:
The department's display name.

When provided, this becomes the department's new name. The name must be unique within the organization among active (non-deleted) departments. This name appears in department listings, employee records, and organizational hierarchy views throughout the platform.

Return 409 Conflict on name collision.

An optional free-text description of the department's purpose or scope.

Provides additional context for employees browsing the organizational structure. Set to null to clear any existing description, leaving the department without descriptive text. Omitting this field from the request entirely preserves the current description unchanged.

parent_id.description:
The UUID of the parent department for hierarchical nesting.

Setting this to null makes the department a top-level department with no parent in the organizational hierarchy. When set to a UUID value, the referenced parent must be an existing top-level department within the same organization that is not the department itself or any of its descendants, preventing circular relationships. The one-level nesting constraint ensures that only top-level departments can serve as parents.

UUID validation (all must pass, return 400 Bad Request with descriptive message on failure): (a) Target parent must exist in the same organization with deleted_at null, (b) Target parent must have null parent_id itself — enforcing one-level nesting constraint, (c) Target must not be the department being updated — no self-referencing, (d) Target must not be a descendant — traverse hierarchy upward from target parent to verify it does not reach this department.

The parent_id manages the department's position in the organizational hierarchy — setting it to null makes the department a top-level department with no parent, while setting it to a UUID assigns the department as a child of the specified parent, which must itself be a top-level department under the one-level nesting constraint.

Search, filter, sorting, and pagination parameters for browsing the organization's department hierarchy.

Query parameter DTO for the PATCH /erpHrm/member/departments index endpoint. Does not map to a single database table; instead, composes filtering, text search, sorting, and pagination controls that are applied to the erp_hrm_departments query scoped to the current organization context (erp_hrm_organization_id from session).

- search: fuzzy text search on the name column using the GIN trigram index (gin_trgm_ops)
- parent_id: hierarchy filter — null returns only top-level departments (parent_id IS NULL), a UUID returns children of that parent, omit the field entirely to return all departments regardless of hierarchy

refresh_token.description:
The current refresh token held by the client, exchanged for a new JWT access and refresh token pair.

The refresh token must correspond to an active, non-expired session in erp_hrm_member_sessions whose associated member account has not been soft-deleted. After successful rotation, this token is immediately invalidated — each refresh token can only be used once.
refresh_token.x-autobe-specification:
Direct mapping from erp_hrm_member_sessions.refresh_token. The server looks up the session by matching the provided token value against the refresh_token column. Unlike access_token (which has an @@unique constraint), refresh_token lookup relies on the token value itself — the rotation mechanism ensures at most one active session holds a given refresh token at any time.

Validation chain: (1) find session WHERE refresh_token = input, (2) verify expired_at > now(), (3) JOIN erp_hrm_members and verify deleted_at IS NULL. On validation success, generate new token pair and update the session record.

IErpHrmMember.IRefresh.description:
Token refresh payload containing the current refresh token to exchange for a new JWT access and refresh token pair.

The provided refresh token is looked up in erp_hrm_member_sessions. If the token is valid, the session has not expired, and the associated member account has not been soft-deleted, the server performs token rotation — issuing new access and refresh tokens and invalidating the old refresh token.

Each refresh token can only be used once. After a successful rotation, the previous refresh token is immediately invalidated, preventing token replay attacks. The new tokens carry the same organization context as the original session.

If the refresh token is expired, invalid, or the member account has been deleted, the request is rejected with 401 Unauthorized, requiring the client to redirect the user to the login flow.
IErpHrmMember.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification:
Maps refresh_token to erp_hrm_member_sessions.refresh_token. The server receives the client's current refresh token and looks up the corresponding session record by matching against the refresh_token column. The @@unique constraint on access_token is not used here — the lookup is by refresh_token value directly.

Once the session is found, the server validates: (1) the session has not expired (expired_at > now), and (2) the associated member account is not soft-deleted (JOIN to erp_hrm_members, deleted_at IS NULL). If either check fails, return 401 Unauthorized.

On success, the server performs token rotation: generating a new JWT access_token and refresh_token, updating the session record with both values, resetting expired_at to a new future timestamp, and updating ip to the current request's IP. The old refresh_token is invalidated by replacement. The @@unique([access_token]) index on the new access_token prevents collisions.

If the session's erp_hrm_organization_id is set, carry that organization context forward in the new tokens. If null, the member must select an organization after refresh.

This is a refresh authorization endpoint — no JWT Bearer token is required because the refresh token itself serves as the authentication credential. The member identity is derived from erp_hrm_member_id in the matched session record.

Optional fields:

- `parent_id`: UUID of a parent department to nest this department under the two-level hierarchy. The parent must exist in the same organization and must not already have a parent of its own.

IErpHrmEmployee.IUpdate.description:
Fields to update on an existing employee record within the currently selected organization.

All fields are optional — only provided fields are modified while omitted fields retain their current values. This follows partial update semantics, allowing callers to update only the specific attributes that need to change.

**Mutable Fields**

- role_id: Reassigns the employee's role within the organization. The new role's permissions take effect immediately upon save. Must reference an existing role in the same organization.
- department_id: Places the employee in a department for organizational grouping. Set to null to remove the employee from any department. Department assignment carries no permission implications.
- position: Free-text job title or position name (e.g., "Software Engineer", "Marketing Lead"). Purely descriptive — carries no inherent permissions.
- employment_type: Classification of the employment relationship. Must be one of: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern. Used for filtering and reporting.
- status: Controls the employee's ability to perform actions. active allows time tracking, timesheet submission, and project participation. deactivated preserves all historical data but prevents new entries. Deactivated employees can be reactivated.
IErpHrmEmployee.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification:
Partial update for erp_hrm_employees within the current organization session scope.

**Authorization & Scoping**:
- Require employee:manage permission on the current organization.
- The target employee's erp_hrm_organization_id must match the current session's selected organization. Reject with 404 if the employee does not exist or belongs to a different organization.
- Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from lookup.

**Mutable Fields** (all optional — only provided fields are included in the UPDATE SET):
- erp_hrm_role_id: Must reference an existing erp_hrm_roles record in the same organization (erp_hrm_organization_id match). Reject with 422 if not found. Role changes take effect immediately.
- erp_hrm_department_id: Must reference an existing erp_hrm_departments record in the same organization. Null clears the department assignment. Reject with 422 if a non-null value does not reference a valid department.
- position: Free-text job title. Nullable — accept null to clear. No format constraints beyond application-level max length.
- employment_type: Must be one of: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern. Reject with 422 for invalid values.
- status: Must be one of: active, deactivated. Reject with 422 for invalid values.

**Immutable** (never included in UPDATE SET):
- erp_hrm_member_id: Ownership — the employee's associated user account cannot be reassigned.
- erp_hrm_organization_id: Scoping — resolved from the authenticated session, not changeable.

**Auto-managed**:
- updated_at is touched to current timestamp on every update.
- id and created_at are never modified.

**Edge Cases**:
- Updating an already-deactivated employee's status to deactivated is idempotent — succeed without error.
- Changing role on a deactivated employee is permitted — the new role takes effect upon reactivation.
- Empty request body returns the current record without modification.

start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.start_date (Timestamptz). Nullable — setting to null clears the start date. When both start_date and end_date are provided (neither null), end_date must not be before start_date. When only one date is updated, validate the constraint against the existing database value for the other date.

end_date.description:
The optional project end date.

Marks the expected or actual completion date of the project. Can be set to null to clear an existing end date. When both start and end dates are specified, the end date must not precede the start date — this cross-field validation is enforced during update to maintain timeline integrity.
end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.end_date (Timestamptz). Nullable — setting to null clears the end date. When both start_date and end_date are provided (neither null), end_date must not be before start_date. When only one date is updated, validate the constraint against the existing database value for the other date.

IErpHrmProject.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing project's editable fields.

All fields are optional — the client may send only the fields that need to change, and omitted fields will retain their current values. The project's lifecycle status (active, archived, or completed) is not modified through this operation; dedicated endpoints handle status transitions.

Nullable fields (description, budget_hours, start_date, end_date) can be set to null to clear their current value. When budget_hours is provided as a non-null number, it must be a positive value greater than zero. When both start_date and end_date are provided, the end date must not precede the start date.

The project to update is identified by the projectId path parameter, and the operation is scoped to the current session's organization context. Only users with the project:manage permission may perform this update.
IErpHrmProject.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification:
Maps to erp_hrm_projects updatable columns: name, description, color_code, budget_hours, start_date, end_date. All fields are optional — only provided fields are updated; omitted fields retain current values.

name: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.name. When provided, must not be empty. No uniqueness constraint at the column level, but should be distinct within the organization for practical identification.

description: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.description. Nullable — setting to null clears the description. No length constraint enforced at the schema level.

color_code: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.color_code. When provided, must not be empty. Typically a hex color value (e.g., '#FF5733') for UI display.

budget_hours: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.budget_hours (DoublePrecision). Nullable — setting to null clears the budget. When provided as a non-null value, must be a positive number greater than zero. Used in project budget reports to compare planned hours against actual logged hours.

start_date: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.start_date (Timestamptz). Nullable — setting to null clears the start date. When both start_date and end_date are provided (neither null), end_date must not be before start_date.

end_date: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.end_date (Timestamptz). Nullable — setting to null clears the end date. When both start_date and end_date are provided (neither null), end_date must not be before start_date.

Validation: When only one date is being updated, validate the cross-date constraint against the existing database value for the other date.

Excluded from this DTO: id (path parameter projectId), organization_id (resolved from session context), status (managed through dedicated status-change endpoints), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (auto-managed timestamps), projectMembers/tasks/timelogs/timers (has-many relations not modifiable through project update).

email.description:
The member's email address used for authentication and as the primary contact identifier.

Must be unique across all non-deleted member accounts. If a previously deleted account used this email, the registration creates a new account and clears the soft-delete marker. This email also serves as the target for organization invitations — when an invitation has been sent to this address, the member is automatically enrolled in the inviting organization upon email verification.

Format must be a valid email address conforming to standard email structure.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.email. Enforce uniqueness via @@unique([email]) index — check for existing non-deleted account (deleted_at IS NULL). If a soft-deleted account (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) matches this email, treat as new registration and clear deleted_at. Also serves as the matching key for pending organization invitations during email verification.

password.description:
The plain-text password for member authentication.

Received as plain text from the client and securely hashed using a strong one-way algorithm (bcrypt or argon2) with a unique salt before storage. The password is never stored or transmitted in plaintext after the initial registration request is processed.

Must meet minimum complexity requirements for account security. The hashed value stored in password_hash cannot be reversed to recover the original password.
password.x-autobe-specification: Plain-text password received from client. Hashed with bcrypt or argon2 before storage in erp_hrm_members.password_hash. Never store or transmit in plaintext after initial processing. The hash must use a cryptographically secure salt and appropriate work factor.

display_name.description:
The member's visible display name shown across the platform in all organizations they join.

Part of the global profile that is shared across all organizations. Displayed in employee lists, project member views, task assignments, activity logs, and all other contexts where the member's identity is shown. This is how other members will see and recognize this person throughout the platform.

This can be changed later through the profile update operation.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.display_name. Becomes the member's visible identity across all organizations they join. Shown in employee lists, project member views, task assignments, activity logs, and all other contexts where the member's identity is displayed.

href.description:
The full URL of the page where the member initiated registration.

Collected for session audit, security analysis, and analytics purposes. Stored in the member's session record alongside authentication tokens. In browser-based clients, this is typically the value of `window.location.href` at the time of registration.

Format must be a valid URI.
href.x-autobe-specification: Session context field stored in erp_hrm_member_sessions.href alongside generated JWT access/refresh tokens. Represents the full URL of the page where the member initiated registration. In browser-based clients, this is typically window.location.href.

referrer.description:
The HTTP referrer URL indicating the page that led the member to the registration page.

Collected for session audit, security analysis, and analytics purposes. Stored in the member's session record alongside authentication tokens. In browser-based clients, this is typically the value of `document.referrer` at the time of registration.

Format must be a valid URI.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Session context field stored in erp_hrm_member_sessions.referrer alongside generated JWT access/refresh tokens. Represents the HTTP referrer indicating the page that led the member to the registration page. In browser-based clients, this is typically document.referrer.

ip.description:
The client's IPv4 address at the time of registration.

Optional — in server-side rendering (SSR) deployments, the server automatically captures the client IP from the request context as a fallback when this field is not provided. In client-side applications, this should be provided explicitly for accurate session tracking and audit purposes.

Stored in the member's session record for security analysis and geographic context. Format must be a valid IPv4 address.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Session context field stored in erp_hrm_member_sessions alongside generated JWT access/refresh tokens. Optional — in SSR deployments, the server automatically captures the client IP from the request context as fallback (body.ip ?? serverIp). In client-side applications, this should be provided explicitly for accurate session tracking.

IErpHrmMember.IJoin.description:
Registration payload for creating a new member account.

Contains the credentials and identity information needed to register a new member. The email address must be unique across all non-deleted accounts and serves as both the authentication credential and the target for organization invitations. The password is received in plain text and securely hashed before storage — it is never stored or transmitted in plaintext after processing. The display name becomes the member's visible identity across all organizations they join.

Session context fields — the page URL, HTTP referrer, and optional client IP address — are collected for audit, security, and analytics purposes. These are stored in the member's session record alongside the generated JWT tokens. Upon successful registration, the member is immediately authenticated and receives access and refresh tokens — no separate login step is required.
IErpHrmMember.IJoin.x-autobe-specification:
Registration payload creating a new member account in erp_hrm_members with session data in erp_hrm_member_sessions.

Column mappings: email → erp_hrm_members.email (unique, check deleted_at IS NULL for conflict; if soft-deleted match, clear deleted_at), password → erp_hrm_members.password_hash (plain text received, hashed with bcrypt/argon2 before storage), display_name → erp_hrm_members.display_name.

Session context (href, referrer, ip) → erp_hrm_member_sessions alongside generated JWT access/refresh tokens. ip is optional — server captures from request context as fallback (body.ip ?? serverIp) in SSR deployments.

Excluded: id (auto UUID), avatar_image/phone_number (set via profile update), created_at/updated_at (auto timestamps), deleted_at (soft-delete marker). All relations excluded — sessions/emailVerifications created server-side post-registration, others not relevant for join flow.

start_date.description:
The effective date when this contract's compensation terms take effect.

Serves as the anchor point for determining which contract is active — the active contract is the one with the most recent start_date on or before the current date whose end_date is either absent (ongoing) or not yet passed. Modifying this date may shift which contract in the employee's history is considered active, so validation ensures no overlap with adjacent contracts.
start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.start_date. Changing this may shift which contract is considered active — validation must ensure the new start_date does not cause overlap with adjacent contracts. When updating the active contract's start_date, verify no newer contract exists whose start_date would conflict.

end_date.description:
The date when this contract's compensation terms expire.

When absent (null), the contract is ongoing with no predetermined termination date and remains in effect until superseded by a newer contract or the employee leaves the organization. When present, the contract is effective from start_date through end_date inclusive. Once the end_date passes, the contract becomes a historical record.
end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.end_date. Nullable — set to null for an ongoing contract with no predetermined termination. When provided, must be chronologically after start_date. A past end_date causes the contract to become historical and immutable.

pay_rate.description:
The numeric amount the employee earns per unit of time as defined by the pay_period.

For example, 25.50 with an hourly pay_period means the employee earns 25.50 currency units per hour worked. The actual currency unit is determined by the organization's settings. Must be greater than zero.
pay_rate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.pay_rate. Must be greater than zero (enforced by exclusiveMinimum: 0 in schema). Stored as double-precision float in the database.

pay_period.description:
The unit of time against which the pay_rate is measured.

Determines how the pay rate is applied to calculate compensation. Supported values are hourly (pay_rate applies per hour worked), daily (per full workday), weekly (per full workweek), and monthly (per calendar month). Combined with pay_rate, this defines the complete compensation structure for the contract.
pay_period.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.pay_period. Must be one of: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly. Used in conjunction with pay_rate to determine the employee's compensation structure. Validation must reject any value outside this set.

working_hours_per_week.description:
The employee's expected weekly time commitment under this contract.

For example, 40 for a standard full-time arrangement, or 37.5 for a slightly reduced schedule. This value informs budget calculations and capacity planning — it is used to compare planned budget hours against actual logged hours in project budget reports and workforce summaries. Must be greater than zero.
working_hours_per_week.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.working_hours_per_week. Must be greater than zero (enforced by exclusiveMinimum: 0 in schema). Stored as double-precision float. Used for budget calculations and capacity planning across the organization.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes recording additional details about the compensation agreement.

May include information such as bonus structures, overtime policies, equity grants, or special terms that fall outside the structured fields of pay_rate, pay_period, and working_hours_per_week. This field is purely informational and has no effect on calculations or business logic.
notes.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.notes. Nullable — free-form text for additional compensation details such as bonus structures, overtime policies, or special terms outside the structured fields. No validation constraints beyond string typing.

IErpHrmContract.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an employee's currently active contract compensation terms.

All fields are optional — include only the fields you wish to change. The contract to update is identified by the contractId path parameter and must be the employee's active contract. Past contracts that have been superseded by newer agreements or whose end date has passed are preserved as immutable historical records and cannot be modified.

**Editable Fields**

- start_date: The effective date when compensation terms take effect. Modifying this may shift which contract is considered active.
- end_date: The expiration date for the contract term. Set to null to indicate an ongoing contract with no predetermined termination date.
- pay_rate: The numeric compensation amount per unit of time as defined by the pay_period. Must be greater than zero.
- pay_period: The classification of how pay_rate is applied — hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.
- working_hours_per_week: The expected weekly time commitment under this contract, used for capacity planning and budget calculations.
- notes: Free-form text capturing additional compensation details such as bonus structures, overtime policies, or special terms.

**Constraints**: Only the currently active contract may be edited. System-managed fields such as the contract ID, employee association, and timestamps are not accepted in the request body.
IErpHrmContract.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Update DTO for erp_hrm_contracts. All fields are optional — only include fields to change. Maps: start_date → start_date, end_date → end_date (nullable), pay_rate → pay_rate, pay_period → pay_period, working_hours_per_week → working_hours_per_week, notes → notes (nullable). Excluded: id (PK, auto-generated), erp_hrm_employee_id (structural FK — immutable; contract identified by path parameter contractId which resolves the employee), employee (relation — not user-provided in request body), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed timestamps). Validation rules: pay_rate > 0, working_hours_per_week > 0, pay_period ∈ {hourly, daily, weekly, monthly}, start_date < end_date when end_date provided, changing start_date must not cause overlap with adjacent contracts. Only the currently active contract (most recent start_date ≤ now with no end_date or end_date ≥ now) can be updated — past contracts are immutable historical records. On update, refresh updated_at and emit contract-edited real-time event.

search.description:
Text search on project name. Supports partial matching via trigram fuzzy search.

Searches the project name column using PostgreSQL trigram similarity. This enables typo-tolerant and partial-string matching, so searching for "market" will find projects named "Marketing", "Market Research", or similar variations.
search.x-autobe-specification: Fuzzy search on erp_hrm_projects.name using the gin_trgm_ops trigram index. Translates to a similarity or ILIKE query (e.g., WHERE name ILIKE '%' || search || '%' or equivalent pg_trgm similarity operator). Supports partial name matching.

status.description:
Filter by project lifecycle status. Accepts 'active', 'archived', or 'completed'. When omitted, returns projects of all statuses.

Projects progress through three lifecycle stages: active projects accept new time entries and task creation; archived projects are preserved but frozen; completed projects have finished and are frozen. Use this filter to narrow results to a specific stage.
status.x-autobe-specification: Exact match filter on erp_hrm_projects.status. Accepts three lifecycle values: 'active' (accepting time entries), 'archived' (frozen, preserved), 'completed' (finished, frozen). When omitted, no status filter is applied and projects of all statuses are returned.

page.description:
Page number for offset-based pagination. 1-indexed (first page is 1).

Controls which page of results to return. Combined with limit to compute the database offset for the SELECT query. The response includes pagination metadata (current page, total pages, total records) for building navigation controls.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination control for offset calculation. 1-indexed (first page is 1). Translated to SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit. Must be >= 1. Defaults to 1 when omitted.

limit.description:
Number of projects per page. Maximum 100.

Controls how many project summaries are returned in a single response. The actual number may be fewer on the last page when total records don't divide evenly. Lower values improve response time; higher values reduce the number of requests needed to browse large datasets.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Pagination control for maximum records per page. Translated to SQL LIMIT. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Defaults when omitted.

sort.description:
Sort criteria as an array of [field, direction] pairs. Supported fields: 'name', 'created_at'. Directions: 'ASC', 'DESC'. Example: ['name', 'ASC']. Defaults to ['created_at', 'DESC'] when omitted.

Controls the ordering of returned projects. Multiple sort criteria are applied in array order (e.g., sort by status first, then by name). The default ordering places the most recently created projects at the top of the list.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Multi-field sort specification as an array of [field, direction] pairs. Each pair is processed in order to build the SQL ORDER BY clause. Supported fields: 'name' (sorts on erp_hrm_projects.name), 'created_at' (sorts on erp_hrm_projects.created_at). Supported directions: 'ASC', 'DESC'. Defaults to ['created_at', 'DESC'] when sort is omitted or empty, ensuring newest projects appear first.

IErpHrmProject.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for browsing and filtering projects within the current organization.

Provides search, status filtering, and pagination controls for the project list endpoint. All parameters are optional — when none are specified, the endpoint returns all active, archived, and completed projects (excluding soft-deleted) ordered by newest first.

This is a pure request DTO with no direct database table mapping. It collects query parameters that are translated into SQL WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and OFFSET clauses against the erp_hrm_projects table.
IErpHrmProject.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameters for browsing erp_hrm_projects scoped to session organization (organization_id = session.organization_id).

Filters:
- search: Trigram fuzzy match on the name column using the gin_trgm_ops index. Supports partial name matching via pg_trgm similarity operators.
- status: Exact match on the status column. Accepts 'active', 'archived', or 'completed'. When omitted, returns projects of all statuses.

Always applied: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted projects).

Pagination: Offset-based using page (1-indexed) and limit. Compute OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit. Maximum 100 records per page.

Sorting: Default ordering by created_at DESC (newest first). When sort parameter is provided, apply specified sort fields in array order. Supported fields: 'name', 'created_at'. Supported directions: 'ASC', 'DESC'.

Authorization: Requires project:view permission. Returns 403 Forbidden otherwise.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the employee record within the organization.

A UUID v4 string that serves as the primary key for all employee operations. This identifier is used in API paths (e.g., /erpHrm/member/employees/{employeeId}) and as a foreign key reference in related entities such as contracts, project memberships, timelogs, and timesheets.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.id. Primary key, UUID format, auto-generated on creation. Used as the unique identifier in all employee-related API paths.

position.description:
The employee's job title or position name within the organization.

Purely descriptive — carries no inherent permissions. Used for organizational clarity, reporting, and display in employee directories. May be null when no position has been assigned to the employee.
position.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.position. Nullable string — no format constraints beyond max length. Free-text job title such as "Software Engineer" or "Marketing Lead".

employment_type.description:
Classification of the employment relationship.

Determines how the employee appears in workforce summaries and organizational charts. Valid values are `full-time`, `part-time`, `contractor`, and `intern`. Used for filtering and reporting across the organization.
employment_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.employment_type. Constrained to one of: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern. Always non-null — every employee has an employment type.

status.description:
Current activity status of the employee within the organization.

Controls the employee's ability to perform actions within the platform. `active` employees can log time, submit timesheets, and participate in projects. `deactivated` employees retain all historical data — timelogs, timesheets, contracts, and project memberships — but cannot create new timelogs, edit existing timelogs, or submit timesheets. Deactivation is reversible through the reactivate endpoint.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.status. Constrained to one of: active, deactivated. Always non-null. Status transitions are handled via dedicated endpoints (deactivate/reactivate).

member.description:
The user account profile associated with this employee record.

Contains the member's global identity fields — display name, email, avatar, and phone number — shared across all organizations the member belongs to. Also includes organization-specific employment details such as the employee ID, position, employment type, status, assigned role name, and department name within the current organization. This consolidated view enables callers to display complete employee information without additional API calls.
member.x-autobe-specification: INNER JOIN erp_hrm_members via erp_hrm_member_id. Returns IErpHrmMember.ISummary — a consolidated view combining the member's global profile (id, email, display_name, avatar_image, phone_number) with organization-specific employment details (employee_id, position, employment_type, status, role_name, department_name). INNER JOIN is appropriate because every employee must have a member.

role.description:
The role assigned to this employee, determining their permissions within the organization.

Each employee holds exactly one role at all times. The role's permission set defines all access rights for the employee and takes effect immediately upon assignment. Includes the role's unique identifier, display name, built-in status (indicating whether it is one of the three immutable built-in roles: Owner, Manager, or Employee), optional description, and the count of permissions granted to the role.
role.x-autobe-specification: INNER JOIN erp_hrm_roles via erp_hrm_role_id. Returns IErpHrmRole.ISummary with the role's id, name, is_builtin flag, description, permissions_count, created_at, and updated_at. INNER JOIN — every employee has a role. The role's permission set determines all access rights for the employee.

department.description:
The department this employee belongs to, or null if not assigned to any department.

Department assignment is purely organizational — it carries no inherent permissions and is used for grouping, filtering, and reporting purposes. An employee can exist without a department. When a department is deleted, affected employees have their department reference cleared without removing the employee records themselves.
department.x-autobe-specification: LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_departments via erp_hrm_department_id. Returns IErpHrmDepartment.ISummary when the employee is assigned to a department, null otherwise. Department is optional — erp_hrm_department_id may be null. When a department is deleted, the reference is cleared without affecting the employee record.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the employee record was created.

Set automatically when the employee joins the organization, whether through invitation acceptance or direct assignment. This value is immutable — it is never modified after the initial creation and serves as an audit record of when the employee's membership began.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.created_at. DateTime with timezone (ISO 8601 format). Set automatically when the employee record is created — either through invitation acceptance or direct assignment. Never modified after creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the employee record.

Updated automatically whenever any employee attribute changes, including role reassignment, department placement, position updates, employment type classification changes, and status transitions between active and deactivated. Provides an audit trail of when the employee's organizational identity was last altered.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.updated_at. DateTime with timezone (ISO 8601 format). Automatically updated on every modification to the employee record, including role reassignment, department changes, position updates, employment type changes, and status transitions.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for data retention and audit integrity.

When set, the employee record is considered removed but preserved for audit purposes. Soft-deleted records are excluded from all query results — this field will always be null in API responses. Set during organization deletion cascades or account deletion cleanup. The timestamp is retained for potential recovery within the data retention window.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.deleted_at. Nullable DateTime with timezone. Soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are excluded from query results, so this field is always null in API responses. Preserved in the schema for type completeness and to support potential future recovery flows.

IErpHrmEmployee.description:
Complete employee profile within an organization.

Represents a single employee's organizational identity including their unique identifier, assigned role with permissions, optional department placement, position title, employment type classification, and current activity status. The member field provides the user's global profile information — display name, email, avatar, and phone — shared across all organizations they belong to.

This is a Read DTO returned by employee detail endpoints. Deactivated employees are returned with their full historical data intact — deactivation prevents new time tracking and timesheet submission but does not affect record visibility. Soft-deleted employees are excluded from query results.
IErpHrmEmployee.x-autobe-specification: Query erp_hrm_employees by id within the current organization scope (erp_hrm_organization_id = session organization). INNER JOIN erp_hrm_members on erp_hrm_member_id to include the member's display_name, email, avatar_image, and phone_number. INNER JOIN erp_hrm_roles on erp_hrm_role_id to include the role's name, is_builtin flag, description, and permissions_count. LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_departments on erp_hrm_department_id to include the department name and description (null if no department assigned). Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). Authorization: require employee:view OR employee:manage permission on the current organization.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the role.

The primary key is a UUID generated by the system when the role is created. For built-in roles, this occurs at organization creation time. For custom roles, this occurs when an owner defines the role.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.id. UUID primary key, system-generated at role creation.

name.description:
Human-readable role name that uniquely identifies the role within its organization.

Serves as the primary way users and administrators distinguish between different roles. Must be unique within a single organization — no two roles in the same organization can share the same name. Examples include the three built-in names (Owner, Manager, Employee) and custom names such as Finance Manager or Senior Developer.
name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.name. Enforced unique within organization via composite unique constraint [erp_hrm_organization_id, name].

is_builtin.description:
Indicates whether this role is one of the three built-in roles provisioned automatically at organization creation.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are immutable — they can never be deleted or modified regardless of how many employees are assigned. Custom roles have this flag set to false and may be soft-deleted when no employees are assigned to them.
is_builtin.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.is_builtin. True for the three immutable built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee), false for custom roles.

description.description:
Optional description explaining the role's intended purpose, scope, and responsibilities within the organization.

Provides context for organization owners and administrators when managing roles, clarifying what level of access each role entails. May be null if no description has been set.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.description. Nullable — null when no description has been provided.

permissions.description:
The complete set of permissions granted to members assigned to this role.

Each entry in the array represents a single permission from the system's fixed permission catalog, identified by a unique dot-notation key (e.g., "org:manage", "time:approve") and a human-readable description of the access it grants. The permission set determines all access rights for employees holding this role.

Permission changes take effect immediately — when an owner updates the role's permissions, all employees assigned to the role receive the updated access rights without requiring re-authentication.
permissions.x-autobe-specification: Resolved via rolePermissions has-many relation on erp_hrm_roles → erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table → erp_hrm_permissions. Each junction row carries a permission ID that joins to the permissions catalog. Project each resolved permission to IErpHrmPermission.ISummary (id, key, description). Load eagerly with the role query for complete permission context.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the role was created.

For built-in roles, this matches the organization creation time since they are provisioned automatically. For custom roles, this reflects when the organization owner created the role.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.created_at. Set at role creation — matches organization creation time for built-in roles, reflects owner action time for custom roles.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the role was last modified.

Updated whenever the role's name, description, or permission set changes. Permission changes propagate immediately — the timestamp reflects when the modification was applied, and all employees assigned to the role receive updated access rights from that moment.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.updated_at. Updated whenever the role's name, description, or permission set changes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete timestamp for the role.

Null for active roles and all built-in roles (which are never deletable). Set to the deletion timestamp when an organization owner soft-deletes a custom role that has no employees assigned to it. Soft-deleted roles are excluded from normal query results but preserved for audit integrity.

IErpHrmRole.description:
A role definition within an organization, including its name, description, built-in status, and the complete set of permissions granted to members assigned to this role.

Roles form the foundation of the role-based access control system. Each employee in an organization holds exactly one role, and the role's permission set determines all access rights for that employee. The three built-in roles — Owner, Manager, and Employee — are provisioned automatically at organization creation and are immutable. Custom roles can be created, updated, and soft-deleted by organization owners.

The permissions array contains the full set of permissions currently assigned to the role, each represented as a summary with its unique key and human-readable description. Permission changes propagate immediately — any employee assigned to this role will have their effective access rights updated instantly when the permission set changes.

The is_builtin flag identifies roles that cannot be modified or deleted. Built-in roles always have this flag set to true. The deleted_at timestamp indicates when a custom role was soft-deleted; it is always null for active roles and built-in roles.

status.description:
Filter by verification status.

Derived filter computed at query time from two columns:
- pending: WHERE verified_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW() — token is unverified and still valid.
- verified: WHERE verified_at IS NOT NULL — token was successfully consumed.
- expired: WHERE verified_at IS NULL AND expires_at <= NOW() — token timed out without being used.

Only one status value can be applied per query. The WHERE clause is constructed dynamically based on the selected const value.
