Cursor-based pagination ensures stable ordering even when new records are inserted between page requests.

Encodes the last record's sort field values (determined by sort_field) to set the starting point for the next page query. Applied as WHERE (sort_field, id) > (cursor_sort_value, cursor_id) with appropriate comparison direction based on sort_direction.

Omit or set to null for the first page of results.

The organization this department belongs to.

All department operations — including queries, updates, and hierarchy traversal — are bounded by the currently selected organization context. This value is set automatically from the authenticated session when the department is created and is never modified.
erp_hrm_organization_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.erp_hrm_organization_id. Identifies the organization this department belongs to. Set from session context on creation and never changed. Enforces multi-tenancy data isolation.

Timestamp when the department was created.

Set automatically at the moment of creation and remains immutable for the lifetime of the department record. Stored in UTC with timezone awareness. Use this for auditing when the department was first established in the organizational structure.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.created_at. Timestamptz — set automatically on creation and never modified thereafter.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the department record.

Updated automatically whenever the department's name, description, or parent relationship is changed. Stored in UTC with timezone awareness. Compare with created_at to determine if the department has been modified since its initial creation.

A department with active child departments cannot be soft-deleted until all children are reassigned or deleted first.

IErpHrmDepartment.description:
Full department record within an organization.

Departments are organizational groupings that categorize employees by functional area or team — such as Engineering, Sales, or Human Resources. They serve purely as a structural organization tool with no bearing on permissions, access control, or project assignments.

The department hierarchy supports a one-level parent-child nesting pattern: a department may optionally reference a parent department, and a department may serve as a parent to child departments, but a child department cannot itself be a parent. The parent field contains the parent department summary when nested within a hierarchy, and is null for top-level departments.

Soft-deleted departments are indicated by a non-null deleted_at timestamp. All employees within the organization can view any department regardless of their role.

The parent_id FK column is excluded from the DTO — it exists only as the join key behind the parent $ref object. IErpHrmTask.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for listing tasks within a project.

All properties are optional — when omitted, no corresponding filter is applied. Filters that accept arrays ({@link status}, {@link priority}) support multiple values for OR-based matching within each filter category.

Filtering supports narrowing results by task status, priority level, assigned employee, parent task relationship, and due date range. The {@link search} field performs fuzzy text matching against task titles using trigram indexing. Set {@link parentTaskId} to `null` to retrieve only top-level tasks (those without a parent).

Sorting is controlled by {@link sort} (field to sort by) and {@link order} (direction). When both are omitted, results default to creation date descending.

Pagination uses {@link page} and {@link limit} for offset-based navigation. The response includes total matching count for building UI pagination controls.

Sortable by due_date, priority, created_at. Pagination via page/limit.

IErpHrmContract.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new employment contract for an employee.

Specifies the compensation terms including pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, and the effective date range. The employee is identified by the `employeeId` path parameter and must not be included in the request body.

When a new contract is created, the system automatically closes the employee's previous active contract by setting its end date to the day before the new contract's start date, ensuring only one contract is active at any given time while preserving all past contracts as immutable historical records.

Excluded: id (auto-generated UUID), erp_hrm_employee_id (from {employeeId} path parameter), created_at/updated_at (auto-set to current timestamp on insert), deleted_at (always null on creation). Business validation: pay_rate > 0, working_hours_per_week > 0, pay_period must be one of hourly/daily/weekly/monthly, if end_date is provided then start_date < end_date. On creation, the system auto-closes the employee's previous active contract by setting its end_date to the day before start_date.

id.description:

old_status.description:
The task status before the transition occurred.

One of four workflow statuses: open (work not yet started), in-progress (work actively underway), completed (deliverable finished), or closed (formally finalized). Together with new_status, this captures both the origin and destination of the state change, enabling audit review of the full lifecycle path.

Example: if a task moves from in-progress to completed, old_status is 'in-progress' and new_status is 'completed'.

new_status.description:

One of four workflow statuses: open (work not yet started), in-progress (work actively underway), completed (deliverable finished), or closed (formally finalized). Together with old_status, this captures both the origin and destination of the state change.

Example: if a task moves from in-progress to completed, old_status is 'in-progress' and new_status is 'completed'.
new_status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.new_status. String enum: open, in-progress, completed, closed. Captured at the moment of status transition — the value after the change was applied.

Identifies the authenticated user who triggered the status transition. This could be the task's assigned employee updating their own task, a project lead managing tasks within their project, or any user with appropriate project management permissions.

The member object includes their global profile — display name, email, avatar image, and phone number — along with their organization-specific employment details such as position title, employment type, role name, and department name within the current organization context.

IErpHrmTaskHistory.ISummary.description:
A compact representation of a single task status history entry for list display.

Each entry records one status transition in a task's lifecycle, showing the status before the change (old_status), the status after the change (new_status), which member performed the transition (changed_by_member), and when it occurred (created_at). Status values follow the task workflow: open, in-progress, completed, and closed.

History entries are immutable — they are created automatically by the system when a task's status changes and cannot be modified or deleted after creation. The complete chronological record provides a full audit trail of how each task moved through its workflow states.

FK column changed_by_member_id is excluded — the member identity is exposed through the richer relation object instead.

IErpHrmTask.description:
Full detail representation of a task entity within a project.

Tasks are the fundamental units of work within a project, each following a status workflow from open through in-progress and completed to closed. Tasks can be assigned to a single employee who must be a member of the parent project.

**Task Hierarchy**: Tasks support one level of subtask nesting. A task with a parent is a subtask; child tasks of a parent are exposed via {@link childTasks}. A parent task cannot itself have a parent, enforcing a maximum depth of one.

**Status and Priority**: The {@link status} field tracks the current workflow state (open, in-progress, completed, closed). The {@link priority} field indicates urgency (low, medium, high, urgent). Every status change is recorded in {@link statusHistories} for a complete audit trail.

HAS-MANY: childTasks (recursive erp_hrm_tasks[] via parent_task_id) → IErpHrmTask.ISummary[], statusHistories (erp_hrm_task_histories[]) → IErpHrmTaskHistory.ISummary[].

IErpHrmContract.description:
Full details of an employee employment contract including compensation terms, effective dates, and metadata.

Each contract defines the pay rate, the pay period classification (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly), the expected working hours per week, and optional free-form notes for additional context such as bonus structures or special terms. Contracts form a historical record over an employee's tenure — an employee may have multiple contracts, with only one active at any given time based on start date recency and end date validity. Past contracts that have been superseded or expired become immutable historical records preserved for auditing and compliance purposes.

The employee reference identifies the organization member to whom this contract belongs, resolved as a summary view including their profile, role, department, and employment status.

Request body for assigning an employee to a project.

Carries the employee to assign and an optional membership role. The target project is specified in the URL path, and the organization context is determined by the authenticated user's session.

The role determines the employee's authority within the project: `member` for regular participants who can track time and view assigned tasks, or `project-lead` for members with task management authority. When omitted, the role defaults to `member`.

Role defaults to 'member' server-side if omitted. Validate role is either 'member' or 'project-lead'.

week_start_date.description:
The Monday date marking the start of the timesheet's calendar week.

Must be a Monday. The system computes the corresponding Sunday as the week end date automatically. Combined with the authenticated employee's identity, this enforces the unique constraint of at most one timesheet per employee per calendar week.

The date determines which ungrouped timelogs are automatically associated with the new timesheet — all timelogs belonging to the employee with dates falling between this Monday and the following Sunday (inclusive) are linked to the timesheet upon creation.

IErpHrmTimesheet.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a draft timesheet.

The authenticated employee's timesheet is created for the calendar week starting on the given Monday date. The system automatically computes the week end date as the following Sunday and associates all ungrouped timelogs within that range with the new timesheet.

The timesheet begins in draft status, allowing the employee to add or remove timelogs before submission. Each employee may have at most one timesheet per calendar week.

Future weeks are allowed for draft creation; submission restrictions for future weeks are enforced separately at submission time.

Excluded: employee_id (resolved from JWT session's currently selected organization context — the authenticated employee owns the timesheet), status (auto-set to 'draft' on creation), week_end_date (computed as week_start_date + 6 days), reviewed_by_user_id/submitted_at/reviewed_at/rejection_reason (all null on creation — populated during submission and review workflows), id/created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed — auto-generated on insert). Validate week_start_date falls on a Monday before creating. Check unique constraint on (employee_id, week_start_date) — reject with 409 if duplicate. After insert, auto-associate ungrouped timelogs (employee_id matches, timesheet_id IS NULL, date within week range, deleted_at IS NULL). Deactivated employees must be rejected.

IErpHrmTask.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new task within a project.

Tasks are the fundamental work units within a project, each with a title, optional description, workflow status, priority level, estimated hours, and deadline. Tasks support optional assignment to an employee who must be an active member of the project, and one-level subtask nesting through an optional parent task reference that must belong to the same project.

IErpHrmProject.ICreate.description:

Optional fields provide additional context: a description explaining the project's purpose or scope, budget hours for comparing planned effort against actual logged time in budget reports, and start and end dates to define the project timeline. Emit project creation real-time event on success.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the task.

System-assigned UUID used as the primary key. Immutable once created. Used as the path parameter in task detail and update endpoints.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_tasks.id. UUID primary key.

title.description:
The task's title summarizing its purpose or objective.

Serves as the primary human-readable identifier in task boards, list views, and assignment displays. Must not be empty.
title.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_tasks.title. Not null, not empty.

status.description:
The current workflow status of the task.

Allowed values are open (initial state, work not yet started), in-progress (work actively underway), completed (deliverable finished), and closed (formally finalized). Every status change is automatically recorded as an immutable entry in the task's status history.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_tasks.status. Allowed values: open, in-progress, completed, closed.

priority.description:
The urgency level indicating how quickly the task should be addressed.

Allowed values are low, medium (default), high, and urgent. Priority serves as guidance for employees and managers on which tasks to address first but does not enforce scheduling behavior on its own. Used for sorting and filtering in task boards.
priority.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_tasks.priority. Allowed values: low, medium, high, urgent. Default: medium.

estimated_hours.description:
Optional numeric estimate of the total hours expected to complete this task.

When provided, must be a positive number. Used for planning and can be compared against actual logged hours from timelogs. Null when no estimate has been set.
estimated_hours.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_tasks.estimated_hours. Nullable DoublePrecision float. Must be positive when provided.

due_date.description:
Optional deadline by which the task should be completed.

Used for planning, sorting, and filtering in task boards. A task without a due date has no fixed deadline. Represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string.
due_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_tasks.due_date. Nullable Timestamptz. ISO 8601 date-time string.

assignedEmployee.description:
The employee assigned to work on this task, or null if unassigned.

When set, contains a summary of the assigned employee including their member profile, role, and department. The assigned employee must be a member of the task's parent project. When an employee is removed from the project, their task assignments are cleared, leaving the task unassigned.
assignedEmployee.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation: JOIN erp_hrm_tasks.erp_hrm_assigned_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees.id, then resolve to IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. Nullable — null when the task is unassigned. The assigned employee must be a project member.

parentTask.description:
The immediate parent task when this is a subtask, or null for top-level tasks.

Provides hierarchical context in task boards by linking a subtask to its parent. Only one level of nesting is supported — a parent task cannot itself have a parent. The parent task must belong to the same project as the child.
parentTask.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to self-referencing relation: JOIN erp_hrm_tasks.erp_hrm_parent_task_id → erp_hrm_tasks.id, resolving to IErpHrmTask.ISummary. Nullable — null for top-level tasks. Parent task must belong to same project.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the task was created.

Automatically set at creation time and never modified thereafter. Used for chronological listing and audit purposes. Represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_tasks.created_at. Timestamptz, auto-set on creation, never modified.

IErpHrmTask.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a task for use in project task boards and paginated list views.

Includes core task attributes — title, status, priority, due date, estimated hours, and creation date — sufficient for browsing and filtering without loading the full task detail. The assignedEmployee field provides the assignee's summary profile when a task is assigned, and is null for unassigned tasks.

For subtasks, the parentTask field contains a summary of the immediate parent task, providing hierarchical context. Top-level tasks have a null parent task. Large fields such as description and composition collections (child tasks, status histories, timelogs) are excluded to keep the payload compact for list rendering. This schema is always queried within the context of a specific project identified by the URL path.
IErpHrmTask.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, title, status, priority, estimated_hours, due_date, created_at. Relations: assignedEmployee via JOIN on erp_hrm_assigned_employee_id → IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary (BELONGS-TO, nullable when unassigned), parentTask via self-referencing JOIN on erp_hrm_parent_task_id → IErpHrmTask.ISummary (BELONGS-TO, nullable for top-level tasks). Excluded: description (large text field), erp_hrm_project_id (project context from URL path), updated_at (not needed for list display), deleted_at (soft-delete filtered at query level). HAS-MANY compositions (childTasks, statusHistories, timelogs, timers) excluded per ISummary convention — summarized data loaded via separate endpoints. BELONGS-TO project relation excluded — project identity is already known from the request path.

week_start_date.description:
The Monday date marking the start of the timesheet's calendar week.

Combined with week_end_date, this defines the Monday-to-Sunday range that determines which timelogs are eligible for inclusion in the timesheet. Must be a Monday. When provided without week_end_date, the end date is automatically calculated as 6 days later.
week_start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_start_date. Must be a Monday (ISO day-of-week = 1). When provided alone, week_end_date is auto-derived as week_start_date + 6 days (Sunday). The (employee_id, week_start_date) pair must be unique across all non-deleted timesheets for the same employee.

week_end_date.description:
The Sunday date marking the end of the timesheet's calendar week.

Always exactly 6 days after week_start_date. Must be a Sunday. When provided without week_start_date, the start date is automatically calculated as 6 days earlier.
week_end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_end_date. Must be a Sunday exactly 6 days after week_start_date. When provided alone, week_start_date is auto-derived as week_end_date - 6 days (Monday). The (employee_id, auto-derived week_start_date) pair must be unique across all non-deleted timesheets for the same employee.

IErpHrmTimesheet.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating a draft timesheet's calendar week range.

Each timesheet groups an employee's timelogs for a specific Monday-to-Sunday calendar week. This payload allows the owning employee or a user with the time:manage permission to adjust the week boundaries of a timesheet while it remains in draft status — before submission locks the definition.

Both week_start_date and week_end_date are optional. Provide both to set the week explicitly, provide just one to have the other derived automatically (Monday-to-Sunday, 6-day span), or provide neither for a no-op update. The week range must not overlap with any other timesheet belonging to the same employee.
IErpHrmTimesheet.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Mutates: week_start_date, week_end_date in the erp_hrm_timesheets table. Both fields are optional — an empty body is a no-op, providing a single field auto-derives the other (6-day span: week_end_date = week_start_date + 6 days, or week_start_date = week_end_date - 6 days). Only valid when the timesheet is in 'draft' status. Validation (enforced at service layer): week_start_date must be a Monday (ISO day-of-week = 1), week_end_date must be a Sunday exactly 6 days after week_start_date, and the (employee_id, week_start_date) pair must not conflict with any other non-deleted timesheet owned by the same employee (enforcing @@unique([employee_id, week_start_date])). Employee context is resolved from the authenticated session — the employee owning the timesheet cannot be changed through this operation. If any contained timelogs have dates outside the new week range, they remain associated to the timesheet; the caller is responsible for managing timelog membership separately.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the task history entry.

A UUID v4 value assigned automatically when the history entry is created. This identifier is immutable and serves as the primary key for direct retrieval of individual history entries through the dedicated endpoint.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated on creation. Immutable after creation.

task.description:
The task whose status transition this history entry records.

Contains a summary view of the task including its title, status, priority, due date, estimated hours, and the assigned employee if any. This provides full context for the status change without requiring a separate task lookup. The task reference is always present — every history entry belongs to exactly one task.
task.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation via JOIN on erp_hrm_task_histories.erp_hrm_task_id = erp_hrm_tasks.id. Returns IErpHrmTask.ISummary — the task whose status changed. Always present since every history entry must belong to a task.

changedByMember.description:
The member who performed the status change.

Contains the member's identity information including display name, email, avatar, and their organization-specific employment details (position, employment type, status, role, department). This ensures full accountability in the audit trail — every status transition is traceable to the specific person who made it.
changedByMember.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation via JOIN on erp_hrm_task_histories.changed_by_member_id = erp_hrm_members.id. Returns IErpHrmMember.ISummary — the authenticated member who performed the status change. Always present to maintain audit accountability.

old_status.description:
The task status before the transition.

One of the four workflow statuses: open (work has not yet started), in-progress (work actively underway), completed (deliverable finished), or closed (formally finalized). Together with new_status, this captures both the origin and destination of the state change, providing a complete picture of the transition.
old_status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.old_status. String value, one of: open, in-progress, completed, closed. Captures the task status immediately before the transition occurred.

new_status.description:
The task status after the transition.

One of the four workflow statuses: open (work has not yet started), in-progress (work actively underway), completed (deliverable finished), or closed (formally finalized). Together with old_status, this captures both the origin and destination of the state change, providing a complete picture of the transition.
new_status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.new_status. String value, one of: open, in-progress, completed, closed. Captures the task status immediately after the transition occurred.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the status change occurred.

An ISO 8601 date-time value recording the exact moment the status transition was committed. This serves as both the creation timestamp of the history entry and the chronological marker for the task's lifecycle. Entries within a task are ordered by this timestamp, forming a complete chronological audit trail. The timestamp is immutable — it reflects the actual time the change happened and cannot be modified.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.created_at. DateTime timestamp recording when the status change occurred. Serves as both the creation time of the history entry and the point-in-time marker for the status transition. Immutable after creation.

IErpHrmTaskHistory.description:
An immutable audit trail entry recording a single status transition of a task.

Each entry captures the status before and after the change, the timestamp of the transition, and the member who performed it. Task history entries are created automatically by the system whenever a task's status is updated and cannot be modified or deleted after creation, providing a complete chronological record of the task's lifecycle.

Status values follow the defined workflow: open, in-progress, completed, and closed. The history entry includes the full task summary for context and the member summary identifying who made the change. Access to history entries follows task visibility rules — only project members and users with project:manage or project:view permissions can view them.
IErpHrmTaskHistory.x-autobe-specification: Direct column mappings: id (UUID primary key), old_status (string, one of: open, in-progress, completed, closed), new_status (string, same enum), created_at (timestamp of the status transition). BELONGS-TO relations: task via JOIN on erp_hrm_task_id → IErpHrmTask.ISummary, changedByMember via JOIN on changed_by_member_id → IErpHrmMember.ISummary. FK columns erp_hrm_task_id and changed_by_member_id are intentionally excluded from the DTO — they are resolved into their respective relation objects. Immutable audit record: entries are created automatically when a task status changes and cannot be modified or deleted after creation. No update or delete operations exist for this entity.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the timesheet.

A UUID that uniquely identifies this timesheet record across the system. Used as the primary reference in API paths for retrieving, updating, and reviewing individual timesheets.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.id. Primary key, UUID.

week_start_date.description:
The Monday date marking the start of the timesheet's calendar week.

Defines the beginning of the Monday-to-Sunday week range covered by this timesheet. Together with week_end_date, this determines which timelogs are eligible for inclusion. An employee may have at most one timesheet per calendar week, enforced by the unique constraint on (employee_id, week_start_date).
week_start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_start_date. Always a Monday date, stored as Timestamptz.

week_end_date.description:
The Sunday date marking the end of the timesheet's calendar week.

Always exactly six days after week_start_date, defining the Sunday boundary of the timesheet's coverage period. Provided alongside week_start_date for query convenience when filtering by date ranges that may cross week boundaries.
week_end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_end_date. Always exactly 6 days after week_start_date, stored as Timestamptz.

status.description:
Current workflow status of the timesheet.

Determines what actions are available on the timesheet:
- **draft**: Timelogs can be added or removed. The employee is still populating the timesheet.
- **submitted**: Awaiting review by a manager or owner. Timelogs are locked against modification.
- **approved**: Review completed and accepted. All contained timelogs are permanently locked.
- **rejected**: Returned to draft status for revision. A rejection reason is provided by the reviewer.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.status. Allowed values: draft, submitted, approved, rejected.

total_hours.description:
Total hours logged across all timelogs in this timesheet.

Aggregates the duration of every timelog contained within this timesheet, converting the sum from minutes to hours. Returns zero when the timesheet has no timelogs yet. This field provides an immediate at-a-glance measure of the work recorded for the week without requiring clients to load individual timelog records.
total_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed: COALESCE(SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes), 0) / 60.0. Aggregates all timelogs linked to this timesheet, converting total minutes to hours with one decimal precision. Returns 0 when no timelogs exist in the timesheet.

submitted_at.description:
Timestamp when the employee submitted this timesheet for review.

Records the exact moment the timesheet transitioned from draft to submitted status. Null when the timesheet is still in draft status and has never been submitted. Once set, this timestamp persists even if the timesheet is later rejected and resubmitted — it reflects the most recent submission.
submitted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.submitted_at. Nullable: null when timesheet has never been submitted (draft status). Set when transitioning from draft to submitted.

employee.description:
The employee who owns this timesheet.

Identifies the organization member whose timelogs are grouped into this timesheet. The employee summary includes the member's profile (display name, email, avatar), their position, employment type, assigned role, and optional department — providing sufficient context to identify the timesheet owner in list views without loading the full employee record.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation: JOIN erp_hrm_employees ON employee_id → IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary (includes member profile via erp_hrm_members for display_name and position). FK column employee_id is not directly exposed.

IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a timesheet for list browsing.

Provides the essential information needed to identify and assess a timesheet at a glance: the calendar week it covers, its current workflow status, total hours logged, submission timestamp, and the owning employee's identity. The total hours field aggregates all contained timelogs' durations, converting minutes to hours for display. Review details such as reviewer identity, review timestamp, and rejection reason are omitted from this compact list view — use the timesheet detail endpoint to retrieve the full review context.
IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, week_start_date, week_end_date, status, submitted_at. Computed: total_hours (COALESCE(SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes), 0) / 60.0, converting minutes to hours). Relation: employee via JOIN on employee_id → erp_hrm_employees → erp_hrm_members for display_name and position. Excluded: reviewed_at, rejection_reason (detailed review context omitted from summary), created_at, updated_at (list view uses week dates not record timestamps), deleted_at (filtered at query), employee_id (FK exposed as employee object), reviewed_by_user_id (reviewer not in summary), reviewedByUser (relation not exposed), timelogs (HAS-MANY excluded from ISummary).

id.description:
Unique identifier of the timer.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies this timer record across all organizations. Used as the primary key for direct timer lookups and as the target for stop, discard, and update operations on the running timer.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.id. UUID primary key.

employee.description:
The employee who owns this timer.

Provides the essential identity and classification of the employee running the timer, including their member profile, assigned role, department, position, employment type, and current status. This is always present since every timer is scoped to a single employee.
employee.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation: INNER JOIN erp_hrm_employees ON erp_hrm_timers.erp_hrm_employee_id = erp_hrm_employees.id → IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. Every timer belongs to exactly one employee.

project.description:
The project against which time is being tracked.

Identifies the project that the employee is currently working on. Includes the project name, color code for visual distinction, current status, and optional description. This is always present since every timer must be associated with a project.
project.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation: INNER JOIN erp_hrm_projects ON erp_hrm_timers.erp_hrm_project_id = erp_hrm_projects.id → IErpHrmProject.ISummary. Every timer targets exactly one project.

task.description:
The specific task within the project that the employee is working on.

When set, this identifies the task being worked on — including its title, status, priority, estimated hours, due date, assigned employee, parent task context, and creation timestamp. When null, the employee is tracking time against the project in general without a particular task focus.
task.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation: LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_tasks ON erp_hrm_timers.erp_hrm_task_id = erp_hrm_tasks.id → IErpHrmTask.ISummary | null. Nullable — timer may track time against a project without a specific task.

start_timestamp.description:
The exact date and time when the timer was started.

Serves as the reference point for calculating the elapsed duration of the tracking session. This value is set once when the timer is created and never changes — even when the employee updates the project, task, or description while the timer continues running.

When the timer is stopped, the elapsed duration is computed as the difference between the stop time and this start timestamp, and a timelog record is created with that duration.
start_timestamp.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.start_timestamp. ISO 8601 date-time format. Represents the moment the employee began tracking. Remains unchanged when the timer's project, task, or description are edited while running.

description.description:
Free-text note describing what the employee is currently working on.

Provides context about the activity being tracked, such as specific tasks, meeting details, or work notes. This field is editable at any point while the timer is running, allowing the employee to refine their description as their activity evolves.

When null, no description has been provided for the current tracking session.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.description. Nullable free-text string. Mutable while the timer is running — the employee can update it to reflect changes in their current activity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the timer record was created in the database.

Reflects the moment the timer was persisted, which may differ slightly from the start_timestamp if there is any processing delay. Used for chronological ordering of timer records and audit purposes.

This value is immutable once set.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.created_at. ISO 8601 date-time format. Automatically set when the timer record is inserted into the database and never modified thereafter.

IErpHrmTimer.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an active timer for list displays.

Represents a currently running time-tracking session for an employee within the organization. Each entry identifies who is tracking time (employee), what they are working on (project and optional task), when they started, and their current work description.

Used in paginated timer list responses where each entry provides enough information to identify and monitor active tracking sessions at a glance. Full timer detail, including the complete employee profile and all project metadata, is available through the timer detail endpoint.
IErpHrmTimer.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Summary view of the erp_hrm_timers table for list displays. Direct columns: id, start_timestamp, description, created_at. BELONGS-TO relations resolved via JOINs: employee (INNER JOIN erp_hrm_employees on erp_hrm_employee_id → IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary), project (INNER JOIN erp_hrm_projects on erp_hrm_project_id → IErpHrmProject.ISummary), task (LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_tasks on erp_hrm_task_id → IErpHrmTask.ISummary | null). Excluded: updated_at (non-essential metadata for summary), all FK columns (erp_hrm_employee_id, erp_hrm_project_id, erp_hrm_task_id — exposed via relation objects). Organization scoping implicit from session context.

employeeId.description:
Filter contracts to a specific employee by their unique identifier.

When provided, only contracts belonging to the specified employee are returned. This parameter is useful for org-wide contract browsing by managers who want to drill down into a single employee's compensation history. When the endpoint already scopes by employee via a path parameter, this filter is redundant and can be omitted.
employeeId.x-autobe-specification: Equality filter on erp_hrm_contracts.erp_hrm_employee_id. When used in the org-wide listing endpoint (/erpHrm/member/contracts), narrows results to a specific employee's contracts. When used in the employee-scoped endpoint (/erpHrm/member/employees/{employeeId}/contracts), this parameter is redundant but harmless since the path parameter already constrains to the same employee.

startDateFrom.description:
Lower bound for filtering contracts by their effective start date.

Contracts with a start date on or after this value are included in results. Use together with startDateTo to define a date range window for browsing contracts that became effective within a specific time period. Both bounds are inclusive.
startDateFrom.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound filter on erp_hrm_contracts.start_date. Combined with startDateTo to form a range query: WHERE start_date >= startDateFrom.

startDateTo.description:
Upper bound for filtering contracts by their effective start date.

Contracts with a start date on or before this value are included in results. Use together with startDateFrom to define a date range window for browsing contracts that became effective within a specific time period. Both bounds are inclusive.
startDateTo.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive upper bound filter on erp_hrm_contracts.start_date. Combined with startDateFrom to form a range query: WHERE start_date <= startDateTo.

endDateFrom.description:
Lower bound for filtering contracts by their expiration date.

Contracts with an end date on or after this value are included. Contracts without an end date (ongoing contracts) are excluded from any end date range filter since null values cannot be compared. Use together with endDateTo to find contracts expiring within a specific window.
endDateFrom.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound filter on erp_hrm_contracts.end_date. Combined with endDateTo to form a range query: WHERE end_date >= endDateFrom. Note that end_date is nullable — contracts without an end date (ongoing) will not match any end_date range filter.

endDateTo.description:
Upper bound for filtering contracts by their expiration date.

Contracts with an end date on or before this value are included. Contracts without an end date (ongoing contracts) are excluded from any end date range filter since null values cannot be compared. Use together with endDateFrom to find contracts expiring within a specific window.
endDateTo.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive upper bound filter on erp_hrm_contracts.end_date. Combined with endDateFrom to form a range query: WHERE end_date <= endDateTo. Note that end_date is nullable — contracts without an end date (ongoing) will not match any end_date range filter.

payPeriod.description:
Filter contracts by one or more pay period types.

Accepted values are hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly. The pay period defines the time unit against which the pay rate is measured — for example, an hourly period means the employee earns the pay rate per hour worked. Multiple values may be specified to include contracts of different pay period types in a single query. At least one value must be provided.
payPeriod.x-autobe-specification: IN filter on erp_hrm_contracts.pay_period. Accepts one or more of the four pay period values: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly. At query time, translates to: WHERE pay_period IN (values). Must contain at least one element.

status.description:
Filter contracts by their current status as active or past.

An active contract is the one currently in effect — determined dynamically as the contract with the most recent start date whose end date is either absent (ongoing) or not yet passed. Past contracts are superseded by a newer contract or have an end date that has already passed. Past contracts are preserved as immutable historical records for auditing and reference.
status.x-autobe-specification:
Dynamic filter computed at query time — no direct column mapping. Determines whether to return active or past contracts:
- 'active': Returns only the currently active contract per employee. A contract is active when (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= NOW()) AND it has the most recent start_date among all non-ended contracts for its employee. At most one active contract per employee.
- 'past': Returns superseded or expired contracts — those where end_date < NOW() or a newer contract with a more recent start_date exists for the same employee.

When absent, all non-deleted contracts are returned regardless of status.

search.description:
Free-text search across contract notes.

Performs a partial, case-insensitive match against the optional notes field of each contract. Notes may contain free-form information such as bonus structures, overtime policies, or special terms. Contracts without notes are never matched by this filter.
search.x-autobe-specification: LIKE pattern match on erp_hrm_contracts.notes. Translates to: WHERE notes LIKE '%searchTerm%' (case-insensitive where database collation supports it). The notes column is nullable — contracts without notes are never matched by any search term.

sort.description:
Column to sort results by.

Controls which field determines the ordering of returned contracts. Available sort columns are startDate (contract effective date), endDate (contract expiration date), payRate (compensation amount), and workingHoursPerWeek (weekly hours commitment). Combine with the order parameter to specify ascending or descending direction.
sort.x-autobe-specification:
ORDER BY column selector. Maps to database columns:
- startDate → erp_hrm_contracts.start_date (contract effective date)
- endDate → erp_hrm_contracts.end_date (contract expiration date)
- payRate → erp_hrm_contracts.pay_rate (compensation amount per pay period)
- workingHoursPerWeek → erp_hrm_contracts.working_hours_per_week (expected weekly time commitment)

When specified without order, defaults to DESC (descending). When absent entirely, defaults to sorting by start_date DESC (most recent contracts first).

order.description:
Sort direction for the result ordering.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order. Only meaningful when combined with the sort parameter. When sort is provided without an explicit order, results are sorted in descending order by default.
order.x-autobe-specification: ASC/DESC direction for ORDER BY. Applied to the column selected by the sort parameter. When sort is specified but order is absent, defaults to DESC (descending). When sort is absent, order is ignored and the default ordering (start_date DESC) applies.

page.description:
Page number for offset-based pagination, starting from 1.

Together with limit, controls which slice of the total result set is returned. Page 1 returns the first batch of records, page 2 returns the next, and so on. The total number of pages is calculated from the total record count divided by the page size and is returned in the pagination metadata of the response.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for offset-based pagination. Translates to SQL offset: OFFSET = (page - 1) × limit. Defaults to 1 when absent. Values below 1 are invalid and should be clamped or rejected.

limit.description:
Maximum number of contract records to return per page.

Controls the page size for paginated results. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. The actual number of records returned may be less than this value on the final page when fewer records remain. Together with page, enables efficient traversal of large contract sets.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records per page for offset-based pagination. Translates to SQL LIMIT. Defaults to 20 when absent. Bounded between 1 and 100 inclusive — values outside this range should be clamped to the nearest valid boundary.

IErpHrmContract.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for filtering and paginating employment contract records.

Supports filtering by employee, contract date ranges (start and end dates), pay period type (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly), and contract status (active vs. past). Active contracts are determined dynamically at query time as the most recent contract whose end date has not passed. Free-text search across contract notes and configurable sorting by date or compensation fields are also supported.

Pagination uses offset-based traversal with configurable page number and limit per page. Sorting defaults to most recent contracts first by start date in descending order. All queries are organization-scoped through the employee relationship and exclude soft-deleted records.
IErpHrmContract.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query filters for listing employment contracts with pagination. Source table: erp_hrm_contracts, organization-scoped via JOIN on erp_hrm_employees (erp_hrm_employee.erp_hrm_organization_id matching current session). Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) in all queries.

Filter mappings:
- employeeId → erp_hrm_contracts.erp_hrm_employee_id equality (org-wide listing; redundant but harmless when employeeId is already in path parameter)
- startDateFrom/startDateTo → erp_hrm_contracts.start_date range (inclusive both ends)
- endDateFrom/endDateTo → erp_hrm_contracts.end_date range (inclusive both ends, nullable column — null end_dates do not match range filters)
- payPeriod → erp_hrm_contracts.pay_period IN filter (multi-value: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly)
- status → dynamic at query time: 'active' = most recent start_date ≤ now AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date ≥ now); 'past' = superseded or expired
- search → LIKE pattern match on erp_hrm_contracts.notes (nullable — contracts without notes are never matched)
- sort → ORDER BY column mapping: startDate→start_date, endDate→end_date, payRate→pay_rate, workingHoursPerWeek→working_hours_per_week
- order → ASC/DESC direction; defaults to DESC when sort is specified but order is absent
- page/limit → offset-based: offset = (page - 1) × limit; default page=1, limit=20

IErpHrmTimer.ICreate.description:
Request body for starting a live time tracking session.

Initiates a real-time timer that begins counting from the moment of creation. The timer tracks work against a specified project, with an optional task for granular tracking and a free-text description of the current work activity.

Only one active timer is allowed per employee — attempting to start a second timer while one is running results in a 409 Conflict error.
IErpHrmTimer.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps: erp_hrm_project_id (required, scalar reference to a project the employee is a project member of), erp_hrm_task_id (optional, must belong to erp_hrm_project_id when provided), description (optional free-text note). Excluded: id (auto UUID v4), erp_hrm_employee_id (JWT session context), start_timestamp (server-set to DateTime.now()), created_at/updated_at (auto).

employee_ids.description:
Filter timers by one or more employee IDs.

Accepts a single UUID or an array of UUIDs identifying employees in the current organization. When provided, only timers owned by the specified employees are returned. Leave empty or omit to include all employees.
employee_ids.x-autobe-specification: WHERE erp_hrm_employee_id IN (...). Accepts single UUID or list of UUIDs. Filters timers to only those owned by the specified employee(s). Cross-organization: only employees within the current organization are valid.

project_ids.description:
Filter timers by one or more project IDs.

Accepts a single UUID or an array of UUIDs identifying projects in the current organization. When provided, only timers associated with the specified projects are returned. Leave empty or omit to include all projects.
project_ids.x-autobe-specification: WHERE erp_hrm_project_id IN (...). Accepts single UUID or list of UUIDs. Filters timers to only those tracking against the specified project(s).

task_ids.description:
Filter timers by one or more task IDs.

Accepts a single UUID or an array of UUIDs identifying tasks. When provided, only timers assigned to the specified tasks are returned. Use the has_task filter instead when you only need to distinguish between timers with or without any task assignment.
task_ids.x-autobe-specification: WHERE erp_hrm_task_id IN (...). Accepts single UUID or list of UUIDs. Filters timers to only those assigned to the specified task(s). Use has_task instead when you only care about whether any task is assigned.

has_task.description:
Filter timers by whether they have a task assigned.

When set to true, only timers with a specific task assignment are returned — the employee is tracking time against a particular task. When set to false, only timers without any task assignment are returned — the employee is tracking time at the project level. Leave unset to include both.
has_task.x-autobe-specification: Transforms to: true → WHERE erp_hrm_task_id IS NOT NULL (timer has a task assigned); false → WHERE erp_hrm_task_id IS NULL (timer has no task). When not provided, no task-assignment filtering is applied.

start_from.description:
Filter timers started on or after this date and time.

An ISO 8601 datetime string representing the inclusive lower bound of the start timestamp range. Use together with start_to to define a time window. Timers started exactly at this timestamp are included.
start_from.x-autobe-specification: WHERE start_timestamp >= start_from. Used with start_to to form a BETWEEN range. ISO 8601 datetime string. Inclusive lower bound.

start_to.description:
Filter timers started on or before this date and time.

An ISO 8601 datetime string representing the inclusive upper bound of the start timestamp range. Use together with start_from to define a time window. Timers started exactly at this timestamp are included.
start_to.x-autobe-specification: WHERE start_timestamp <= start_to. Used with start_from to form a BETWEEN range. ISO 8601 datetime string. Inclusive upper bound.

search.description:
Free-text search against the timer's description.

Performs a case-insensitive partial match against the description field of each timer. Useful for finding timers by keywords in the work description. Results are returned in chronological order (most recent first), not by search relevance.
search.x-autobe-specification: WHERE description ILIKE '%search%'. Case-insensitive partial match against the timer's description text. Results are ordered by start_timestamp DESC regardless of search relevance.

cursor.description:
Opaque cursor for keyset-based pagination.

Encodes the position of the last timer from the previous page of results. When provided, the response returns timers starting after this position in the result set. When null or omitted, results begin from the most recent timer. This is the primary pagination mechanism for traversing large result sets efficiently.
cursor.x-autobe-specification: Decoded cursor for keyset pagination on start_timestamp DESC. The cursor encodes the last item's position (start_timestamp + id) from the previous page. When provided, returns the next page of results after the cursor position. When null or omitted, returns results from the beginning. This is the primary pagination mechanism — page-based navigation is a convenience alternative.

limit.description:
Maximum number of timer records to return per page.

Controls the page size for paginated results. Must be between 1 and 100. If omitted, a default of 20 records per page is used. The actual returned count may be less than the limit on the final page.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Page size for pagination. Defaults to 20 when not provided. Maximum allowed value is 100. Applied as LIMIT in the SQL query. Controls how many timer records are returned per page.

page.description:
Target page number to retrieve (1-indexed).

Specifies which page of results to return. Page numbering starts from 1. If omitted, null, or undefined, defaults to page 1 (first page). Requesting a page beyond the available range returns an empty data array with valid pagination metadata reflecting the actual totals.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for page-based pagination. Defaults to 1 if null or omitted. Convenience alternative to cursor-based navigation. Internally translates to an offset: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Requesting a page beyond available data returns an empty data array with valid pagination metadata.

IErpHrmTimer.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying active timers within the current organization.

Supports filtering by specific employees, projects, or tasks, as well as by whether any task is assigned. A date range filter constrains results by timer start time, and a free-text search field matches against the timer description.

Pagination is page-based with a configurable limit. Results are ordered with the most recently started timers appearing first. All results are scoped to the member's currently selected organization context.
IErpHrmTimer.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query filter DTO for the PATCH /erpHrm/member/timers index endpoint. All properties are optional — the request body may be empty to return all active timers in the organization.

Cross-organization enforcement: JOIN erp_hrm_timers INNER JOIN erp_hrm_employees ON erp_hrm_employee_id, filtered by erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_organization_id = current session organization. Never return timers from other organizations.

Filter mappings:
- employee_ids → WHERE erp_hrm_employee_id IN (...)
- project_ids → WHERE erp_hrm_project_id IN (...)
- task_ids → WHERE erp_hrm_task_id IN (...)
- has_task: true → WHERE erp_hrm_task_id IS NOT NULL; false → WHERE erp_hrm_task_id IS NULL
- start_from/start_to → WHERE start_timestamp BETWEEN start_from AND start_to
- search → WHERE description ILIKE '%search%'
- cursor → decoded cursor for keyset pagination on start_timestamp DESC
- limit → page size, default 20, max 100
- page → 1-indexed page number, defaults to 1

IErpHrmTimelog.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new timelog entry recording work performed by an employee on a specific date.

A timelog captures a duration in minutes against a required project and an optional task within that project. The employee who performed the work is typically derived from the authenticated session; users with the `time:manage` permission may optionally specify an `employee_id` to create timelogs on behalf of other employees.

The `billable` flag distinguishes billable from non-billable work for reporting purposes. When not explicitly provided, it defaults to `true`.
IErpHrmTimelog.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps to erp_hrm_timelogs table. Required: project_id (UUID, must reference an active project the employee is a member of), date (calendar date of work), duration_minutes (positive integer). Optional: task_id (UUID, must belong to the same project as project_id), description (free-text work notes), billable (boolean, defaults to true when omitted), employee_id (UUID, only usable with time:manage permission — when omitted, derived from authenticated session). Excluded: id (auto-generated UUID), timesheet_id (derived from path parameter in timesheet-scoped endpoint), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed timestamps).

employee_id.description:
UUID of the employee whose membership role is being updated.

The employee must already be an active member of the project — this operation does not create new project assignments. Together with the project ID from the URL path, this uniquely identifies the membership record to update.

The employee must belong to the same organization that owns the project. Use the project members list endpoint to look up valid employee-project pairings before calling this operation.
employee_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_project_members.erp_hrm_employee_id. Combined with the path parameter projectId to uniquely identify the membership record via the unique constraint on (erp_hrm_employee_id, erp_hrm_project_id). The employee must belong to the same organization as the project and must already be an active member (deleted_at IS NULL).

role.description:
New role to assign to the project member.

The role determines the member's authority level within the project. "member" grants regular participant access including time tracking and viewing assigned tasks. "project-lead" grants elevated authority including the ability to create, edit, assign, and manage tasks within the project.

Setting the same role as the current assignment is allowed — the operation succeeds and returns the unchanged membership record.
role.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_project_members.role. Validation enforces exact match against 'member' or 'project-lead'. When the requested role matches the current role, the update is idempotent — the record is returned unchanged with original timestamps preserved.

IErpHrmProjectMember.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing project member's assigned role.

The membership to update is identified by the combination of the project ID in the URL path and the employee ID provided in this body. Only the role can be changed — the original join date is preserved and never modified by this operation.

Valid roles are "member" (regular participant with time tracking and view access) and "project-lead" (elevated authority with task management permissions within the project). Setting the same role as the current assignment is allowed and returns the unchanged record.
IErpHrmProjectMember.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Update request for an existing project member's role. The membership target is identified by the projectId path parameter (maps to erp_hrm_project_id) and the employee_id body field (maps to erp_hrm_employee_id). Only the role column is mutable — joined_at is preserved from creation. Excluded: id (PK, not user-provided), erp_hrm_project_id (from path), joined_at (immutable — set at creation), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed), employee and project relations (Request DTO uses scalar FKs, not relation objects). Validation: role must be 'member' or 'project-lead'. Update is idempotent — setting the same role as current succeeds.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the project membership record.

A UUID v4 value generated automatically when the membership is created. This identifier is stable across the membership's entire lifecycle — it does not change when the member's role is updated or when the member is removed from the project.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.id. Primary key, auto-generated UUID.

role.description:
The member's role within the project, determining their level of authority.

Two values are supported: "member" for regular project participants who can track time and view assigned tasks, and "project-lead" for members with elevated authority who can create, edit, assign, and manage tasks within the project. The role can be changed at any time via the update endpoint without affecting the original join date.
role.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.role. Must be either "member" or "project-lead". Server-side validation enforces these two values.

employee.description:
The employee who is a member of this project.

Contains the employee's summary profile including their member identity, assigned organizational role, department, position, employment type, and current status. The employee must belong to the same organization as the project.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation: JOIN erp_hrm_project_members.erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees.id. Returns IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. Always present — every project membership links to exactly one employee.

project.description:
The project to which the employee is assigned.

Contains the project's essential identifying fields including name, color code, current status, and optional description. The project's status determines whether new members can be added — only active projects accept new assignments.
project.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation: JOIN erp_hrm_project_members.erp_hrm_project_id → erp_hrm_projects.id. Returns IErpHrmProject.ISummary. Always present — every project membership links to exactly one project.

joined_at.description:
Timestamp when the employee was assigned to the project.

Set automatically at creation time and never modified thereafter. Serves as a permanent historical record of when the membership relationship began, regardless of subsequent role changes or eventual removal from the project.
joined_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.joined_at. Immutable — set once at creation, never updated by any operation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this membership record was created.

Set automatically when the employee is first assigned to the project. Together with updated_at, provides an audit trail of the record's lifecycle.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.created_at. System-managed, auto-set on creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this membership record.

Updated automatically whenever the member's role is changed. Compare with created_at to determine how recently the membership was modified.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.updated_at. System-managed, auto-updated on every modification (e.g., role change).

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the employee was removed from the project, or null if the membership is active.

When set, the membership is considered soft-deleted — the employee no longer participates in the project, but the historical record is preserved for audit purposes. Null indicates an active membership.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.deleted_at. Nullable — null for active memberships, set to timestamp when member is removed from project. Filtered at query level: only active records (deleted_at IS NULL) are returned in list endpoints unless explicitly requested.

IErpHrmProjectMember.description:
A project membership record linking an employee to a project with an assigned role.

Each membership represents one employee's participation in a project within the organization. The membership carries a role — either "member" for regular project participants or "project-lead" for those with elevated task management authority within the project. The joined_at timestamp records when the assignment began and is immutable, serving as a permanent record of when the member joined the project.

All data is scoped to a single organization through the project's organization membership. When a member is removed from a project, the record is soft-deleted and the deleted_at timestamp is set.
IErpHrmProjectMember.x-autobe-specification:
Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members with joined relations.

Columns: id, role, joined_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.
Belongs-to relations: employee via JOIN on erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees (IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary), project via JOIN on erp_hrm_project_id → erp_hrm_projects (IErpHrmProject.ISummary).
FK columns erp_hrm_employee_id and erp_hrm_project_id are superseded by their respective relation objects and excluded from the DTO.
Organization scoping is implicit through the project's organization_id — all membership records are queried within the session's active organization context.

date_start.description:
Start of the date range filter.

Filters timelogs to include only entries whose work date is on or after this value. Combined with date_end to define an inclusive date range.

When omitted, no lower bound is applied — all timelogs from the earliest record are eligible. The value is transmitted as a datetime for transport compatibility but is treated as date-only; the time component is ignored during comparison.
date_start.x-autobe-specification: Filters erp_hrm_timelogs.date >= date_start. When both date_start and date_end are provided, applies SQL BETWEEN with inclusive bounds. Date-only comparison — strip time components before comparing. Transmitted as date-time for wire compatibility but semantically date-only.

date_end.description:
End of the date range filter.

Filters timelogs to include only entries whose work date is on or before this value. Combined with date_start to define an inclusive date range.

When omitted, no upper bound is applied — timelogs up to the present are eligible. The value is transmitted as a datetime for transport compatibility but is treated as date-only; the time component is ignored during comparison.
date_end.x-autobe-specification: Filters erp_hrm_timelogs.date <= date_end. When both date_start and date_end are provided, applies SQL BETWEEN with inclusive bounds. Date-only comparison — strip time components before comparing. Transmitted as date-time for wire compatibility but semantically date-only.

project_id.description:
Filter timelogs by the project they were logged against.

When specified, only timelogs belonging to the given project are returned. The project must exist within the currently selected organization.

Use this to review all time logged against a specific project across all employees.
project_id.x-autobe-specification: Filters erp_hrm_timelogs.project_id = project_id. Direct equality match on the project foreign key column. The project must exist and belong to the current organization context. Combined with task_id filter: when both are provided, the task must belong to the specified project.

task_id.description:
Filter timelogs by the task they were logged against.

When specified, only timelogs associated with the given task are returned. The task must belong to the project specified by the project_id filter when both are provided.

Use this to drill down into time logged against a specific work item within a project.
task_id.x-autobe-specification: Filters erp_hrm_timelogs.task_id = task_id. Direct equality match on the task foreign key column. The task must exist in the database. When both project_id and task_id filters are provided, the task must belong to the specified project — otherwise the filter combination returns zero results.

billable.description:
Filter timelogs by their billable classification.

When set to true, only billable timelogs are returned — these contribute to billable hour calculations in time and budget reports. When set to false, only non-billable entries are included.

When omitted entirely, both billable and non-billable timelogs appear in results. New timelogs default to billable, but this filter allows overriding that default selection during browsing.
billable.x-autobe-specification: Filters erp_hrm_timelogs.billable = billable. When true, returns only billable timelogs (those contributing to billable hour calculations). When false, returns only non-billable timelogs. When omitted, no billable filter is applied — both billable and non-billable entries appear in results.

employee_id.description:
Filter timelogs by the employee who performed the work.

Only honored when the requesting user holds the view-all-time permission. When the caller lacks this permission, this filter is silently ignored and results are automatically restricted to the caller's own timelogs.

Use this as a manager or owner to review a specific team member's time entries across the organization. Without the required permission, providing this filter has no effect.
employee_id.x-autobe-specification: Filters erp_hrm_timelogs.employee_id = employee_id. Permission-gated: only applied when the caller holds the view-all-time permission. Without this permission, the filter is silently ignored and results are automatically scoped to the requesting employee's own timelogs via employee_id match from the authenticated session context. This ensures employees can never use the filter to view another employee's timelogs.

search.description:
Full-text search against timelog descriptions.

Matches timelogs whose free-text description contains text similar to the search term. Uses trigram-based fuzzy matching via PostgreSQL's pg_trgm extension, making it tolerant of minor spelling variations and partial word matches.

The search is case-insensitive. Use this to find timelogs by keywords in their work descriptions — for example, searching for "meeting" returns all timelogs where the description mentions meetings, regardless of exact phrasing.
search.x-autobe-specification: Performs GIN trigram (pg_trgm extension) fuzzy text search on erp_hrm_timelogs.description. Uses PostgreSQL ILIKE with trigram similarity matching via the description column's GIN index (gin_trgm_ops). Case-insensitive. Tolerant of partial words and minor spelling variations. Applied as an AND condition alongside other active filters.

sort.description:
Sort order for the result set.

An array of sort criteria applied in sequence to determine the ordering of returned timelogs. Each entry follows the format field_direction.

Supported fields and their meanings:
- date: The calendar date the work was performed
- duration_minutes: The length of the work session in minutes
- created_at: The timestamp when the timelog entry was created

Supported directions:
- asc: Ascending order (oldest first, shortest first)
- desc: Descending order (newest first, longest first)

Examples: ["date_desc"] sorts newest work first; ["date_asc", "created_at_asc"] sorts oldest work first with ties broken by creation time. When omitted, results default to newest date first, then newest creation time first.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Sort criteria array applied as ORDER BY clauses in the generated SQL query. Each element uses the format {field}_{direction}. Allowed field values: date (erp_hrm_timelogs.date), duration_minutes (erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes), created_at (erp_hrm_timelogs.created_at). Allowed direction values: asc (ascending), desc (descending). Multiple entries are applied in the order they appear in the array. Default sort when omitted or empty: date DESC, created_at DESC. Each element is validated against the regex pattern ^(date|duration_minutes|created_at)_(asc|desc)$ before being incorporated into the query.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Specifies which page of results to return. Page numbering starts at 1 for the first page. Combined with limit to control which slice of the total result set is returned.

For example, with limit set to 20: page 1 returns records 1–20, page 2 returns records 21–40, and so on. When omitted, the first page is returned by default.
page.x-autobe-specification: Page number for offset-based pagination. Minimum value is 1 (first page). Used with limit to compute SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit. Defaults to 1 when omitted by the client or when an out-of-bounds value is provided. The total number of available pages is returned in the response's pagination metadata.

limit.description:
Maximum number of timelogs per page.

Controls how many records are returned in a single page of results. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.

Lower values reduce payload size and improve response times. Higher values reduce the number of API calls needed to browse through large result sets. Combined with page to navigate through paginated results.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records per page. Minimum 1, maximum 100. Used as the SQL LIMIT value. Combined with page to compute OFFSET for pagination. Defaults to a system-configured value (typically 20) when omitted by the client. Values outside the 1–100 range are clamped to the nearest valid boundary.

IErpHrmTimelog.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for browsing timelog entries.

Provides a comprehensive set of optional query parameters for the timelog index endpoint. All filters are combinable with AND logic — when multiple filters are provided, only timelogs satisfying every condition are returned.

Filtering is available across five dimensions: date range (date_start, date_end), project (project_id), task (task_id), billable classification (billable), and employee (employee_id, honored only for users with the view-all-time permission). A free-text search (search) matches against timelog descriptions using fuzzy trigram matching. Results are ordered by the sort criteria and paginated via page and limit.
IErpHrmTimelog.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Pure query filter and pagination DTO for the timelog index endpoint. All properties are optional and AND-combinable — when multiple filters are provided, only timelogs matching all criteria are returned. Soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are automatically excluded from all queries. Authorization scoping: without view-all-time permission, results are automatically restricted to the requesting employee's own timelogs via session-scoped employee_id; with view-all-time permission, all organization timelogs are returned and the optional employee_id filter is honored. Each property's specification documents the exact DB column mapping and query behavior.

currentPassword.description:
The member's current password for identity verification.

Must match the stored password hash exactly. If the provided password does not match, the operation is rejected with a 403 Forbidden response. The member is identified from the current authenticated session and does not need to provide their email address.
currentPassword.x-autobe-specification: Plain text password provided by the authenticated member for identity verification. Compare against erp_hrm_members.password_hash using the same hashing algorithm used for password storage. If the comparison fails, return 403 Forbidden with an error message indicating that the current password is incorrect. Must not be empty. The member identity is resolved from the current authenticated session — email is not required in this DTO.

newPassword.description:
The new password to set for the member account.

Must differ from the current password to enforce a meaningful update. Must satisfy password strength requirements including minimum length and complexity rules. Once accepted, the new password takes effect immediately and must be used for all subsequent login attempts. The current authenticated session is preserved — no re-authentication is required.
newPassword.x-autobe-specification: Plain text new password to replace the current one. Must differ from currentPassword — if identical, return 422 Unprocessable Entity indicating the new password must differ from the current password. Must pass standard password strength validation including minimum length and complexity requirements — if validation fails, return 422 Unprocessable Entity with specific validation error details. On success, hash using the same hashing algorithm used for password_hash storage and write to erp_hrm_members.password_hash. The change takes effect immediately for all subsequent login attempts. Do not invalidate the current authenticated session.

IErpHrmMember.IChangePassword.description:
Password change payload for the authenticated member.

The member provides their current password for identity verification and the new password to set. The change takes effect immediately for all subsequent login attempts. The member remains authenticated after the change — no re-authentication is required.

This operation targets the member's global authentication identity and is independent of organization context. All fields are transmitted as plain text and hashed server-side before storage.
IErpHrmMember.IChangePassword.x-autobe-specification: Maps to erp_hrm_members.password_hash through two distinct transformation paths. currentPassword is plain text compared against the stored password_hash using the same hashing algorithm for identity verification — return 403 Forbidden if the comparison fails. newPassword is plain text that must differ from currentPassword (422 Unprocessable Entity if identical) and must pass password strength validation including minimum length and complexity requirements — on success, hash and store in password_hash, replacing the existing value. The change takes effect immediately for all subsequent login attempts. Do not invalidate the current authenticated session — the member remains authenticated after the change. This operation targets the member's global authentication identity and is independent of organization context; skip organization context middleware for this endpoint.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the timer.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies this timer record across the system. Assigned automatically by the server when the timer is created and never modified thereafter. Use this identifier to retrieve, update, stop, or discard the timer.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.id. UUID v4 primary key, server-generated on creation. Immutable.

start_timestamp.description:
The exact date and time when the timer was started.

Set to the server's current time at the moment of timer creation. This timestamp serves as the reference point for calculating elapsed duration when the timer is eventually stopped. It remains fixed throughout the timer's lifespan — editing the project, task, or description does not affect this value.

Format: ISO 8601 datetime with timezone offset (e.g., "2026-05-01T04:19:41Z").
start_timestamp.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.start_timestamp. Set to DateTime.now() (server time) when the timer is created. Immutable — preserved unchanged even when project, task, or description are edited while the timer is running.

description.description:
Free-text note describing what the employee is currently working on.

Provides real-time context about the tracked activity. This field is mutable throughout the timer's lifespan — the employee can update it to reflect changes in their work without stopping and restarting the timer.

Nullable — may be empty when the employee has not provided a description.
