description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.description. Nullable free-text field. Mutable — the employee can update it at any point while the timer is running. May be set to null to clear.

employee.description:
The employee who owns this timer.

Identifies the employee whose work time is being tracked. Only this employee may view, update, stop, or discard the timer. The employee's organization context is verified to prevent cross-organization access.

Contains a summary of the employee's profile including their member identity, assigned role, optional department, position, employment type, and current status.
employee.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation via JOIN on erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees. Returns IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. Strictly the owner of this timer — only this employee may view or manage it. Organization context is verified through the employee's organization_id for cross-organization access prevention.

project.description:
The project against which time is being tracked.

Identifies the project the employee is currently working on. The employee must be an assigned project member of this project. This assignment is editable while the timer is running — if the employee shifts focus to a different project, they can update this reference without stopping and restarting the timer.

Contains the project's summary information: name, color code, status, and optional description.
project.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation via JOIN on erp_hrm_project_id → erp_hrm_projects. Returns IErpHrmProject.ISummary. The employee must be an active project member of this project. Mutable — the employee can switch to a different project while the timer is running, provided they are a member of the new project.

task.description:
The specific task within the project that the employee is working on.

Provides granular tracking at the task level when the employee is focused on a particular task within the selected project. When null, the employee is tracking time against the project in general without a specific task assignment.

This assignment is editable while the timer is running and may be set to null to clear it. The task must belong to the currently selected project.

Contains the task's summary information: title, status, priority, estimated hours, due date, assigned employee, and parent task context.
task.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation via JOIN on erp_hrm_task_id → erp_hrm_tasks. Returns IErpHrmTask.ISummary | null. The task must belong to the project referenced by erp_hrm_project_id. Nullable — the employee may track time against a project without specifying a particular task. Mutable — can be changed or cleared while the timer is running.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the timer was created.

Records the exact moment the timer record was inserted into the database. Automatically set by the server and never modified thereafter. Serves as an audit trail alongside the start_timestamp for distinguishing between timer creation time and tracking start time (which are typically identical but independently recorded).

Format: ISO 8601 datetime with timezone offset.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.created_at. Auto-set on insertion, never modified. Represents when the timer record was created in the database.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the timer.

Automatically updated whenever the timer's description, project assignment, or task assignment is changed. The start_timestamp remains fixed even when other fields are modified.

Format: ISO 8601 datetime with timezone offset.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timers.updated_at. Auto-updated on every modification to the timer record, including description, project, or task assignment changes. Set to current timestamp on each update.

IErpHrmTimer.description:
Represents a live time tracking session for an employee.

Each timer records when tracking started, which project (and optionally which task within that project) work is being performed against, and a free-text description of the current activity. An employee may have at most one active timer at any given time — enforced by a unique constraint on the employee reference.

When the timer is stopped, the elapsed duration is calculated from the start timestamp and a timelog record is created. When discarded, the timer is deleted without producing any time entry.

Access to timer records is strictly owner-exclusive. No other user within the organization — including managers, owners, or users with elevated permissions — can view another employee's running timer.
IErpHrmTimer.x-autobe-specification: Read DTO for the erp_hrm_timers table. Direct column mappings: id (UUID primary key), start_timestamp (ISO 8601, server-set on creation, immutable thereafter), description (nullable free-text, mutable), created_at (auto-set on creation), updated_at (auto-updated on every modification). FK columns erp_hrm_employee_id, erp_hrm_project_id, erp_hrm_task_id are excluded — resolved as ISummary objects via BELONGS-TO relations: employee (JOIN erp_hrm_employees → IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary), project (JOIN erp_hrm_projects → IErpHrmProject.ISummary), task (JOIN erp_hrm_tasks → IErpHrmTask.ISummary, nullable). Access is strictly owner-exclusive — only the employee who owns the timer may view it, verified by comparing the authenticated employee's ID against erp_hrm_employee_id within the current organization context. Cross-organization access enforced via the employee's organization_id.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the contract.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies this contract record across the system. Used as the primary key for direct contract lookups and as a foreign key reference in related entities.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.id. UUID primary key.

employee.description:
The employee to whom this contract belongs.

Provides a summary view of the employee including their member profile (display name, email, avatar), assigned role, optional department membership, position title, employment type classification, and current active or deactivated status. Each employee may have multiple contracts over time forming a complete compensation history.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Join from erp_hrm_contracts.erp_hrm_employee_id to erp_hrm_employees.id. Returns IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary with member profile, role, department, position, employment type, and status.

start_date.description:
The date when this contract's compensation terms take effect.

Serves as the anchor point for determining which contract is currently active — the active contract is the one with the most recent start_date on or before the current date whose end_date has not yet passed. Past contracts retain their original start_date as an immutable historical record.
start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.start_date. ISO 8601 datetime with timezone.

end_date.description:
The date when this contract's compensation terms expire.

When null, the contract is ongoing with no predetermined termination date and remains in effect until superseded by a newer contract or the employee leaves the organization. When set, the contract is effective from start_date through end_date inclusive. Past contracts retain their original end_date as an immutable historical record.
end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.end_date. Nullable DateTime — null means ongoing with no predetermined termination date.

pay_rate.description:
The numeric amount the employee earns per unit of time.

Interpreted in conjunction with pay_period: for example, 25.50 with an hourly pay_period means the employee earns 25.50 currency units per hour worked. The actual currency is determined by the organization's configured currency setting.
pay_rate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.pay_rate. Float (DoublePrecision) — the numeric amount earned per unit of time defined by pay_period.

pay_period.description:
The unit of time against which the pay_rate is measured.

Supported values:
- hourly: pay_rate applies per hour worked
- daily: pay_rate applies per full workday
- weekly: pay_rate applies per full workweek
- monthly: pay_rate applies per calendar month
pay_period.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.pay_period. String — one of: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly.

working_hours_per_week.description:
The employee's expected weekly time commitment under this contract.

For example, 40 for a standard full-time arrangement, or 37.5 for a slightly reduced schedule. This value informs budget calculations and capacity planning across the organization, and is used in project budget reports to compare planned hours against actual logged hours.
working_hours_per_week.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.working_hours_per_week. Float (DoublePrecision) — expected weekly time commitment.

is_active.description:
Whether this contract is currently in effect.

Determined dynamically at query time based on two conditions: the contract must not have expired (end_date is null or still in the future), and it must be the most recent non-expired contract for its employee. Only one contract per employee can be active at any given moment. Past contracts that have been superseded by a newer contract or whose end_date has passed will have this flag set to false.
is_active.x-autobe-specification: Computed at query time. Logic: true when (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) AND this contract has the most recent start_date among all contracts for the same employee where (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP). In other words, the contract is not expired AND no newer active contract exists for the same employee.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this contract record was created in the system.

Set automatically at creation time and never modified thereafter. Provides an audit trail for when the contract was first entered into the system, which may differ from the contract's effective start_date.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.created_at. ISO 8601 datetime with timezone. Set automatically on creation.

IErpHrmContract.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an employment contract for list views.

Displays the core compensation terms — pay rate, pay period, and weekly working hours — along with the contract's effective date range. Each contract is linked to its employee through a summary reference, and the is_active flag indicates whether this contract is currently in effect, determined dynamically at query time based on recency and date validity.

Contracts form a historical chain per employee: only one contract is active at any given time, while past contracts remain visible as immutable records for auditing and reference purposes.
IErpHrmContract.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, start_date, end_date (nullable DateTime?), pay_rate (Float), pay_period (String), working_hours_per_week (Float), created_at (DateTime). Relation: employee resolved as IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary via erp_hrm_employee_id FK join. Computed: is_active (boolean) — determined at query time: true when end_date IS NULL or end_date >= now, AND this contract has the most recent start_date among all non-ended contracts for its employee. Excluded: notes (large text field per ISummary rules), updated_at (not in summary spec), deleted_at (soft-deleted records excluded at query level), erp_hrm_employee_id (replaced by $ref).

IErpHrmProject.description:
Full project entity with all descriptive fields, related members, tasks, and aggregated time tracking metrics.

Represents a complete project record within the current organization. Includes the project's identity (id, organization_id), display properties (name, description, color_code), lifecycle status, budget tracking (budget_hours), and timeline dates (start_date, end_date).

Related entities are included as nested arrays: {@link IErpHrmProjectMember projectMembers} lists all employees assigned to this project with their roles, and {@link IErpHrmTask.ISummary tasks} provides lightweight summaries of work units within the project.

Aggregated metrics provide quick insights: timelogs_count reflects total time entries logged against this project, and timers_count shows the number of live tracking sessions associated with this project.
IErpHrmProject.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, organization_id, name, description, color_code, status, budget_hours, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at. Relations: projectMembers (HAS-MANY composition via erp_hrm_project_members, full entity), tasks (HAS-MANY composition via erp_hrm_tasks, ISummary array). Aggregations: timelogs_count (COUNT of erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE project_id = this.id), timers_count (COUNT of erp_hrm_timers WHERE project_id = this.id). Excluded: deleted_at (filtered at query level — soft-deleted rows return 404).

id.description:
Unique identifier for the activity log entry.

A UUID v4 value assigned at creation time. Immutable — activity log entries are never updated or deleted once created, forming an append-only audit trail.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated on creation.

action_type.description:
Category label classifying the nature of the action performed.

Recognized types include: employee_invited, employee_deactivated, employee_reactivated, contract_created, contract_edited, project_created, project_archived, project_completed, project_deleted, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected, role_assigned, and role_changed.

This field enables filtering and grouping of activity log entries by action category for audit review and operational oversight.
action_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.action_type. Categorizes the logged action for filtering and grouping.

target_entity.description:
The type of business object affected by the action.

Examples include: employee, contract, project, task, timesheet, role. Together with target_id, this forms a polymorphic reference that identifies the specific entity instance that was created, modified, or transitioned.

This is not a foreign key — it identifies the target table conceptually rather than enforcing a database-level constraint, since it can point to multiple different entity types.
target_entity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.target_entity. Identifies the type of business object affected (e.g., employee, contract, project, task, timesheet, role).

target_id.description:
The unique identifier of the specific business object affected by the action.

Combined with target_entity, this identifies the exact entity instance — for example, the specific project that was archived or the particular timesheet that was approved.

This is a polymorphic reference — the actual target table is determined by the target_entity value. It does not enforce a foreign key constraint since it can point to multiple different entity types.
target_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.target_id. UUID value identifying the specific entity instance affected.

details.description:
Optional contextual information stored as a JSON string, supplementing the action record.

Contains action-type-specific data that varies by the nature of the logged action. Examples include: old and new status values for task status changes, rejection reasons for timesheet rejections, contract terms for contract edits, or role names for role assignment changes.

This field is null when no additional context is available for the action. When present, clients should parse the string as JSON for structured access to the contextual data.
details.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.details. Nullable — returned as raw string for client-side JSON parsing. Null when no additional context was recorded for the action.

user.description:
The authenticated member who performed the action.

Every activity log entry is traceable to a specific user, establishing individual accountability for all recorded events. The user is represented as a summary object containing the member's global profile (display name, email, avatar, phone) alongside their organization-specific employment details.

All logged actions must have a known actor — this field is never null.
user.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via user_id to erp_hrm_members (BELONGS-TO relation). Resolved as IErpHrmMember.ISummary — the member's identity and organization-specific employment details at the time of the action.

created_at.description:
The exact date and time when the action was completed and this log entry was recorded.

Stored with timezone information for accurate chronological ordering across different time zones. This is the sole temporal field on activity log entries — activity logs are immutable append-only records that are never updated or deleted after creation.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.created_at. ISO 8601 date-time with timezone (Timestamptz).

IErpHrmActivityLog.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an activity log entry for list display.

Activity logs are immutable, append-only audit trail entries recording significant actions across the organization. Each entry captures who performed what action on which entity at what time, providing a complete chronological record of operational changes for accountability and transparency.

The action_type classifies the nature of the action — recognized types include employee_invited, employee_deactivated, employee_reactivated, contract_created, contract_edited, project_created, project_archived, project_completed, project_deleted, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected, role_assigned, and role_changed. The target_entity and target_id fields together identify the specific business object affected through a polymorphic reference pattern.

The user field identifies the authenticated member who performed the action, ensuring individual accountability for every recorded event. The details field may contain action-type-specific contextual information as a JSON string, such as old and new values for status changes or rejection reasons for timesheet rejections.
IErpHrmActivityLog.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs: id, action_type, target_entity, target_id, created_at. Relations: user via JOIN on user_id to erp_hrm_members (BELONGS-TO, resolved as IErpHrmMember.ISummary). Nullable: details (contextual JSON string, returned as-is for client-side parsing). Excluded: organization_id (session-scoped multi-tenancy filter — resolved from current session context), user_id (FK column redundant when user relation object is present).

token.description:
The cryptographic token string sent to the member's email address in the password reset link.

Extracted from the query parameter of the password reset URL delivered via email. This token proves the caller has access to the registered email address associated with the account. The token must match the one stored in the corresponding password reset record exactly.

Tokens are cryptographically secure, globally unique, and time-limited. Presenting a valid token is required before the system will accept a new password.
token.x-autobe-specification: Compared against erp_hrm_member_password_resets.token for the reset record identified by path parameter resetId. Must be an exact, case-sensitive match. The token is cryptographically secure and globally unique across all active reset records. If the reset record does not exist or has expired (expired_at < now), the request is rejected before token comparison occurs. On success, the matching reset record is used to identify the target member via erp_hrm_member_id.

password.description:
The new password to set for the member's account.

Submitted as plain text and immediately hashed on the server side — the plaintext value is never stored, logged, or transmitted beyond the initial request.

Must meet all password policy requirements: at least 8 characters in length, must not be identical to the current password, and must not be a commonly compromised password. The system will reject the request with a validation error if any requirement is not met.
password.x-autobe-specification: Plaintext password submitted by the user. Validated server-side: minimum 8 characters, must not match the member's current password, must not appear in lists of commonly compromised passwords. On successful validation, the password is hashed and stored in erp_hrm_members.password_hash of the member referenced by erp_hrm_member_password_resets.erp_hrm_member_id (resolved via token verification against erp_hrm_member_password_resets.token). The plaintext value is never persisted, logged, or transmitted beyond this initial request.

IErpHrmMemberPasswordReset.ICompletion.description:
Request body for completing a password reset.

Contains the cryptographic token extracted from the password reset email link and the new password the member wishes to set. The token proves the caller has access to the registered email address. The new password replaces the existing password hash upon successful verification.

Password must meet minimum length requirements (at least 8 characters), must not be the same as the current password, and must not be a commonly compromised password.
IErpHrmMemberPasswordReset.ICompletion.x-autobe-specification:
Cross-entity request body spanning erp_hrm_member_password_resets and erp_hrm_members.

token: Compared against erp_hrm_member_password_resets.token for the reset record identified by path parameter resetId. Must be an exact, case-sensitive match. The token is cryptographically secure and globally unique. If the reset record does not exist or has expired (expired_at < now), the request is rejected before token comparison occurs.

password: Validated server-side (minimum 8 characters, must not match current password, must not be a commonly compromised password). On successful validation, the plaintext password is hashed and stored in erp_hrm_members.password_hash of the member referenced by erp_hrm_member_password_resets.erp_hrm_member_id. The reset record is then hard-deleted to prevent token reuse. The plaintext value is never persisted or logged.

No organization context or role check is applied — this endpoint is accessible to both unauthenticated guests and authenticated members.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the timesheet.

A UUID v4 string that serves as the primary key. Automatically assigned at creation time and never modified.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.id. Primary key, UUID v4. Auto-generated on creation, immutable.

employee.description:
The employee who owns this timesheet.

Contains the employee's summary profile — member identity, role, department, position, employment type, and status — identifying the person whose timelogs are grouped into this timesheet. Always present since every timesheet must belong to an employee.
employee.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation: JOIN erp_hrm_employees ON erp_hrm_timesheets.employee_id = erp_hrm_employees.id, then INNER JOIN erp_hrm_members for profile fields. Returns IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary including the member's display name, email, position, employment type, status, and assigned role. Organization scoping is implicit — the employee belongs to the same organization as the timesheet.

week_start_date.description:
The Monday date marking the start of the timesheet's calendar week.

Always falls on a Monday and defines the beginning of the seven-day period (Monday through Sunday) that this timesheet covers. Together with the owning employee, this date uniquely identifies the timesheet — an employee cannot have two timesheets for the same calendar week.
week_start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_start_date. MUST be a Monday (ISO day-of-week = 1). Combined with employee_id to form the unique constraint @@unique([employee_id, week_start_date]) ensuring one timesheet per employee per week. Used alongside week_end_date to determine which timelogs are eligible for inclusion (timelogs with date between week_start_date and week_end_date inclusive).

week_end_date.description:
The Sunday date marking the end of the timesheet's calendar week.

Always exactly six days after the week start date, defining the Sunday boundary of the seven-day period. Used alongside week_start_date for date-range queries and to determine timelog eligibility.
week_end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_end_date. Always exactly 6 days after week_start_date (Sunday). Stored redundantly alongside week_start_date for query convenience — enables efficient date-range filtering without computing the Sunday on every query. Computed automatically on creation and update: week_end_date = week_start_date + 6 days.

status.description:
The current workflow status of the timesheet.

Controls what actions are available on the timesheet and its timelogs. One of four values: `draft` — the initial state where timelogs can be freely added or removed; `submitted` — awaiting manager review, timelogs are locked against addition or removal; `approved` — terminal state where all contained timelogs are permanently locked against any modification; `rejected` — returned to draft for the employee to revise based on the rejection reason before resubmitting.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.status. Enum values: 'draft' (editable, timelogs can be added/removed), 'submitted' (awaiting review, timelogs locked from add/remove), 'approved' (terminal state, all timelogs permanently locked), 'rejected' (returned to draft for revision with mandatory rejection_reason). State transitions: draft→submitted (submit), submitted→approved (approve), submitted→rejected (reject), rejected→submitted (resubmit after revision). Approved is terminal — no further transitions allowed.

submitted_at.description:
Timestamp of when the employee most recently submitted this timesheet for review.

Set automatically when the timesheet transitions from draft to submitted status. Remains populated even after rejection — it always reflects the most recent submission. Null when the timesheet has never been submitted and is still in its initial draft state.
submitted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.submitted_at. Nullable DateTime. Set to NOW() when the timesheet transitions from 'draft' to 'submitted' status. Remains set even if the timesheet is later rejected — it records the most recent submission. Null for timesheets that have never been submitted.

reviewed_at.description:
Timestamp of when a reviewer approved or rejected this timesheet.

Captures the exact moment the review decision was made, regardless of whether the outcome was approval or rejection. Set together with the reviewer's identity. Null when the timesheet has not yet been reviewed — it remains null throughout draft and submitted statuses.
reviewed_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.reviewed_at. Nullable DateTime. Set to NOW() simultaneously with reviewed_by_user_id when the timesheet transitions to 'approved' or 'rejected' status. Null for timesheets still in 'draft' or 'submitted' status. Records the moment of review regardless of outcome.

reviewedByUser.description:
The user who reviewed this timesheet.

Identifies the manager or owner who performed the approval or rejection. Contains the reviewer's member profile summary — display name and email — for audit and accountability. Null when the timesheet has not yet been reviewed; populated for both approved and rejected timesheets.
reviewedByUser.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation: LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_members ON erp_hrm_timesheets.reviewed_by_user_id = erp_hrm_members.id. Returns IErpHrmMember.ISummary with the reviewer's display name, email, and organization-specific employee details. Null when status is 'draft' or 'submitted' (no review has occurred). Populated for both 'approved' and 'rejected' statuses. The reviewer is always a member with the time:approve permission, never the timesheet's owning employee.

rejection_reason.description:
The explanation provided by the reviewer when rejecting this timesheet.

Contains the reason the timesheet was not approved, giving the employee clear guidance on what needs to be corrected before resubmission. Always present and non-empty when the timesheet is in rejected status; null for draft, submitted, and approved timesheets.
rejection_reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.rejection_reason. Nullable String. Mandatory and non-empty when status is 'rejected' — the reject operation requires a non-blank reason. Null for all other statuses (draft, submitted, approved). Provides the employee with actionable context for why the timesheet was not approved and what corrections are needed before resubmission.

timelogs.description:
The collection of timelog entries grouped into this timesheet.

Contains all time entries that fall within the timesheet's calendar week and have been associated with it. Each entry includes the work date, duration in minutes, billable classification, and references to the project and optional task. When the timesheet is in draft status, timelogs can be added or removed; once submitted, the collection is locked against changes; once approved, all contained timelogs become permanently immutable.
timelogs.x-autobe-specification: HAS-MANY composition resolved via query: SELECT FROM erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id = :this.id AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns IErpHrmTimelog.ISummary[] — each entry includes id, date, duration_minutes, billable flag, and $ref relations to employee, project, task, and timesheet. Soft-deleted timelogs excluded from this array. When the timesheet is approved, all timelogs in this array become permanently locked against edit or delete regardless of caller permissions. The array may be empty for draft timesheets with no associated timelogs.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when the timesheet was initially created.

Automatically recorded at the moment of creation and never modified thereafter. Useful for audit trails and chronological ordering of timesheets.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.created_at. Auto-set on INSERT, never modified. Records the moment the timesheet record was first persisted. Used for chronological sorting and audit trails.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the timesheet.

Updated automatically whenever any field on the timesheet changes — including status transitions, week range adjustments, timelog additions or removals, and review actions. Serves as the last-modified indicator for synchronization and caching purposes.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.updated_at. Auto-updated on every modification: week range changes, timelog additions/removals, status transitions (submit, approve, reject), and review metadata updates. Tracks the most recent change to any field on the record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp marking when this timesheet was removed.

When set, the timesheet is considered deleted and is excluded from all normal queries and list results, returning a 404 Not Found if accessed directly. The record is preserved for audit and potential recovery. Null for active timesheets.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.deleted_at. Nullable DateTime. When set, the timesheet is considered soft-deleted — excluded from normal queries (filtered at query level with WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). The record is preserved for audit integrity. Deleted timesheets return 404 Not Found when accessed directly. Null for active timesheets. Deletion is only permitted on timesheets not in 'submitted' or 'approved' status.

IErpHrmTimesheet.description:
A weekly timesheet that groups an employee's timelogs for a Monday-to-Sunday calendar week into a single submission and approval unit.

**Workflow**: Timesheets progress through four statuses. They begin in `draft` status, where the employee can freely add or remove timelogs. When ready, the employee submits the timesheet, transitioning it to `submitted` status and making it available for manager review. A reviewer with the `time:approve` permission may then either approve the timesheet — locking all contained timelogs permanently — or reject it with a mandatory reason, returning it to `draft` for revision.

**Week Boundaries**: The `week_start_date` always falls on a Monday, and `week_end_date` is exactly six days later on Sunday. All timelogs within the timesheet fall within this inclusive date range. An employee may have at most one timesheet per calendar week.

**Review Metadata**: The `submitted_at` timestamp records when the employee submitted the timesheet. When reviewed, `reviewed_at` captures the review timestamp and `reviewedByUser` identifies the reviewer. The `rejection_reason` field is populated only when the timesheet is rejected and provides the employee with actionable feedback for corrections.

The member provides their registered email address to request a password reset token. The system generates a time-limited, cryptographically secure token and sends it to the email address if a matching active member account exists.

weeks.description:
Weekly summary entries, one per ISO week within the report date range.

Each entry covers a Monday-to-Sunday week and includes total hours, billable versus non-billable breakdown, timelog count, and per-project and per-employee breakdowns. Weeks are ordered chronologically by start date.

When no timelogs match the query criteria, this array is empty rather than absent.

Computed array of weekly summary entries, each representing one ISO week (Monday-Sunday) within the report date range.

Computation:
1. Query erp_hrm_timelogs joined with erp_hrm_employees and erp_hrm_projects, filtered by organization scope, date range [startDate, endDate], and optional projectId.
2. GROUP BY ISO week. For each week, compute aggregate statistics: totalHours, billableHours, nonBillableHours, totalTimelogs, projectBreakdown (per-project), employeeBreakdown (per-employee).
3. Each week entry maps to IErpHrmWeeklySummaryReport.IWeek with weekStartDate, weekEndDate, and all aggregated metrics.
4. Sort by weekStartDate ascending.
5. All hour values rounded to 2 decimal places.

If no timelogs match the criteria, return an empty array (not null, not 404).

IErpHrmWeeklySummaryReport.description:
Weekly summary report aggregating time tracking data for an organization.

Groups timelogs by ISO week (Monday through Sunday) within the specified date range, providing total hours, billable versus non-billable hour breakdowns, and per-project and per-employee summaries for each week. Only members with the `report:view` permission can access this report.

All data is scoped to the member's currently selected organization. Individual timelog descriptions and notes are never exposed — only aggregated statistics at the week, project, and employee level are returned. Deactivated employees' historical data is included in aggregates.
IErpHrmWeeklySummaryReport.x-autobe-specification:
Computed report aggregating timelog data across the organization, scoped to the member's currently selected organization context.

Source tables: erp_hrm_timelogs (duration_minutes, billable, date), erp_hrm_employees (id, name via erp_hrm_members), erp_hrm_projects (id, name).

Authorization: Requires `report:view` permission. Returns 403 Forbidden if the member lacks this permission.

Query Parameters:
- startDate (required): ISO 8601 date string defining the start of the report period. Filter timelogs where date >= startDate.
- endDate (required): ISO 8601 date string defining the end of the report period. Filter timelogs where date <= endDate.
- projectId (optional): UUID string. When provided, filter timelogs to only those belonging to the specified project within the organization. When omitted, include all projects.

Aggregation Logic:
1. Query erp_hrm_timelogs joined with erp_hrm_employees (on employee_id) and erp_hrm_projects (on project_id).
2. Filter: employee's erp_hrm_organization_id matches the member's selected organization, deleted_at IS NULL on all joined tables, timelog date within [startDate, endDate].
3. When projectId is provided, additionally filter project_id = projectId.
4. Group timelogs by ISO week (Monday-Sunday). For each week compute:
   - weekStartDate: Monday of that week
   - weekEndDate: Sunday of that week
   - totalHours: SUM(duration_minutes) / 60 across all matching timelogs
   - billableHours: SUM(duration_minutes) / 60 where billable = true
   - nonBillableHours: totalHours - billableHours
   - totalTimelogs: COUNT of timelog records
   - projectBreakdown: array of per-project summaries (projectId, projectName, totalHours, billableHours, timelogCount)
   - employeeBreakdown: array of per-employee summaries (employeeId, employeeName, totalHours, billableHours, timelogCount)
5. Round all hour values to 2 decimal places.
6. Sort weeks chronologically by weekStartDate ascending.

Privacy: No individual timelog descriptions or notes exposed. Employee breakdown shows only aggregated hours — individual timelog details are never included. Deactivated employees' historical data is included in aggregates.

Edge cases: Empty result set returns { weeks: [] } (not 404). If startDate is after endDate, return 400 Bad Request. Date range may span multiple weeks; each week is computed independently.

Ungrouped timelogs (those without a timesheet association) remain freely editable by their owner or by users with the time:manage permission.

The employee field identifies who performed the work, the project field indicates which project the work belongs to, and the optional task field provides granular tracking within that project. IErpHrmActivityLog.description:
An immutable audit trail entry recording a significant business action within an organization.

Each activity log entry captures who performed what action on which entity at what time, forming the organization's permanent chronological record of operational changes. The log is append-only — entries are never modified or deleted once created.

**Actor**: The `user` property identifies the member who performed the action, establishing individual accountability for every recorded event. Every entry has a known actor — this field is never null.

**Action Classification**: The `action_type` field categorizes the nature of the action. Recognized types include `employee_invited`, `employee_deactivated`, `employee_reactivated`, `contract_created`, `contract_edited`, `project_created`, `project_archived`, `project_completed`, `project_deleted`, `task_status_changed`, `timesheet_submitted`, `timesheet_approved`, `timesheet_rejected`, `role_assigned`, and `role_changed`.

**Target Identification**: The `target_entity` and `target_id` fields together form a polymorphic reference identifying the specific business object affected by the action. `target_entity` specifies the entity type (e.g., `employee`, `contract`, `project`, `task`, `timesheet`, `role`), while `target_id` holds the UUID of the affected instance. This is not a foreign key — it can reference multiple different entity types.

**Contextual Details**: The `details` field stores action-type-specific contextual information as a JSON string. Examples include old and new status values for task status changes (`{"old_status": "in_progress", "new_status": "completed"}`), rejection reasons for timesheet rejections (`{"reason": "Hours exceed project allocation"}`), or changed fields for contract edits (`{"changed_fields": ["pay_rate", "pay_period"]}`). This field is `null` when no additional context is available.

**Access Control**: Activity log entries are scoped to the currently selected organization context via `organization_id`. Access is restricted to users holding the organization management permission — cross-organization access is not permitted, and a 403 Forbidden is returned for unauthorized actors.

**Immutability**: Entries are append-only and immutable. They are never modified or deleted through any user-facing operation. Removal only occurs via cascading deletion when the owning organization is permanently deleted.

The user relation is resolved via BELONGS-TO JOIN on user_id → erp_hrm_members.id, returning IErpHrmMember.ISummary (consolidated view of global profile + org-specific employment details). The raw user_id FK column is intentionally excluded — surfaced through the user object. No insert/update/delete DTOs exist — activity logs are append-only, created server-side during business operations, and never modified through any user-facing endpoint.
